precepts.label: Psalms 17:15
precepts.why:
Men, we want dominion. We want rulership; we want to subdue the nations. God said, “Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion,” and he told them, “Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it.” Being made after his image, we were supposed to subdue the earth and bring everything under foot.

When you read “after our likeness,” understand it is more than what you look like. At that time everybody was of color, yet God gave a specific people rulership. David shows what the likeness is: “As for me, I will behold thy face in righteousness: I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with thy likeness.”

His likeness is not just appearance; it is being righteous. Christ is black, God is black, and we are made after his image, but the image alone does not bring the dominion. In being righteous we will subdue and have dominion over things.

So the government must be in place, and in that we must be keeping the commandments. It is the only way we are going to get it. That government cannot happen unless we are righteous.

thread.label: Genesis 3:15
thread.text: And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.

precepts.label: Genesis 4:6-7
precepts.why:
In the garden, before Adam and Eve were put out, God said, “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”. Enmity is hatred. Satan has seed on this earth, and the woman’s seed, the descendants who would come through her, is Israel. When that was spoken, Cain was not yet born. The seed of Satan was Cain.

Genesis 4 shows how. “And the Lord said unto Cain, Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen? If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted?” If you obey me, will you not be accepted by me? But “and if thou doest not well”, if you choose to break my commandments, “sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.” The one spoken of there is Satan: Satan would be Cain’s desire, and would rule over him. Satan would be Cain’s god and Cain’s father.

Cain chose not to obey, and he killed Abel. From that moment the enmity of Genesis 3:15 was at work in the earth: the seed of the serpent against the seed of the woman.

It did not end with Cain. His line died in the flood, but all spirits return. Cain came back as Esau, the one who “came out red, all over like an hairy garment”, and Abel, or Seth, came back as Jacob, whose hand took hold on Esau’s heel. So Genesis 3:15 and Genesis 4:7 explain the hatred Edom has for Israel to this day: it is the enmity God put between the two seeds in the beginning.

precepts.label: Genesis 5:3
precepts.why:
“And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth”. Don’t you see something wrong there? Abel was already dead, and Cain was still alive. So why does it never say that Cain was in Adam’s image?

Go back to the making of Adam: “And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle”. Adam, the black man, was made in the image of God. Adam and Eve had Cain and Abel; Cain killed Abel, because God had told him that if he did not do well, sin lay at the door and Satan would rule over him.

Then, when it names the son born “in his own likeness, after his image”, it names Seth, not Cain. People say everybody is in the image of God. No: Cain was not in the image of God, and he is never said to be in Adam’s image.

So whose image was Cain in? John answers it: Cain “was of that wicked one”. Seth was of Adam; Cain was of Satan. That is why the seed of the woman and the seed of the serpent are two different seeds, and why Seth’s line, the line that returns as Jacob, is the one that carries Adam’s image.

precepts.label: 1 John 3:10-12
precepts.why:
“In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil”. There are children of God on the planet, and there are children of the devil on the planet. And “whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God, neither he that loveth not his brother. For this is the message that ye heard from the beginning, that we should love one another”.

“Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother.” Wait: we thought Cain was of Adam. It says no. Seth was of Adam; Cain was of that wicked one, of Satan. That is exactly what God told Cain in Genesis 4: unto thee shall be his desire, and he shall rule over thee. “And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.”

This is the enmity of Genesis 3:15 made plain: “between thy seed and her seed”. Satan’s seed is Cain, the children of the devil, and her seed is Israel, the children of God.

Cain’s line died in the flood, but all spirits return. Cain came back as Esau, and Abel, or Seth, came back as Jacob. Esau “came out red, all over like an hairy garment”, and Idumea, the Greek and Roman name for Edom, is that same Esau. So when we ask who the children of the devil are in the earth today and why they hate us, John has already told us: not as Cain, who was of that wicked one.

precepts.label: 2 Thessalonians 2:9
precepts.why:
Paul speaks of the man of sin: “Even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders”. His coming is after the working of Satan, meaning Satan is his father, as he was Cain’s. That is Esau, Cain come again.

Genesis 3:15 ends, “it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.” Christ is our head, smitten so that the sheep were scattered. But the heel is Edom’s Achilles heel. Jacob took hold of Esau’s heel at birth, and in Daniel 2 “a stone was cut out without hands, which smote the image upon his feet that were of iron and clay, and brake them to pieces.”

The image is the empires. The head of gold is Nebuchadnezzar and Babylon; the silver is Persia and Media; the brass is Greece, “which shall bear rule over all the earth.” That was Alexander, “son of Philip, the Macedonian”, who “slew the kings of the earth” until “the earth was quiet before him; whereupon he was exalted and his heart was lifted up”: the beginning of white supremacy in the earth. His kingdom was parted among his generals, “and evils were multiplied in the earth.” Their own books, The Chronology of Ancient Nations and The Rise of Christendom, trace Philip back to Esau. The iron is Rome, and we are still in it: America and NATO, a kingdom “partly strong, and partly broken”, strong in military, with the toes as the European nations. The miry clay is the melting pot: “they shall mingle themselves with the seed of men: but they shall not cleave one to another”.

The stone is Christ, “Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone”. He strikes the image on its feet, its heel, and “the stone that smote the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth.” And “in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed: and the kingdom shall not be left to other people”. We are living in the days of these kings. What we teach is the beginning of that kingdom, and it cannot be stopped; it will consume all these kingdoms with the word of God.

thread.label: Genesis 4:1-24
thread.text: And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the Lord.

precepts.label: Genesis 3:21
precepts.why:
“Unto Adam also and to his wife did the Lord God make coats of skins, and clothed them.” That don't mean they were butt naked and needed clothes. It means God gave them a way to get forgiveness of their sin. Animal sacrifice was introduced right here, in Genesis 3:21: God clothed them with righteousness and forgiveness.

That is the key to Genesis 4. Cain “brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord.” Abel “brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof.” “And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering”, because Abel's offering was in accordance with Genesis 3:21. Cain did not roll that way. He decided he was not going to do what God said and brought fruits and vegetables instead.

“But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell.” His countenance falling means he got mad. He got pissed off. God asked him, “Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen?” and told him, “If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door.” Doing well was obeying what God had set in place; sin lying at the door was disobedience.

So the difference between Cain and Abel was not the gift; it was obedience. Abel followed the way God had already shown his parents, and Cain replaced it with his own way. That disobedience is where Cain's line started.

precepts.label: Genesis 3:16
precepts.why:
God said to Cain, “And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.” This is a parable. God is speaking about the spiritual demon, Satan: the “thee” is Satan, and it is Cain's desire that would be unto him.

To see the pattern, go back to Genesis 3:16. “Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.” If a woman desires anything, whether it is sex, wisdom, knowledge or money, it must be to her husband, and he rules over her.

Read Genesis 4:7 with that in mind. Just as a woman's desire is to her husband, Cain's desire would be to Satan. Anything Cain wanted, he would have to go to Satan for it, and Satan would rule over him.

So Satan was over Cain and over his seed. When we read about Cain's children, the city, the cattle, the music, the weapons and Lamech's vengeance, we should not read them as holy and righteous. This is Cain's seed, and their desire is always unto Satan.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 39:25-27
precepts.why:
After Abel was slain, “Cain knew his wife; and she conceived, and bare Enoch: and he builded a city”. If Cain was the only child left, why would he need to build a city? There were already thousands upon thousands of people on the earth. He named the city after his son Enoch, and down the line came Lamech, who took two wives, the first time multiple wives appear in scripture.

Adah bore Jabal, “the father of such as dwell in tents, and of such as have cattle.” What could be wrong with tents and cattle? Ecclesiasticus answers: “For the good are good things created from the beginning: so evil things for sinners.” From the beginning means from the time of Cain and Abel. “The principal things for the whole use of man’s life are water, fire, iron, and salt, flour of wheat, honey, milk, and the blood of the grape, and oil, and clothing.” “All these things are for good to the godly: so to the sinners they are turned into evil.”

Bring it up to today. What do they do with food? GMOs, and things put inside the chicken and the cows to make them larger, and that causes sickness. They monopolize water and bottle it. With fire they create bombs, even nuclear fire. With iron they make bullets and guns to kill people. The milk today is not the same milk we drank as children. The clothing is made of mixed fabrics. Everything good, the sinful man turns to evil.

That is Cain's city. Jabal dealt in cattle with pricing and unrighteousness. His brother Jubal was “the father of all such as handle the harp and organ”, and it was not holy music: it was music about shake your ass, show me what you going with. Damn. It was songs about murder, drugs, debauchery and adultery, the same wicked songs many love today. Zillah bore Tubal-cain, “an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron”: that man was making all kinds of weapons. Good things created from the beginning, turned into evil by the seed whose desire was to Satan.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 27:2
precepts.why:
“As a nail sticketh fast between the joinings of the stones; so doth sin stick close between buying and selling.” When you are dealing in business with a sinner, the balances will be offset, because he always takes the favor, exceedingly. He will not take a five percent interest; he wants a hundred or two hundred percent.

That opens up Jabal, “the father of such as dwell in tents, and of such as have cattle.” It sounds harmless, but this is the seed of Cain in Cain's city. Jabal was dealing in tents and cattle with pricing and unrighteousness, buying and selling with sin stuck fast in between.

What Cain's seed did in the city of Enoch is what sinners do in business today. There is no new thing under the sun.

precepts.label: 1 John 3:10-12
precepts.why:
In case anyone doubts that Satan ruled over Cain, John explains it: “In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil: whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God, neither he that loveth not his brother.” There are children of God on the earth, and there are children of the devil.

John was correcting the Israelites he wrote to: “For this is the message that ye heard from the beginning, that we should love one another.” “Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother.” He was telling them, do not be like Cain. And who is that wicked one? The devil of verse 10. Cain was under Satan; Satan was his father.

“And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.” That is Genesis 4: Abel did well and was accepted, Cain did not do well, his desire went to Satan, and “Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.”

It shows in Cain's seed. Lamech said, “I have slain a man to my wounding, and a young man to my hurt.” “If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold.” They did not just kill the one man who hurt Lamech; they wiped out that whole lineage: the sons, the daughters, the aunts, the grandparents. That is how Esau gets down too. Remember who their desire was to: Satan. Everybody comes from Adam, but not everybody is a child of God.

thread.text: And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth:

precepts.label: Genesis 1:26
precepts.why:
“And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth”. Why is it written like that? Seth was in Adam's likeness, after Adam's image. It never says that about Cain. John said Cain “was of that wicked one”: Cain was in the image of Satan, not in the image of Adam.

Go back to the beginning: “And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth”. That was the point. God's image was given to man, and that image carried down to Seth, but everybody is not in God's image.

Everybody came from Adam, yes, but Satan's kids came from Adam too; that was Cain's lineage. Coming from Adam does not make someone a child of God. The image and likeness went through Seth, and that is the line to follow through Genesis.

precepts.label: Genesis 2:7
precepts.why:
“And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.” That was Adam. God made Adam in his own image and breathed the breath of life into him.

Read Genesis 5:3 again with that in mind: Adam “begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth”. Seth was in the image of Adam, and Adam was in the image of God. So Seth carried God's image.

Cain was not in the image of God. He was not in Adam's image, and he was not in God's image; he was of that wicked one. That is why everybody is not a child of God, and why Cain's line and Seth's line have to be read differently. All of this was playing out in the city Cain built, named Enoch after his son.

thread.label: Genesis 6:1-14
thread.text: And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them,

precepts.label: 1 John 3:1
precepts.why:
All of this was happening in the city called Enoch, named after Cain's son. Genesis says “the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.” In Christianity they say the sons of God are angels coming down. John shows who the sons of God are: “Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God”.

The sons of God is not talking about angels. It is talking about men, our people. Before we were called Israelites, we were called the sons of God.

Genesis 6 proves it: “And the Lord said, My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh”. God is angry with man, the sons of God, who are flesh, not angels. It is hard to see how Christian scholars can read that and say angels.

So when the sons of God took them wives of all which they chose, it is talking about interracial marriage: we started marrying the women of other nations. It still happens, a brother bringing in a white woman and claiming she is of the tribe of Gad, when everybody knows she is an Edomite.

precepts.label: Romans 8:19
precepts.why:
“For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.” Everybody is waiting for our manifestation, for us to be called the sons of God. That is the same name Genesis 6 gives, which settles who the sons of God were: men of our people, not angels.

With that understanding, Genesis 6 reads plainly. It says that “when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown.” That spark from God that we had produced renowned and powerful men on the earth, and they were battling the giants.

But we were not righteous; we had already started breaking God's laws inside that city. “And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.” Think of the great cities today, like New York City: murder, wicked music, buying and selling, stealing. It is the same thing going on now that was going on then, down to a married man looking over at other nations' women.

“The earth also was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with violence.” God told Noah, “the earth is filled with violence through them”, and that “them” goes back to Cain's seed. What we read in Genesis 4 about Cain's children affected all people on the earth. So God said, “Make thee an ark of gopher wood”. The sons of God were meant to be manifest, but by mixing with Cain's world they were corrupted with it.

thread.label: Genesis 9:1-16
thread.text: And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth.

precepts.label: Genesis 1:29-30
precepts.why:
After the flood, “God blessed Noah and his sons, and said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth.” Why replenish? Because God killed everybody on the planet. People say God is all love; then they have never read the Bible. He is all love when you obey, but he is also a great and terrible God.

Then: “Every moving thing that liveth shall be meat for you; even as the green herb have I given you all things.” This is the first time meat was introduced into our diet. Genesis 1 shows the diet before: “Behold, I have given you every herb bearing seed, which is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree, in the which is the fruit of a tree yielding seed; to you it shall be for meat.” Our diet was herbs and seeds.

And not only ours: “to every beast of the earth, and to every fowl of the air, and to every thing that creepeth upon the earth, wherein there is life, I have given every green herb for meat: and it was so.” Even the lions, the tigers and the bears ate herbs and vegetables. Nobody ate meat until Genesis 9:3. So when someone asks how the animals on the ark did not eat each other, the answer is that their diet was herbs and vegetables. When God introduced meat to us after the flood, the carnivores came with it.

Even then God set a limit: “But flesh with the life thereof, which is the blood thereof, shall ye not eat.” Do not eat anything with blood in it. And he gave a sign: “I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth.” The rainbow was first created there, as a promise that the waters would no more become a flood to destroy all flesh, and it has nothing to do with LGBT.

thread.label: Genesis 25:21-31
thread.text: And Isaac intreated the Lord for his wife, because she was barren: and the Lord was intreated of him, and Rebekah his wife conceived.

precepts.label: Genesis 2:7
precepts.why:
When Rebekah’s twins were born, “the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau.” It was important for that to be written down, because everybody was of the same complexion before. Genesis 2:7 shows why: “the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground.” Man was made from the earth, and the deeper you dig, the darker the earth gets.

Even the ground people call red earth is not red. In Oklahoma City the clay-looking dirt is a bright, vivid brown; put your hand next to it and you see it. The old Indian red crayon was brown too, because the natives were not red. That is another way to show that the natives were black, and the book Black Indians shows it.

Then the verse goes on: he “breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.” The breath of life is the Lord’s statutes and commandments, the same laws the Christian pastor tells you that you do not have to keep. When you are not keeping the Lord’s statutes and commandments, you are dead.

Back in Genesis 25, notice that when Jacob came out, “his hand took hold on Esau’s heel,” and nothing is said about his color. It did not need to be said: everybody was brown, different shades of brown, as the dust they were made from. Esau came out red and hairy, and that was different enough that it had to be documented. He is the one whose name was changed to Edom, which means red, and from him came a different manner of people.

precepts.label: Proverbs 7:2
precepts.why:
Proverbs 7:2 finishes what Genesis 2:7 opened. God “breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul,” and that breath of life is his statutes and commandments. Solomon says it plainly: “Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.”

If you want to have life, you must keep God’s laws; there are no two ways about it. The man who is not keeping the Lord’s statutes and commandments is dead, no matter what the Christian pastor tells him about not having to keep them.

This matters for the story of Jacob and Esau. The two came from the same belly, but “two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels.” One people keeps the law of their God and lives; the other lives another way, like Esau who cried “Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage.” We are not supposed to be eating blood; our food has to be cooked. But you know how they did the Negroes: they wanted to be just like their masters, so they started eating all the garbage Esau eats. The way back to life is to keep his commandments and hold his law as the apple of our eye.

thread.label: Genesis 27:37-40
thread.text: And Isaac answered and said unto Esau, Behold, I have made him thy lord, and all his brethren have I given to him for servants; and with corn and wine have I sustained him: and what shall I do now unto thee, my son?

precepts.label: 2 Kings 8:20
precepts.why:
Isaac told Esau, “Behold, I have made him thy lord, and all his brethren have I given to him for servants.” Jacob was made Esau’s lord; the elder would serve the younger. Everybody on this planet was meant to be our servants. It is our birthright; we are the rulers of this earth. But the only way to get it back is to remember where we fell off and what we did wrong, and Christianity will not teach us that. It keeps us in the wrong, and keeps us divided into Adventist, Protestant, Pentecostal, Mormon and Jehovah’s Witness, with none of them telling us who we are.

Esau “lifted up his voice, and wept,” and he still got a blessing: “thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above.” The best portions of the earth, and the dew that falls on the whole earth. But the whole earth was already given to Jacob. How the hell is Esau going to get the best part of the earth? The next words answer it: “by thy sword shalt thou live.” He would take it by the sword. He is a killer, yet wherever he goes he says he comes in peace, that he only wants to liberate the people and bring them freedom, while it is missiles after missiles, rape after rape, nothing but atrocities once he is let in. That's what democracy is about: now you could be a homo, nobody can judge you; now you could be a transgender, nobody can judge you. The book of Maccabees shows evil multiplying on the earth when they took control.

The blessing ends, “and shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck.” 2 Kings 8:20 shows that yoke breaking: “In his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah, and made a king over themselves.” Edom had served Judah, and in the days of the kings he threw it off.

From there it went back and forth. There was dominion again in 193 AD under Septimius Severus, wicked as hell as it was, and it was lost again around the Renaissance. So Isaac’s words have come to pass: Esau has possession of the earth, and he killed to get it.

precepts.label: Proverbs 30:7-9
precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain; for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.” To see what that means, go to Proverbs.

“Two things have I required of thee; deny me them not before I die: Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me: Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the Lord? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.”

Lest I be full and deny thee: that is one way of taking his name in vain. Lest I be poor and steal: that is sin, and sinning while bearing his name is taking the name of my God in vain. We are called by his name; he says we are a holy people, and he put his spirit in us.

So when they say you cannot keep the commandments, why can’t we? That does not mean we have never sinned. All men have sinned, and if anybody says they have not sinned, they lie. But when they say you cannot keep the commandments, it is because they want to remain in their sins.

This sits inside the first four commandments, which go into loving the Lord thy God. All of this blending of religions is meant to take you away from serving him and to keep you in sin.

precepts.label: Psalms 2:8-10
precepts.why:
Leviticus 25:46 says of the heathen bondmen, “ye shall take them as an inheritance for your children after you”. Hold that, and hear Psalm 2: “Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession.”

The Lord is saying, don’t worry, it is going back to that. He is going to give us the heathen for our inheritance. Meaning what? We are going to own them. That is what it is saying right there. We were their possession, but they were originally our possession; we sinned against our God and became theirs, and it is going to go back to the way it is supposed to be.

“Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron; thou shalt dash them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.” If they don’t want to get right, boom, upside the head. “Be wise now therefore, O ye kings: be instructed, ye judges of the earth.”

So the inheritance of Leviticus 25:46 and the inheritance of Psalm 2:8 are the same: the heathen given to Israel for an inheritance and a possession, ruled with a rod of iron.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 3:14
precepts.why:
Leviticus 25:46 says “they shall be your bondmen for ever”. For how long? Forever. Esau thinks he can change his judgment. No. No. You cannot change it. God said it, it is in writing, it is stamped. So that means you are going back into slavery.

“I know that, whatsoever God doeth, it shall be for ever: nothing can be put to it, nor any thing taken from it: and God doeth it, that men should fear before him.” Whatever God does is forever. Nothing can be put to it to change it, nor anything taken from it. There it is: that men should fear before him.

Isaiah shows it coming to pass: “the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids: and they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.” For servants and handmaids, because that is the role the Lord gave them, and for how long? Forever. The judgment of Leviticus 25:44-46 cannot be undone.

precepts.label: Luke 1:68-74
precepts.why:
Leviticus 26 says that even “when they be in the land of their enemies”, like today here in America, “I will not cast them away, neither will I abhor them, to destroy them utterly”. Then: “But I will for their sakes remember the covenant of their ancestors”. Who said bloodline ain’t important? The Bible says he will remember the covenant of your ancestors. Luke 1 is saying the same thing in the New Testament.

“Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people, And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David”. The horn of salvation is Christ. He is the king, out of the house of David. “As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began: That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us”. That is what Leviticus 26 is saying: in the land of their enemies he will not cast them away.

“To perform the mercy promised to our fathers”, our ancestors, “and to remember his holy covenant; The oath which he sware to our father Abraham”. That is the covenant of the ancestors in Leviticus 26:45, remembered for their sakes and brought to pass through Christ.

And what is it for? “that we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies might serve him without fear”. The God who brought our fathers out of Egypt in the sight of the heathen has not broken his covenant with us. He will deliver us out of the hand of our enemies so that we serve him without fear.

precepts.label: Acts 5:35-37
precepts.why:
Korah, Dathan, Abiram and On “took men”, “two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly, famous in the congregation, men of renown”. They were not nobodies; they had a name, and what they had was influence over the congregation. They used it against Moses and Aaron: “Ye take too much upon you”. And the results of those leaders: the earth “swallowed them up, and their houses, and all the men that appertained unto Korah, and all their goods”, and fire from the Lord “consumed the two hundred and fifty men that offered incense.” Everyone who followed them went down with them.

These things were written aforetime for our learning, and Acts 5 shows the same lesson. The apostles were brought before the council, and Gamaliel stood up and warned them: “Ye men of Israel, take heed to yourselves what ye intend to do as touching these men.” Then he gave examples.

“For before these days rose up Theudas, boasting himself to be somebody; to whom a number of men, about four hundred, joined themselves”. Four hundred men joined themselves to a man who came across as a leader, and he “was slain; and all, as many as obeyed him, were scattered, and brought to nought.” Then “rose up Judas of Galilee in the days of the taxing, and drew away much people after him: he also perished; and all, even as many as obeyed him, were dispersed.”

That is the pattern with false leaders: the leader perishes, and the ones that obeyed him perish and are scattered with him, just like the men that appertained unto Korah. “For the leaders of this people cause them to err; and they that are led of them are destroyed.” The leaders of the black community today, the Christian pastors, have our people living in hell, with drugs, gang violence, shootings on the block and adultery, and those that follow them are destroyed with them.

thread.label: Numbers 24:1-25
thread.text: And when Balaam saw that it pleased the Lord to bless Israel, he went not, as at other times, to seek for enchantments, but he set his face toward the wilderness.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 2:43-47
precepts.why:
Balaam, in his trance, saw that Israel’s “king shall be higher than Agag, and his kingdom shall be exalted.” Agag was an Edomite, a real tall one. The kingdom that is going to be exalted is the kingdom of the Lord, and the king higher than Agag is Christ.

Ezra saw that same king: “in the midst of them there was a young man of a high stature, taller than all the rest, and upon every one of their heads he set crowns, and was more exalted”. Ezra asked the angel who these were, and he answered, “These be they that have put off the mortal clothing, and put on the immortal, and have confessed the name of God: now are they crowned, and receive palms.” Then, “What young person is it that crowneth them, and giveth them palms in their hands?” And the answer: “It is the Son of God”.

So that is what Balaam saw in the spirit realm about the Israelites. His king shall be taller even than Agag. There will be no question in the kingdom which one is the Son of God. He is going to be the tallest one, and not by an inch or a foot; it is going to be astronomically clear. You will look and say, that is the Son of God right there.

And Balaam saw more of him: “he shall eat up the nations his enemies, and shall break their bones, and pierce them through with his arrows.” Balaam saw Christ destroying the nations. And “Blessed is he that blesseth thee, and cursed is he that curseth thee”: anybody that blesses Israel shall be blessed, and anybody that curses us shall be cursed.

precepts.label: Joshua 13:22
precepts.why:
Balaam dealt with enchantments, which lets us know he was a witch, a soothsayer, a diviner. When it says “the spirit of God came upon him”, notice the little s: this is on the left hand side. It is not the Holy Spirit coming on Balaam. He would fall into trances with his eyes wide open and see visions, and he knew it was the Lord sending that spirit upon him, which is why he told Balak he could not go beyond the commandment of the Lord. Even so, he saw Christ only from afar: “I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh”, because he is not an Israelite.

What happened to Balaam? “Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Israel slay with the sword among them that were slain by them.” What was he? The soothsayer: a witch, a warlock.

The Lord had used that witch, sending unrighteous angels to tell him this and tell him that. Then he told the Israelites: kill Balaam, destroy him; he is not our people. God got tired of him and had him put to death.

That is the end of the false prophet. Balaam could see all the way to the latter days and speak blessings over Israel, but his gift came from the left hand side, and he was slain among the enemies of Israel.

thread.label: Deuteronomy 7:3
thread.text: Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.

precepts.label: Joshua 23:12
precepts.why:
“Else if ye do in any wise go back, and cleave unto the remnant of these nations, even these that remain among you, and shall make marriages with them, and go in unto them, and they to you”. Even when we took the land, there was a remnant of the nations left in the midst of us, and Joshua warned us not to cleave to them.

The warning goes on: “Know for a certainty that the Lord your God will no more drive out any of these nations from before you”. Our forefather Joshua told us: marry these nations, and know for sure God will not get rid of them for you. We were warned to stay the hell away from these people, because their God is not our God. And we did exactly what we were warned not to do.

That is the reason behind Deuteronomy 7:3. “Neither shalt thou make marriages with them”, “For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods”. Look at it this week: Venus Williams married in Italy, and Italians are among the most racist people on the planet; do your history. Richard Williams put his life on the line for his black daughters to enter a space no one wanted them in; he protected them, provided for them, fought for them. The greatest thing a daughter can do for her father is bring home a man who honors him, and both of them spit in his face and married the same enemy their father fought against. This is the same man who was raping them, killing and whipping their fathers and mothers in front of them, abusing their children, and today they marry him voluntarily. And he would never have married her if the money were not there; remember what that white man did to Halle Berry. That is today's black woman society, and it is why God said do not make marriages with them.

precepts.label: Malachi 2:11
precepts.why:
“Judah hath dealt treacherously, and an abomination is committed in Israel and in Jerusalem; for Judah hath profaned the holiness of the Lord which he loved, and hath married the daughter of a strange god.” By marrying the other nations, Judah profaned the holiness of the Lord. And it is not only Judah; the whole twelve tribes did it.

This is spiritual. Those married to that nation all look bugged the hell out, because they have a different spirit in them, the beast spirit. Look at Serena Williams today, all bleached; she looks crazy because of that beast. You are not supposed to mingle the warrior seed with this beast, or mix the royal seed with pig seed.

So Deuteronomy 7:3 is not about skin alone: “For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods”. Marrying the daughter of a strange god is marrying the other god and taking on another spirit. It is called lust, and in the end the lust fades away.

thread.label: Deuteronomy 23:7
thread.text: Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite; for he is thy brother: thou shalt not abhor an Egyptian; because thou wast a stranger in his land.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:48
precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite; for he is thy brother”. Use this verse to your advantage; don't run from it. In Romans 9:13 Paul speaks on behalf of God, and that is what God says about Esau. But God's law to us is: thou shalt not abhor an Edomite, for he is thy brother, a wicked brother.

And look at our condition: “Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things”. If you know you have to serve this man for food, water and clothing, you can't go around saying I hate your guts, I just want to harm you. You think you're going to have a job? You're going to lose everything.

There was a brother at camp on Eastern Parkway, on medication, who said he couldn't work because he gets violent: I hate white people; when I sit in the office or do construction, I look at them and I just want to harm them. And there was a martial artist, a black belt, who drew young Haitian brothers to him, skinny at first and diesel two or three months later, calling themselves the barbershop crew in Brooklyn. One night a brother called to be gotten out of jail: they were getting diesel and learning to fight to do home invasions and burglaries.

The bottom line is, professing yourself to be an Israelite is not on the premise of wanting to harm white people. A lot of Israelite camps teach that, and the leaders of those camps are bums: either they are bums or they live off the congregation, and they can talk that way without repercussions because they have no boss to answer to. We serve our enemies under the curse, so we keep the law: we do not abhor the Edomite.

precepts.label: Ephesians 4:26
precepts.why:
In an interview with Soft White Underbelly came the question: when you're teaching this, doesn't it cause people to be angry? Yes, they get angry. The Bible says anger is okay: “Be ye angry, and sin not: let not the sun go down upon your wrath”.

The sin would be if you start murdering people; the sin would be if you start stealing. Remember the series American Gods: Anansi was on a slave ship and asked, are you angry? That's good; anger gets stuff done. Surely oppression makes a wise man mad. Not I'm going to go kill everybody, but let's organize, let's do better. And you know who got that actor fired? Black people, who said what he was saying would make white people mad. The whole show was cancelled, and all those black people lost their jobs.

So “Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite; for he is thy brother” does not mean you can't be angry at what was done. Be angry and sin not: let the anger drive you to organize and build, not to harm, steal or kill.

precepts.label: Romans 12:18
precepts.why:
“If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.” That's if possible. As much as lies in you, you live peaceably, and that includes the Edomite the law says you shall not abhor, for he is thy brother.

But we've seen some instances on the news where it was impossible; you had to throw hands with some people, because some people are irate and some people are unreasonable. Paul did not say peace at any cost; he said as much as lieth in you.

So the law of Deuteronomy 23:7 is not a command to be harmless. It is a command not to carry hatred and seek harm. We live peaceably as far as it depends on us, and we are not the ones who start it.

precepts.label: Matthew 5:22
precepts.why:
“But I say unto you, That whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment”. The key is without a cause. If I'm mad with you and I have no reason to be mad with you, I'm in danger of judgment.

But now somebody does something to your daughter, your wife, your loved one: do you have a reason? Yes. At one of the schools a sister's phone kept going ding, somebody sending her indecent pictures on Instagram. It went on for a while until the heads of the school had everybody bring their phones up and closed the doors. One brother said his phone was dead; they said don't worry, we got a charger. Sure enough, it was him. They told everybody to move back, and the husband said, move out my way. That is anger with a cause.

As the saying goes, in order to be a man of peace you must be capable of great violence; if you're not capable of violence, you're just harmless. So “Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite; for he is thy brother” forbids hatred without a cause, not the defense of your own.

thread.label: Deuteronomy 28:47-48
thread.text: Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness, and with gladness of heart, for the abundance of all things;

precepts.label: Nehemiah 8:10
precepts.why:
“Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness, and with gladness of heart, for the abundance of all things”. We had the whole earth, the whole thing belonged to us, and we were ungrateful children. We murmured and murmured and murmured. The Lord delivered us out of Egypt, we watched plagues upon plagues come upon Egypt, and then we turned back and worshipped the same gods the Lord destroyed in Egypt.

Even today it is like pulling teeth to get many of us to be happy and joyous on a feast day. We have to change that, because we did not have gladness before, and that is why we went into captivity. So now, coming back to serve the Lord, if you want your strength, you had better apply Nehemiah: “the joy of the Lord is your strength.” There are no two ways about it.

The blueprint is already set. The Bible tells you exactly what you need to do and how you need to go about living; we just do not want to listen. The curse of serving our enemies came because we would not serve the Lord with gladness, and the way back is to serve him with the joy that is our strength.

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 11:4
precepts.why:
“Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies”, “in want of all things”. We serve for food, for water, for clothes, for all kinds of paperwork, because nothing is real in your life until the so-called white man says it is real. You are not even dead until the white man says you are dead; without a paper stamped by Esau Edom you cannot even get the money your daddy left behind.

So even the understanding you have of the Bible was taught to you by Esau, and that is why you do not have the right spirit on you. When you read 2 Corinthians 11:4, once you serve “another Jesus”, you get “another gospel”, and once you get the other gospel, you get “another spirit”. That is the spirit in these churches; that is why those little boys are twitching in the church.

The enemy did not only put the yoke on our necks; he set up shop in our heads using Christianity, and you have to be dumb to believe Jesus is white with no Bible proof while you carry the biggest Bible under your arm. The only way for us to deal right is to come out of these churches and join this movement. No weapons, no guns, no physical fight will save us; the only thing that will save us is this book.

precepts.label: Romans 1:26
precepts.why:
Look at the Christian church: gangsters, homos and lesbians coming out of that church. It has mutated to a whole different level. Why? Because once you serve another God, according to the book of Romans, the Lord gives you up unto “vile affections”.

So if you keep staying in that Christianity, serving the false deity, or keep being a Muslim, serving a rock, do not be mad when the evil spirit jumps on you and you start defiling your body, changing kind and doing all kinds of nonsense. That is what is going to happen. Your choir master is making all those songs dedicated to another deity, and the Lord is unhappy with that. He says, you want to devote all your time to serving another god? I am going to remove myself from here, and watch what happens to you.

That is the curse of Deuteronomy 28:47-48 working in the spirit: because we did not serve the Lord with gladness, he sent our enemies against us, and when we took up their gods, he gave us up. Thank the Lord for saving a remnant, because we all would have been as Sodom and Gomorrah.

precepts.label: Habakkuk 3:14
precepts.why:
Officer Tatum was asked if black men like him were better off during slavery, and he answered, 100 percent. He said that after slavery there was an explosion of success, black Wall Street, men married to the women they had children with, and now look at the inner cities. What he does not understand is that he thinks white people just switched and started loving us after they let us out of slavery.

“Thou didst strike through with his staves the head of his villages: they came out as a whirlwind to scatter me”. When Christ returns, these same people who had us in slavery, and have us in slavery, are going to try to fight against Christ.

“their rejoicing was as to devour the poor secretly.” These same slave owners rejoice to devour the poor, and they do it secretly. Even though slavery supposedly ended with the emancipation proclamation in 1863, then what? You had the school to prison pipeline. Redlining. Sundown towns. Sharecropping. It is still the same thing.

Look at us now, and why? Because he is setting up all these traps. That is why he is still oppressing us to this day, and that is the “yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” But Tatum cannot see that.

precepts.label: Isaiah 14:32
precepts.why:
Habakkuk said their rejoicing is “to devour the poor secretly.” Who are the poor? “What shall one then answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.”

The poor of his people. We are the poor that they are devouring secretly. The poor are Israel, and it is Zion that the Lord founded for them to trust in.

Tatum blames the murders, the violent crime and the abortions in the inner cities on our people alone. But who legalized abortion? The white people. Who started Planned Parenthood with Margaret Sanger? He just skips past that; according to him they are not the cause. That is the secret devouring of the poor, and it is the yoke of iron of Deuteronomy 28:48 still on our neck.

precepts.label: Acts 24:16
precepts.why:
Tatum said black people need to do better: y’all whole life is activism, y’all still complaining and protesting like y’all still slaves. Why were the brothers in Ocean Springs, Mississippi? Because one of our brothers, Nolan Wells, had a mysterious death with a bunch of white people around it, in a town known for lynching black people. Yes, we are activists. Yes, we stand up for righteousness and speak against the evils and atrocities that happen to our people. That puts fear in our oppressors, and he is doing their bidding: hey, you’ve been cooning great lately.

So what is better than standing up for God and standing up for his people? “And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men.”

We always have to do what is right toward God and toward our people. Better looks like getting your household in order, not committing fornication and adultery, taking care of your family. What is better than that? That is what a conscience void of offence looks like, and he is not speaking from the point of a black man.

precepts.label: Nehemiah 9:27
precepts.why:
“Therefore thou deliveredst them into the hand of their enemies, who vexed them”. That is what happened to us: we have been delivered into the hands of our enemies, the yoke of iron of Deuteronomy 28:48.

“and in the time of their trouble, when they cried unto thee, thou heardest them from heaven”. That is what is happening now. The Lord is starting to hear our cry. We are supposed to pray unto the Lord until he brings vengeance; that is what the Bible tells us to do.

“and according to thy manifold mercies thou gavest them saviours, who saved them out of the hand of their enemies.” How is that happening? By the purple and gold going to this city and that city, this country and that country, teaching the word of God. These are the saviours, and the saviours showed up in Ocean Springs, Mississippi.

So when we see these things happen to our people, yes, we are going to be there, and no, we are not going to stop. We don’t care if we have coons among our own people; we are going to rise up and save the day, because that is how God ordained it. Tatum is mad about it. Get mad. You hate your people and you hate your God.

precepts.label: Exodus 7:4
precepts.why:
A 1966 CBS documentary, Black Power, White Backlash, went into Cicero, Illinois, where 15,000 black people worked in the factories every day but not a single black family lived, and every one of them had to leave when the sun went down. A resident said there are many good coloreds, but the ones that are going to march, I don’t like.

They do not like it when we march, because when we march we have our pride, our dignity, our respect and our confidence. They do not like when we stand up as the nation of Israel; it angers them and it makes them afraid. We have been marching; Marcus Garvey was marching back in the day.

“But Pharaoh shall not hearken unto you, that I may lay my hand upon Egypt, and bring forth mine armies, and my people the children of Israel, out of the land of Egypt by great judgments.” Mine armies. We have been marching since Egypt, and we marched around the walls of Jericho.

Israel came out of Egypt as the armies of the Lord, by great judgments on the ones who held them. That is why our marching troubles our oppressors.

precepts.label: Revelation 11:11
precepts.why:
They do not like when we stand up on our feet with confidence as the nation of Israel, not as blacks, but as the nation of Israel.

“And after three days and an half the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them.”

Great fear falls on them when they see us rise up as the children of God, as the army of the living God. That is what the man in Cicero feared when he said he could not stand the ones who march, and it is what puts fear in our oppressors when the brothers show up in a town like Ocean Springs. The yoke of iron destroyed us, but the Spirit of life from God stands us back on our feet.

precepts.label: 2 Chronicles 17:9
precepts.why:
Tatum claimed he had not seen black Hebrew Israelites going out and saying anything in the community when a black man died. That is a lie; he has been found a liar. That is what we do literally every week. We teach in the hoods and the ghettos where our people are: O Block in Chicago, East St. Louis, Memphis, Miami, Compton, LA, Philly. We go toe to toe and face our people.

“And they taught in Judah, and had the book of the law of the Lord with them, and went about throughout all the cities of Judah, and taught the people.”

They taught in Judah: we go to our people just like the forefathers did. They had the book of the law of the Lord with them: we bring the Bible with us. They went throughout all the cities: we do not just go to one city or one state. Wherever our people are scattered, wherever our people are being afflicted, we are there, teaching the people.

precepts.label: Matthew 15:24
precepts.why:
A pastor named Pam declared that the gospel cannot be for one ethnicity only, that it cannot be just for black men or for white men, and that this is a heretical doctrine preached by false, cultic ministries. Either the cultic ministries are right or Jesus is right; somebody is wrong. It’s you, Pam.

“But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”

It is only for one nation, twelve tribes. If you are not part of that, you are not getting in. Some of our people are bugged the hell out, and it is a direct correlation to slavery. A white pastor even said God blessed black Americans through white people and slavery, and Tatum agrees with that. But Christ was sent to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, the same people under the yoke of iron of Deuteronomy 28:48.

precepts.label: Revelation 21:12
precepts.why:
The holy city “had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel”.

Praises to the Most High for that. The kingdom is only for God’s people. The gates of the city carry the names of the twelve tribes, and no other nation’s name is written there.

That settles what Pam called heresy. Christ was not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel, and the city he brings has twelve gates for the twelve tribes. The same people the Lord sent into bondage with a yoke of iron upon their neck are the people whose names are on the gates.

thread.text: But king Solomon loved many strange women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh, women of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Zidonians, and Hittites;

classes.title: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

precepts.label: Tobit 4:12-13
precepts.why:
“But king Solomon loved many strange women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh”. When you turn against the Lord in this, you turn against your neighbor too, because you are taking foreign women. We know it will turn your heart away from following the Lord, but what does it do to your brother? It says you hate your brother. Tobit shows it.

“Beware of all whoredom, my son, and chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father’s tribe”. He calls interracial marriage whoredom. “for we are the children of the prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: remember, my son, that our fathers from the beginning, even that they all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children, and their seed shall inherit the land.”

“Now therefore, my son, love thy brethren, and despise not in thy heart thy brethren, the sons and daughters of thy people, in not taking a wife of them”. Don’t despise your brethren. Passing over the daughters of your own people for strange women is despising your brethren in your heart. “for in pride is destruction and much trouble, and in lewdness is decay and great want: for lewdness is the mother of famine.”

That is exactly where Solomon went. The Lord had said of those nations, “Ye shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in unto you: for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods”, and Solomon clave unto them in love. His wives turned away his heart after Ashtoreth, Milcom, Chemosh and Molech, and he built high places for them and for all his strange wives. That is how syncretism enters: through the strange wife, and it begins by despising your own people.

thread.label: 1 Kings 11:9-13, 27-31
thread.text: And the Lord was angry with Solomon, because his heart was turned from the Lord God of Israel, which had appeared unto him twice,

classes.title: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 1:17
precepts.why:
“And the Lord was angry with Solomon, because his heart was turned from the Lord God of Israel”. What happened? Solomon got old. He had seven hundred wives and three hundred concubines, and he built houses of worship for their individual gods. They did not all serve the same god: Chemosh, Remphan, Ashtoreth of the Zidonians, Molech. Some of those gods required child sacrifice; some involved sexual orgies. And Israel had to pay taxes for those gods.

Solomon said it himself: “And I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly: I perceived that this also is vexation of spirit.” Madness and folly means all kind of sin. However your mind can go, Solomon went there. When Solomon got old, he did a lot of evil. And yes, he did repent, when you read Ecclesiastes 12.

So the Lord said, “I will surely rend the kingdom from thee”, but “Notwithstanding in thy days I will not do it for David thy father’s sake: but I will rend it out of the hand of thy son.” That is why Ahijah tore Jeroboam’s new garment into twelve pieces and told him to take ten: the northern kingdom, while one tribe was kept for David’s sake. That is the tabernacle of David that fell.

thread.label: 1 Kings 12:1-19
thread.text: And Rehoboam went to Shechem: for all Israel were come to Shechem to make him king.

classes.title: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 30:4-6
precepts.why:
Rehoboam took his father’s throne. “Though his father die, yet he is as though he were not dead: for he hath left one behind him that is like himself.” When you die, your son should be in your image. “While he lived, he saw and rejoiced in him: and when he died, he was not sorrowful.”

“He left behind him an avenger against his enemies, and one that shall requite kindness to his friends.” Your son is supposed to look after his father’s friends.

The old men who stood before Solomon were his father’s friends, and they counselled him: “If thou wilt be a servant unto this people this day, and wilt serve them, and answer them, and speak good words to them, then they will be thy servants for ever.” “But he forsook the counsel of the old men”. And he was like his father in the worst way: Solomon in his old age forced the people to pay tribute to the houses of his wives’ gods, and Rehoboam said, “my father hath chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.” I am going to be worse than my father.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 3:6
precepts.why:
Rehoboam “forsook the counsel of the old men, which they had given him, and consulted with the young men that were grown up with him”. Those are his peers. Notice the difference: to the old men he asked, “How do ye advise that I may answer this people?” To the young men, “What counsel give ye that we may answer this people”? We, all together: y’all are my peers, we are running this thing.

Paul warns about that kind of counsel: “Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.” A novice is a beginner, a newbie, a neophyte. Lifted up with pride: I know all the precepts. His head gets big because he thinks he knows it all. That is young men, and that type of spirit will destroy itself.

So that is who Rehoboam looked to, and the young men told him to say, “My little finger shall be thicker than my father’s loins.” Some of you in here make that same mistake.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 10:21
precepts.why:
“And the king answered the people roughly, and forsook the old men’s counsel”. Sirach tells what that does: “The fear of the Lord goeth before the obtaining of authority: but roughness and pride is the losing thereof.” You rule people with roughness and pride, you are going to lose your position.

That is what happened to Rehoboam. The ten tribes said “What portion have we in David?” “to your tents, O Israel: now see to thine own house, David.” When he sent Adoram, who was over the tribute, all Israel stoned him to death: you came to collect money? We are not giving you anything. Rehoboam made speed to get up to his chariot and flee to Jerusalem, thinking they would kill him next. “So Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.”

We just had a case like that in Cali, and many cases in the states, New York and Texas, where brothers felt that in order to be the leader of the sanctuary they had to rule the people with roughness and pride, and they were taking advantage of the brothers and sisters. No: we had to remove you. Roughness and pride is the losing of authority.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 9:4
precepts.why:
The man of God out of Judah was charged by the word of the Lord, “Eat no bread, nor drink water, nor turn again by the same way that thou camest.” The Lord told him what not to do and what to do. He refused the king, even for half his house. Then an old prophet in Bethel came after him: “I am a prophet also as thou art; and an angel spake unto me by the word of the Lord, saying, Bring him back with thee into thine house, that he may eat bread and drink water. But he lied unto him.”

This dude was lying. God said the only one he speaks with mouth to mouth is Moses; everybody else he speaks to with dreams and visions, and this man said an angel came to him. The man of God went back, ate and drank, and “a lion met him by the way, and slew him”: “It is the man of God, who was disobedient unto the word of the Lord”.

That is why the Lord said, “Take ye heed every one of his neighbour, and trust ye not in any brother: for every brother will utterly supplant, and every neighbour will walk with slanders.” That is why you have to be mindful with brothers. If God tells you something, follow it; don’t go to the left or right of what he says because a brother says so. Follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth.

Some people are in your life for blessings, some are in your life for cursings; but ultimately it is to try us, each and every one of us.

thread.label: 2 Kings 19:14-37
thread.text: And Hezekiah received the letter of the hand of the messengers, and read it: and Hezekiah went up into the house of the Lord, and spread it before the Lord.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 5:7
precepts.why:
Assyria had already taken the northern kingdom around 722 BC, and around 701 they came for Judah. Their ambassador was talking big: we are going to wipe the floor with you, destroy you and bring you into slavery. Then came a letter of threats. And look at what Hezekiah did with it: he “went up into the house of the Lord, and spread it before the Lord.” He took the letter, spread it out before him, and began to pray: “thou art the God, even thou alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth”.

That is what Peter teaches: “Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.” Sometimes we get in situations and fear comes upon us. Go before the Lord. Whatever the problem is, the Lord knows; go before him and spread it out before him, the way Hezekiah did.

And the Lord answered. Isaiah was not in the room when Hezekiah prayed, but the Lord told him to go to the king and say, “That which thou hast prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria I have heard.” That is how you know Isaiah was a prophet. Hezekiah cast his care upon the Lord, and that same night one angel smote 185,000 Assyrians.

precepts.label: Matthew 12:36
precepts.why:
The Lord asks Sennacherib, “Whom hast thou reproached and blasphemed? and against whom hast thou exalted thy voice, and lifted up thine eyes on high? even against the Holy One of Israel.” By his messengers he had reproached the Lord with his boasting words, and every one of them came up into the Lord's ears: “thy rage against me and thy tumult is come up into mine ears”. The same words also remind our people how we have despised the Lord.

Christ said, “every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.” We have to be mindful of this. Sometimes we speak frivolous things and don't realize the Most High is recording everything. Idle means idolatrous: every idolatrous word we speak.

Sennacherib's words were recorded and answered: the Lord put his hook in his nose and turned him back the way he came. So be careful what comes out of your mouth; the Most High hears it all and will bring it to account.

precepts.label: Job 11:6
precepts.why:
When you go to the Christian commentaries on Isaiah 33, many of them refer it back to this history: Hezekiah, the king of Assyria, and the angel that wiped them all out. They try to keep every prophecy in the past, as history that already happened. That is why the apologists love to say, that happened already: they read a Christian commentary that said so.

But the scriptures have dual meanings. Job says he “would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is!” We all want to know the secrets of wisdom, and they are double to that which is written. You read something, but it has a double meaning behind it. That's how the scriptures are written.

So Isaiah 33:1, “Woe to thee that spoilest, and thou wast not spoiled; and dealest treacherously, and they dealt not treacherously with thee!”, was Assyria; but guess who also does that today? The United States of America. To spoil means to rob: the oil of Venezuela, the riches of Libya and of Saddam Hussein, Iran, which did nothing to America. “when thou shalt cease to spoil, thou shalt be spoiled”. The history of 2 Kings 19 happened, and the same word speaks to our day.

thread.text: Even after a certain rate every day, offering according to the commandment of Moses, on the sabbaths, and on the new moons, and on the solemn feasts, three times in the year, even in the feast of unleavened bread, and in

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 35:1
precepts.why:
Solomon offered “according to the commandment of Moses”, on the sabbaths, the new moons and the solemn feasts, “three times in the year”: the feast of unleavened bread, the feast of weeks and the feast of tabernacles. It is the same law given in Deuteronomy 16:16: “Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord thy God”, and “they shall not appear before the Lord empty.” So we are supposed to gather and give an offering three times a year. We come together.

But do we give a physical offering today? No. So what do we offer? We offer ourselves; we offer obedience. Sirach puts it plainly: “He that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough: he that taketh heed to the commandment offereth a peace offering.”

Keeping the law is the offering. The one who takes heed to the commandment is not coming before the Lord empty; his obedience is his peace offering. That is how Israel keeps these feasts now, the feast of weeks, which is Pentecost, among them: by gathering together and bringing a life that keeps the commandments.

precepts.label: Isaiah 45:1
precepts.why:
During the Persian captivity we got liberty. Cyrus proclaimed, “The Lord God of heaven hath given me all the kingdoms of the earth”, and he said that because he knew it was a prophecy. Isaiah had written it: “Thus saith the Lord to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have holden, to subdue nations before him; and I will loose the loins of kings, to open before him the two leaved gates; and the gates shall not be shut”.

Why is that important? Write this down: it was written 150 years before the birth of Cyrus. So when he came of age, he was shown his name in the scriptures, and he knew that the God of Israel, based on that prophecy, was dealing with him to release his people. It goes into more detail in the writings of Flavius Josephus, how the prophets showed Cyrus what he must do. And he obeyed.

So he made his proclamation to all twelve tribes: “Who is there among you of all his people?” Not just Judah. And whoever chose to stay where they had been living for decades, “let the men of his place help him with silver, and with gold, and with goods, and with beasts”. Some of the northern kingdom went back with Judah; some of the southern kingdom stayed out. Everybody did not go back.

thread.label: Job 5:11-27
thread.text: To set up on high those that be low; that those which mourn may be exalted to safety.

precepts.label: 1 Samuel 2:3-8
precepts.why:
Job 5:11 says the Lord will “set up on high those that be low.” That is us: we are low right now, but he is going to set us up on high. And “those which mourn may be exalted to safety”: our people that mourn shall be exalted to safety and comfort. 1 Samuel 2 goes with it.

“Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth.” The arrogancy is the foolishness, the teaching and the wisdom of this world. Pastor, don’t let that come out of your mouth. “For the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.” He is going to judge all of us on our actions. Not your thoughts, though you must control your thoughts, but on what you do.

“The bows of the mighty men are broken, and they that stumbled are girded with strength.” “The Lord killeth, and maketh alive”: it is the Lord that kills and the Lord that makes alive. “The Lord maketh poor, and maketh rich: he bringeth low, and lifteth up.” That is what Job 5:11 just said: we are being brought low, but we are going to be exalted.

“He raiseth up the poor out of the dust.” The dust represents confusion, a low state of confusion, and the poor are the poor in spirit. “And lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill.” We are the beggar. Our people are begging for reparations, give us money; I want Section 8, I want a job, I want this. And the dunghill is this low place: whatever kind of house you have, compared to where we came from, it is a dunghill.

But he lifts them up “to set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory: for the pillars of the earth are the Lord’s, and he hath set the world upon them.” The Lord is going to make us inherit the throne of glory. That is the setting up on high of those that be low in Job 5:11.

precepts.label: Romans 5:3-5
precepts.why:
Job 5:17: “Behold, happy is the man whom God correcteth: therefore despise not thou the chastening of the Almighty.” We get corrected all the time. We might not be happy while we are going through it, but it says happy is the man whom God corrects. Romans 5 shows why.

“And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience.” There is a purpose behind tribulation: it works patience. “And patience, experience”: patience teaches you experience. “And experience, hope: And hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts.”

That means we understand why God is allowing us to go through tribulation. He is teaching us something. While we are in it we might not understand it, but he is saying, I am trying to teach you a lesson here. That is why we do not despise the chastening of the Almighty.

precepts.label: Hebrews 12:6-8
precepts.why:
“For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth.” Whom the Lord loves, he chastises. This is why we go through things in our lives that we might not like at the moment. It is the same thing Job 5:17 says: “happy is the man whom God correcteth.”

“And scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.” So if you are in this truth, expect to get scourged. Expect to get beat.

“If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?” If you endure that chastisement, God is dealing with you like a son. “But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.” Nobody wants to be a bastard. So “despise not thou the chastening of the Almighty”: the chastening is the proof that you are his son.

precepts.label: Isaiah 1:4-6
precepts.why:
Job 5:18: “For he maketh sore, and bindeth up: he woundeth, and his hands make whole.” He makes us sore, and Isaiah 1 shows where we are bruised from the top of our head.

“Ah sinful nation”: that is us, you and me. “A people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters”: we are the corrupters. “They have forsaken the Lord”: our people have forsaken the Lord. “They have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, they are gone away backward”: we have gone backwards from God’s laws.

“Why should ye be stricken any more?” God is saying, I keep punishing you over and over, why should you be stricken any more? “Ye will revolt more and more: the whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint. From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with ointment.”

In Isaiah 1:4-6 he is talking about us in comparison with Job. Job was real, don’t get it wrong, but his life represents the nation of Israel. He lost everything, even his health, from the top of his head to the soles of his feet, and that is what Isaiah says about the nation of Israel as a whole. But the same God that “maketh sore” also “bindeth up”; “his hands make whole.” He will make us whole again.

precepts.label: Revelation 11:15
precepts.why:
Job 5:19: “He shall deliver thee in six troubles: yea, in seven there shall no evil touch thee.” The six troubles mean the six trumps. And the seventh?

“And the seventh angel sounded; and there were great voices in heaven, saying, The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ; and he shall reign for ever and ever.”

So by the seventh trump there shall no evil touch us. It is going to be kingdom time. Then Job goes on: “In famine he shall redeem thee from death: and in war from the power of the sword.” “Thou shalt be hid from the scourge of the tongue”: nobody is going to utter a word ever against the twelve tribes of Israel; you fix your lips to call us something, that’s off with your head. “Neither shalt thou be afraid of destruction when it cometh”: he is telling us not to be afraid when destruction comes, because it is going to come. Some don’t believe that because of America, God bless the USA, nothing could ever happen here. But it is coming, and the angels are going to protect the brothers and sisters that are alive at that time.

precepts.label: Isaiah 60:21-22
precepts.why:
Job 5:24: “And thou shalt know that thy tabernacle shall be in peace; and thou shalt visit thy habitation, and shalt not sin.” We won’t sin. Isaiah 60:21 says the same.

“Thy people also shall be all righteous”: our people shall be all righteous. “They shall inherit the land for ever”: we shall inherit the land forever. “The branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified”: we are the branch of God’s planting.

“A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation: I the Lord will hasten it in his time.” We are going to have a whole lot of children. He is going to make sure to bring back certain spirits through marriage and childbearing; certain spirits are going to come back real quick.

That is Job 5:25-26: “thy seed shall be great, and thine offspring as the grass of the earth.” Our children are going to grow up quick. “Thou shalt come to thy grave in a full age, like as a shock of corn cometh in in his season.” Like a shock of corn comes back over and over, Israel is going to have a long, long life. That is why he calls it forever, eternal.

precepts.label: Psalms 91:7
precepts.why:
We read the judgment: the sword coming for Esau and for the nations, for the Lord “will give them that are wicked to the sword”. “But he saveth the poor from the sword, from their mouth, and from the hand of the mighty.” Israel is the poor, and you escape that judgment by keeping the commandments with faith in the Lord and Saviour Jesus the Christ. “So the poor hath hope”: hope that something better is coming than what we are in right now.

“He shall deliver thee in six troubles: yea, in seven there shall no evil touch thee.” David shows what that looks like: “A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand; but it shall not come nigh thee.” That fire is not coming near you.

All that is read here is judgment: famine, war, the sword. “In famine he shall redeem thee from death: and in war from the power of the sword.” He is going to deliver you and redeem you from the power of that sword, even while thousands fall around you.

But it comes with correction: “happy is the man whom God correcteth”. Brothers get soft and mealy and yellow about correction, and sisters get bitter at those who correct them. Get rid of that soft spirit; man up and woman up. “he maketh sore, and bindeth up: he woundeth, and his hands make whole.” He wounds you with the word and makes you whole again, so that no evil touches you when the judgment falls.
