precepts.label: Job 5:12-13
precepts.why:
“The steps of his strength shall be straitened, and his own counsel shall cast him down. For he is cast into a net by his own feet, and he walketh upon a snare.” His own counsel casts him down.

Job 5 says the same: “He disappointeth the devices of the crafty, so that their hands cannot perform their enterprise. He taketh the wise in their own craftiness: and the counsel of the froward is carried headlong.”

Remember it: crafty counsel. All of the things they did against us are crafty counsel. The way your neighborhood is set up, redlining, benign neglect, all of it; slavery, exploitation, colonization: all of it is crafty counsel. And God takes the wise in their own craftiness. The net Esau laid is the net his own feet are caught in, and his counsel is carried headlong.

That is how “the light of the wicked shall be put out”. And when Esau's light is put out, the black Christian's head comes right out of the white man's behind. That is the only way the Lord can separate you from the white man, because you are too far gone.

precepts.label: Acts 26:23
precepts.why:
“Terrors shall make him afraid on every side”: the missiles, the ICBMs. “His strength shall be hungerbitten, and destruction shall be ready at his side. It shall devour the strength of his skin: even the firstborn of death shall devour his strength.”

Who is the firstborn of death? Paul tells it: “That Christ should suffer, and that he should be the first that should rise from the dead”. That is the firstborn of death right there: Christ. He was the first raised up.

So it is Christ who will devour Esau's strength. “His confidence shall be rooted out of his tabernacle, and it shall bring him to the king of terrors.” Your slave master, the one who taught you how to fear God, will be brought to the king of terrors. “brimstone shall be scattered upon his habitation. His roots shall be dried up beneath, and above shall his branch be cut off.” His branch is his children. The one who rose first from the dead is the one who cuts him off.

precepts.label: Psalms 109:15
precepts.why:
“His remembrance shall perish from the earth, and he shall have no name in the street.” Your slave master, the one who taught you about this Bible, shall perish from the earth. David says it too: “Let them be before the Lord continually, that he may cut off the memory of them from the earth.” God said their memory will be cut off.

“He shall be driven from light into darkness, and chased out of the world.” There is going to come a time when knowing about Esau will be like a bad dream: man, I had a dream I was in slavery to the basest people on planet earth.

“He shall neither have son nor nephew among his people, nor any remaining in his dwellings.” Cut off totally; a time is coming when they will not be around any more. “Surely such are the dwellings of the wicked, and this is the place of him that knoweth not God.” This ain't talking about our people; it is talking about Esau, the wicked on the earth. Destruction is coming to him, and even his memory will be cut off.

precepts.label: Job 20:24
precepts.why:
Here is more about Esau: “Knowest thou not this of old, since man was placed upon earth, That the triumphing of the wicked is short, and the joy of the hypocrite but for a moment?” Triumphing means victory: the victory of the wicked is short. America is the biggest hypocrite on planet earth, and its joy is but for a moment. This is temporary; there is going to be an end to it. All we have to do is be patient and wait.

And how does it end? “He shall flee from the iron weapon, and the bow of steel shall strike him through.” The iron weapon is the missile.

It goes with what was read in Isaiah 54: “Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire, and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work; and I have created the waster to destroy.” The smith of old is what is called a scientist today, who makes weapons, and the waster is nuclear power. God let him create the waster to destroy, and the same weapons he made will strike him through.

So do not be joined to him. Isaiah says, “every one that is joined unto them shall fall by the sword.” Everyone found married to these demons and having kids by them shall be thrust through, and many of our people will fall into that. Do not feel sorry for them. The triumphing of the wicked is short.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 12:10-12
precepts.why:
Job 20:12-13 says “Though wickedness be sweet in his mouth, though he hide it under his tongue; Though he spare it, and forsake it not”. This white man loves wickedness, and he hid it for almost sixty years. From the civil rights era up until this new administration, you saw a new America: they loved black and brown people, we got jobs, we reached the heights of government, even President Barack Hussein Obama. Then the new administration came in and said, you're fired, you're fired. DEI, get out. Affirmative action, no more. Howard University dropped 52 incoming freshmen, and over 3,000 black women in high-ranking positions were fired. This is not a new America; it's the old America coming back.

So God says, “Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.” It will surely come to pass. “Though he humble himself, and go crouching”: he's nice to you, you got the promotion you wanted, you got that house at a discount, they helped you get a discount on a new car. You say, no, these are good white folks, I know them. “yet take good heed and beware of him”.

“and thou shalt know that his rust hath not been altogether wiped away.” The rust represents his wickedness. It's still there, kept still within his mouth, just as Job says.

“Set him not by thee, lest, when he hath overthrown thee, he stand up in thy place”. That is what happened historically. We set them by us at the end of the dark ages, and they conquered us and took our place as the Jews and the Christians. Even the records show it: the Arab historians and geographers, who were black Jews that spoke Arabic, wrote of black Jewish communities in Africa, the land of the Hebrews between Abyssinia and Congo and the Jews on both sides of the river Niger, and Esau asked, is this real or imagined, and wrote them down as imagined. He stood up in our place.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 12:10-12
precepts.why:
Job 20:12 says “Though wickedness be sweet in his mouth, though he hide it under his tongue”. That is the white man. He hid the evil speech for about sixty years, from the civil rights, and now he says the time is up: we're tired of feeling bad, we ain't humbling ourselves to you no more, we're going to tell you exactly how we feel. They call it black fatigue. “Though he spare it, and forsake it not”: it's still there.

Now Sirach gives a name to this wicked man: “Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.” But to understand this you must be able to identify who the enemy is. Black people call each other the enemy, but they will never look at their oppressor and say, that white man enslaved us, that's the enemy.

“Though he humble himself, and go crouching, yet take good heed and beware of him”. He's nice to you today; they smile that plastic smile in your face. The white man gave me a raise: that don't mean nothing, they had a budget. Affirmative action? They got rid of that too, thanks to that negro Clarence Thomas, who became a judge by affirmative action and then ended it: I made mine, now I'm ending it. “and thou shalt be unto him as if thou hadst wiped a lookingglass, and thou shalt know that his rust hath not been altogether wiped away.” Like a looking glass covered with dust that you wipe: now you can see through the glass. The wickedness of verse 10 is still with him.

“Set him not by thee, lest, when he hath overthrown thee, he stand up in thy place”. That is what we did. The black Jews wanted to fight against the Muslims, went to the Caucasus Mountains and said, we need the help of the Khazars. They converted to Judaism, joined our army, and we set them by us all through our military. Now he's the Jew and you're the Gentile; he's the Christian and you're the Gentile.

“neither let him sit at thy right hand, lest he seek to take thy seat”. When black people get in business with white folks, it'll be the black man's business, and somehow the white man takes it over, like the brother who made an Edomite's empty steakhouse boom and it all got copyrighted away from him. Don't trust these white folks, even the one you think is different. “and thou at the last remember my words, and be pricked therewith”: when they tell you to put your teeth on the curb, like American History X, then you're going to remember God's words.

precepts.label: Romans 10:14-18
precepts.why:
David says “Day unto day uttereth speech, and night unto night sheweth knowledge”, and “Their line is gone out through all the earth”. You might think that speech and knowledge is the sun, the moon and the stars. No, it is the teachers, brothers out teaching day by day and night by night. Paul broke it down for us so we don't have to do guesswork: “But I say, Have they not heard? Yes verily, their sound went into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world.” Paul is quoting Psalm 19, and their sound is the sound of teaching.

Start at verse 14: “How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher?” Our people cannot call on the Lord if they have not heard. You need a preacher to hear this gospel. “And how shall they preach, except they be sent?” To preach is to prophesy, and it takes being sent. “How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!” That is why brothers are told: be prepared. Prepare yourself to be sent.

“Lord, who hath believed our report?” The report is the Bible, the scriptures. The prophets preach the report, and the question is who has believed it.

“So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.” That is how you increase faith. New brothers and sisters ask how to increase their faith: you must consistently addict yourself to the hearing of the gospel, over and over. However old you are, calculate it: that is how many years of brainwashing you must undo. Coming in once a week will not undo it. It must be daily listening to the word, and reading more than the four chapters a day.

And whose sound is going into all the earth? All praises to the Lord for favouring this teaching. The doctrine of having sex with as many women as you can and not taking care of the babies is not going throughout all the earth. The groups talking about raping women and having concubines, the garbage teaching that John the Baptist is a wicked Israelite, the teaching that we are under the old covenant of animal sacrifice: none of that is going throughout the earth. The line that has gone out is repentance for the twelve tribes of Israel in the name of our king whom the world calls Jesus the Christ, heard now in all languages.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 32:27
precepts.why:
“I was cast upon thee from the womb: thou art my God from my mother’s belly.” The trinitarians read it this way: when Christ came into the world as a human being, that's when his Father became his God. The Father has divine essence, the Holy Spirit has divine essence, the Son has divine essence, so when Christ came on the earth keeping humanity and godhood, he is his own god. And not only that: he is his own god and he has a God above him. That's two. It's a ridiculous argument.

“Behold, I am the Lord, the God of all flesh: is there any thing too hard for me?” The Father is the God of all flesh. So if Christ is the essence of his Father, then Christ becomes the God of his own humanity, God over his own flesh. It's madness. Pressed with it in the debate, the trinitarian answered exactly that: Christ is God over his own flesh. And his own side laughed at him; you could see his friend's face in the back. They know that's stupid.

That one question stumped them. There is no scripture that says the heavenly Father becomes his God when he is human, as opposed to being his God always. That's pure theology. Ask them where the Bible says it. Nowhere in Psalms 22 do we read that Christ, out of his mother's womb, is fully God and fully man. That is a Greco-Roman hermeneutical interpretation; they even admitted there is an element of philosophy in it. It isn't an element; it's full-blown philosophy.

The scripture is clear. Resurrected and glorified, Christ says “my God” four times in one verse: “Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God.” And risen from the dead, “I ascend unto my Father, and your Father; and to my God, and your God.” Even “being in the form of God”, he “thought it not robbery to be equal with God”, but “made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant”: God or man, he knew the Father was above him. These men follow the Greeks, “Not setting by the honours of their fathers, but liking the glory of the Grecians best of all”. They are unreasonable people, going in circles like a cartwheel, and you cannot waste your time with them.

precepts.label: Isaiah 35:3-4
precepts.why:
David prays, “raise me up, that I may requite them”: raise me up the third day, so I can get vengeance on the traitor who ate of my bread. Isaiah tells the faithful to hold on for that vengeance: “Strengthen ye the weak hands, and confirm the feeble knees.”

In every IUIC school some brothers may be weak and feeble, spiritually. Build them up. You have to build your inner circle up, loyal and faithful brothers who know the scriptures and fear God, and then have a circle outside of that of trustworthy, loyal men, so that when Jacob's trouble comes you don't all fall.

“Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not”. Brothers and sisters, be strong, because at times you might get afraid, but the Lord has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of a sound mind.

Then: “behold, your God will come with vengeance, even God with a recompence; he will come and save you.” We must believe that our God will come with vengeance. A recompence is a requital, the same word as “that I may requite them” in the psalm: an appropriate return for wrongdoing.

Isaiah 47 shows that vengeance on Babylon: “Thy nakedness shall be uncovered, yea, thy shame shall be seen”. All these fake Christians talking about America being a Christian society: their nakedness is uncovered by the word of God, and all their shameful deeds are revealed. “I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man.” Christ is not coming back meeting them as a man. So strengthen the weak, fear not, and wait on the God who comes with recompence to save us.

Let's examine it. Who is running the earth? Who has military bases all over the world? Whose money is the money you must do business with? The so-called white man, Esau. Who has the power to go into another country, take out its leader, bring him to their own country, and nothing happens to them? Who can say, I don't like your policies, we're going to kill you? They did it in Libya. Recently they did it in Haiti: they killed the president. He didn't want the COVID vaccine, and he had just come from a meeting in Turkey with Russian officials and struck a deal with Russia to make Haiti what it is supposed to be. Two months later: no, you've got to go. Look at the man's rap sheet: a murderer, a killer, and insatiable.

“he covereth the faces of the judges thereof”. Who are the judges? We are. And our faces are covered because we are not known. You can see it on the walls of those churches in Russia and Romania: you still have the black images we left behind. But when they paint a new picture, they paint it white. That is how they covered the faces of the judges. All their movies are white; go on Google and everything is white. But in the Bible, the judges are black.

So when God says to the wicked, what hast thou to do to declare my statutes, he is speaking to the one whose hand the earth was given into. As a Christian he declares the Lord's statutes, as a Jew he claims to keep the laws, taking the old covenant and the new, remixing them and saying everybody can be saved, while he covers the faces of the true judges and takes the land by wickedness.

precepts.label: Job 9:24
precepts.why:
“Truly God is good to Israel, even to such as are of a clean heart”: to the twelve tribes, those who walk in righteousness and do the commandments. “But as for me, my feet were almost gone; my steps had well nigh slipped. For I was envious at the foolish, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.” Some of us in here get envious the same way when we see the prosperity of the wicked.

Who is the wicked? Job says: “The earth is given into the hand of the wicked”. If you don't know who the wicked is, it is telling you by a process of elimination. It ain't the black man and the Latin man; we are not ruling anything. We can't even rule our own homes. The white man rules supreme on this planet. You want anything done in your country, you have to go through that white man.

“he covereth the faces of the judges thereof”. The judges are God, Christ, the angels and the Israelites, and it is the white man who covers their faces. Look at the paintings: black Mary with a black baby Christ, and somehow that baby grows up and, Shazam, becomes a white man, and nobody sees anything wrong with that.

So the wicked whose prosperity Asaph envied is the one the earth has been given to for a time: the man who whitewashed the faces of the judges.

precepts.label: Malachi 1:3-4
precepts.why:
Job 9:24 says the wicked has the earth. Malachi names him: “And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.” That is the Dark Ages, when God made Esau poverty-stricken.

“Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places”. They returned in the time called the Renaissance, and that is when they conquered us and made us their slaves, Christian slaves. “thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down”. God said, I will give you a chance to build: they built up America, England, France, Germany, Australia, all those places they robbed and pillaged.

“and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” Indignation means righteous anger, for ever. So it identifies who the wicked is: Esau, Edom.

That is why Asaph saw him prospering: wherever Esau goes, it seems whatever he touches turns to gold. But he is building only to be thrown down.

precepts.label: Psalms 140:1-5
precepts.why:
“Therefore pride compasseth them about as a chain; violence covereth them as a garment.” They have so much wealth that pride covers them like a chain, and much of their old slave money is invested in war companies, weaponry and the military. David names him: “Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man: preserve me from the violent man”. This is about the white man. Preserve us from him.

“Which imagine mischiefs in their heart; continually are they gathered together for war.” If there is no war, you can bet your last dollar the white man will start one. He can never let there be peace on earth; the way God made him, it is his nature. Trump pledged to end global conflict and bombed at least seven countries in 2025; under Obama in 2016, 26,171 bombs were dropped on seven countries. And they took Maduro with weapons that shut his military down in minutes.

“They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent; adders’ poison is under their lips. Selah.” Selah means it is true. Whatever comes out of their mouth, religion or politics, is the worst kind of poison; for some of them politics is their religion. Take hold of it and you will die.

“Keep me, O Lord, from the hands of the wicked; preserve me from the violent man; who have purposed to overthrow my goings.” Their purpose on earth is to overthrow the twelve tribes of Israel. They can't rest if they see one of us in a nice car or a nice home: he must be selling drugs. “The proud have hid a snare for me, and cords; they have spread a net by the wayside; they have set gins for me.” The cords and the net are their traps of religion and politics, and a gin is a trap too. He is the wicked of Job 9:24 and Malachi 1, and he wears violence like he wears clothes.

precepts.label: Micah 6:11-12
precepts.why:
“Behold, these are the ungodly, who prosper in the world; they increase in riches.” Read the top ten billionaires: Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos, Bernard Arnault, Bill Gates, Mark Zuckerberg, and the rest. Zuckerberg stole Facebook from the college kids who hired him to create it. Micah asks: “Shall I count them pure with the wicked balances, and with the bag of deceitful weights?” Wicked balances are unjust judgments.

“For the rich men thereof are full of violence”. These rich people come from old money, gotten through the rape, robbery and pillaging of our nations and our people.

“and the inhabitants thereof have spoken lies, and their tongue is deceitful in their mouth.” Their descendants will say anything to justify the evil of their ancestors: it wasn't me, it was my ancestors, but I enjoy what they did. Why? Because they benefit from it.

That is what Asaph envied before he went into the sanctuary of God. Many times we envy people without knowing how they got their money, but nine times out of ten, especially with white folks, it came through criminality. Only by reading and understanding the word of God will you understand their end: set in slippery places and cast down into destruction.

thread.label: Psalms 91:1-16
thread.text: He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 29:29
precepts.why:
“He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.” The secret place of the Most High is the Bible. Moses says so: “The secret things belong unto the Lord our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law.” God's word is his secrets, and what he has revealed of it belongs to Israel and our children forever, so that we may do his law.

So dwelling in the secret place means living in his word and keeping it. That is why “his truth shall be thy shield and buckler”: his law is thy shield and buckler. The one who dwells there can say “He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust.”

That is who the psalm protects when destruction comes. And it is coming, though some do not believe it because of God bless the USA, nothing could ever happen here. Job says “neither shalt thou be afraid of destruction when it cometh”, because the Lord is telling us it is going to come. The arrow that flieth by day is the missile, and the destruction that wasteth at noonday tells you the time.

“A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand; but it shall not come nigh thee. Only with thine eyes shalt thou behold and see the reward of the wicked.” The only reason we will see that and not be touched is “Because thou hast made the Lord, which is my refuge, even the most High, thy habitation”: because we dwell in the secret place, his word and his law.

precepts.label: Matthew 24:30-31
precepts.why:
“For he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways. They shall bear thee up in their hands, lest thou dash thy foot against a stone.” What is that talking about? Matthew 24 shows it.

“And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory. And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” Those are the angels given charge over us.

There is going to be so much destruction that the angels will make sure we do not get hurt. We are going to be delivered while our enemies are being put to death. That is “Only with thine eyes shalt thou behold and see the reward of the wicked.” The angels will protect the brothers and sisters alive at that time, so that, as Job says, “At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh.”

Then “Thou shalt tread upon the lion and adder: the young lion and the dragon shalt thou trample under feet”: these are the nations, and we are going to trample them. Because the believer has set his love upon the Lord, he says “therefore will I deliver him: I will set him on high, because he hath known my name.” “I will be with him in trouble; I will deliver him, and honour him. With long life will I satisfy him, and shew him my salvation.”

precepts.label: Revelation 21:12-17
precepts.why:
David says, “Jerusalem is builded as a city that is compact together: Whither the tribes go up, the tribes of the Lord, unto the testimony of Israel.” Other nations aren't there; they are not mentioned here. Why does it say the city is compact together? Revelation shows the city.

It “had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel.” This is our book. The kingdom is ours. The names on the gates are the tribes that go up.

“And the city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth: and he measured the city with the reed, twelve thousand furlongs. The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal.” So it is 1,500 miles, the length, the breadth and the height all equal, like a square, like a box. That is a city compact together.

“And he measured the wall thereof, an hundred and forty and four cubits, according to the measure of a man, that is, of the angel.” A hundred and forty-four cubits is approximately 216 feet by a man's measure, but it is the measure of the angel, so it is actually larger. That is the Jerusalem the tribes of the Lord go up to.

precepts.label: Revelation 20:4
precepts.why:
David says of Jerusalem, “For there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.” John saw those thrones: “And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them.”

Thrones set, people sitting on them, and judgment given to them. And who are they? The souls “beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands; and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.”

The thrones of judgment in the psalm are real thrones in the kingdom, where the faithful reign with Christ. That is the Jerusalem the tribes go up to, and that is why we pray for its peace: it is a people before it is a place, and those thrones belong to us.

precepts.label: Luke 22:29-30
precepts.why:
The psalm says that in Jerusalem “there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.” Christ tells his apostles who sits on them and whom they judge: “And I appoint unto you a kingdom, as my Father hath appointed unto me; That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.”

Sit on thrones doing what? Judging the twelve tribes of Israel. The thrones of judgment are for Israel, just as the tribes that go up to Jerusalem are “the tribes of the Lord, unto the testimony of Israel.”

So don't read all this and try to throw the Chinese and the Japanese and everybody in there. Stop it. The kingdom, the table, the thrones and the judgment all belong to the twelve tribes.

precepts.label: Isaiah 62:7
precepts.why:
David says, “Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: they shall prosper that love thee.” Some of y'all are busy praying for Haiti, praying for Puerto Rico, praying for Mexico, praying for America. But the Bible said pray for Jerusalem.

Isaiah says how to pray for it: “And give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth.” Give the Lord no rest until he establishes Jerusalem and makes it a praise in the earth.

Remember, Jerusalem is a people before it is a place. We are Jerusalem; pray for us. We are not supposed to be praying, stop the war over there. No: they have to be moved out of our land so that we can go back home. That is the peace of Jerusalem, and that is the prayer that gives God no rest until it is done.

thread.label: Psalms 137:5-6
thread.text: If I forget thee, O Jerusalem, let my right hand forget her cunning.

classes.title: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 33:2
precepts.why:
The Israelite way of life is structured so that if you lose your nationality, you are also cut off from your heritage. When they strip you of your identity, your laws, statutes and commandments follow it out the door; you stop performing the laws. Ezra prayed for “seed unto our heart, and culture to our understanding”: culture is heritage.

So “If I forget thee, O Jerusalem, let my right hand forget her cunning.” The right hand is your strength; you usually work with your right hand. Jerusalem is our homeland, the place where you keep the laws and keep the feasts. Forget Jerusalem, and it is like forgetting your ability to work, the thing you know how to do.

Deuteronomy 33:2 shows what is in that right hand: “The Lord came from Sinai, and rose up from Seir unto them; he shined forth from mount Paran, and he came with ten thousands of saints: from his right hand went a fiery law for them.” The law came from God's right hand.

So if you forget your identity, guess what else goes with it? Your way of life, the fiery law. Forgetting Jerusalem and losing the cunning of the right hand is losing the law along with the nationality.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 3:26
precepts.why:
“If I do not remember thee, let my tongue cleave to the roof of my mouth.” If we do not remember the Lord and his laws, statutes and commandments, the tongue sticks and you cannot talk; you cannot teach his laws to your people. The pastors in the churches have their tongues cleaving to the roof of their mouths, because they are not teaching the laws of God.

Ezekiel 3:26 says God does it: “And I will make thy tongue cleave to the roof of thy mouth, that thou shalt be dumb.” That thou shalt be a Christian. You are not Israel anymore, you are not keeping the commandments, you do not have faith in Christ; you have faith in white Jesus and in the white man. God made you into a Christian dummy.

Try to talk with your tongue cleaving to the roof of your mouth and hear how you sound. Everybody looks at you like, what's wrong with this dude? That is how Christians sound to those who know the Bible: level five retards, dumb ass Christians making up dumb doctrines, who think they are in the spirit of the Lord. To other Christians they sound totally fine and normal.

“and shalt not be to them a reprover”: you will be unable to reprove your people with this Bible. You are going to be like Michael Todd and Pastor Pam and all these foolish idiots, ordained ministers from the white man's theology schools and seminary classes.

And “if I prefer not Jerusalem above my chief joy”: we cannot prefer Jerusalem as our chief joy if we do not even know we are the Israelites.

precepts.label: Joshua 1:8
precepts.why:
What is supposed to be in your mouth? “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night.” The book of the law, the Bible, God's laws: that is what belongs in your mouth, the word of God and the laws of God.

But because we have been so wicked, God made our tongue to cleave to the roof of our mouth, and we sound like idiots trying to break this Bible down. When you are a Christian you do not know it, so you say strange things and strange doctrines, like the burning mountain is a meteorite. That is the stupidness that comes out when the law is not in the mouth.

Look at the black pastor today, preaching a sermon while getting a haircut: soft, sweet, moist, squishy, and a leader in the black church. That is the result when the law departs out of the mouth of those who are supposed to teach it.

So Psalms 137:6 is the curse on the tongue for forgetting Jerusalem, and Joshua 1:8 is what the tongue was made for: the law, spoken and meditated on day and night, so that we may observe to do all that is written therein.

thread.text: These six things doth the Lord hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him:

precepts.label: Proverbs 16:18
precepts.why:
The first thing on the list of what the Lord hates is “A proud look.” Proverbs 16 shows where that proud look ends: “Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.”

Whenever you see somebody fall off, just know there is some form of pride in that man or that woman: something they do not want to address, an inflated ego, disdain, a haughty look, a refusal to come back to God. You might not have seen it. They might have masked it as confidence in your eyes, but God saw it as pride.

Pride is not always loud and in your face. It can be subtle: not asking for help because you do not want to seem weak, holding grudges because you feel justified, saying I am good when you are not, shutting down and thinking you do not need anybody. Pride always points the finger at somebody else and never at yourself. So when you start feeling yourself too much, puffing your chest out, say, Oh no, I am not trying to fall; let me be humble, let me be loving.

Every kingdom has failed because of pride, even ours. “Woe to the crown of pride, to the drunkards of Ephraim”: the northern kingdom fell because of pride, separating from God to do their own thing, going back to the split under Rehoboam, who would not listen to the elders. Then the southern kingdom: “After this manner will I mar the pride of Judah, and the great pride of Jerusalem.” And the warning to us: “Hear ye, and give ear; be not proud: for the Lord hath spoken.”

So the proud look is first on God’s list because it is the start of the fall. God made your eyes, your body and the mind you think with; walking in pride is departing from your maker, and it ends in destruction.

thread.label: Proverbs 22:20-21
thread.text: Have not I written to thee excellent things in counsels and knowledge,

precepts.label: Romans 15:4
precepts.why:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning.” The excellent things God wrote in Proverbs 22:20, the counsels and knowledge that make us “know the certainty of the words of truth”, were written for us to learn.

And not only to learn: “that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” These excellent things are written for us to apply to our lives, so that we can be excellent and great in God’s eyes. Learn and apply, that is what Romans 15:4 is telling us.

Everything in this Bible is the excellent things of God, the truth he wants us to know. It is not to be used to get rich off of prosperity teaching, and it is not up for debate for us to decide what we should and should not do. It is not up for debate whether we want to be great or average. God gave us excellent things because he expects excellence out of us.

So we have to change our mindset and live up to the standards of God, not the standards the world has placed on black men and women and Hispanic men, to be comfortable with the crumbs society gives us. Those excellent things are what we have to apply, and it starts with a change in the mind.

precepts.label: 1 Samuel 2:3
precepts.why:
“Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.”

Actions are weighed when it comes to the Most High. That is why he gave us the excellent things of Proverbs 22:20: to learn them and apply them, because he wants actions behind those things. Not lip service, but actual action from all of us that he called.

Romans 15:4 says the scriptures were written for our learning; 1 Samuel 2:3 says what he does with that learning. He weighs what we do with it. Proud talk and arrogancy out of the mouth weigh nothing with him, because he is a God of knowledge and knows whether the words are backed by works.

That is the pride of thine heart: to talk big about the things of God and not live them. The one who has been given the excellent things has to put his actions where his mouth is, and keep arrogancy out of it.

precepts.label: Isaiah 45:15
precepts.why:
“Verily thou art a God that hidest thyself, O God of Israel, the Saviour.” He hides himself. That means he is not dealing with everybody. It is not like you just say, hey God, and he turns around. He answers and reveals himself to whom he wants to.

So for you to have even a little understanding of his excellent things, to learn them and apply them to your life, means something. He is the “God of Israel, the Saviour.” If God has revealed himself to you, that you are an Israelite, that you even have a mind to conceive his words and understand them, that means something to God. It means you are worthy enough for him to reveal his words to you, so that you get a chance to know what these excellent things are.

You can’t take that lightly. Far too many people in this world do, and use the Bible for material gain and to feel good on their terms. God doesn’t get down like that. He is a God that hides himself, so if he is letting you know what these words mean, you better take heed to him.

And that is where the humbling comes in. Romans 12:3 follows it: “not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.” If he is revealing himself to you when he does not deal with everybody, you better have some humbleness, because that is the King of kings, the omnipotent Most High God. We are Israelites and we have to keep God’s commandments, so don’t think too highly of yourself. Humble down.

thread.text: If a wise man contendeth with a foolish man, whether he rage or laugh, there is no rest.

precepts.label: Sirach 33:5
precepts.why:
“If a wise man contendeth with a foolish man”: if a wise man debates with a stupid man or woman. And “whether he rage or laugh”: whether that fool laughs at it or is angry at it, “there is no rest.” There is no conclusion. It is a circular argument; you argue the same thing over and over again and it goes nowhere.

Sirach shows why: “The heart of the foolish is like a cartwheel; and his thoughts are like a rolling axletree.” The fool is a circular idiot. His mind just goes in circles, nonstop. That is the Trinity man: three is one, one is three, they are all the same, the Father and the Son of one substance. Round and round, and you cannot win. They are dead set in it, their minds sealed as with a hot iron.

Show them that the Father has sons, the children of Israel, and they cannot understand it: no, they are all one. Stump them in a debate and they keep going: but what about this? It is ongoing. It is a cartwheel. They will not yield to reason. Even the German had some sense when he called insanity doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results.

So leave that negro alone. You are wasting your time. These are unreasonable people, and you have to let them go. The wise man who keeps contending with the fool gets no rest, because the fool's heart only rolls in circles of nonsense.

thread.label: Ecclesiastes 1:9
thread.text: The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be; and that which is done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 6:10
precepts.why:
“The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be”. What is “The thing that hath been”? Solomon names it: “That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it is man: neither may he contend with him that is mightier than he.” It is known that it is man. So the thing that is, is man.

Go back to Ecclesiastes 1:9 with that understanding. The thing that hath been is man, and it is that which shall be. “and that which is done is that which shall be done”: what man does on the earth, whether he keeps God's laws or doesn't keep God's laws, is what shall be done again. “and there is no new thing under the sun”: what happened in the past is what will happen again in these last days.

That is why the class goes back to Genesis. Cain would not bring the offering God required; sin lay at the door, and his desire was unto Satan, who ruled over him. His seed built the city Enoch: tents and cattle, buying and selling with unrighteous pricing; the harp and organ, and not holy music; Tubal-cain and every artificer in brass and iron, weapons; Lamech avenged seventy and sevenfold, wiping out a whole line. The sons of God took wives of all which they chose, the earth was filled with violence, and God destroyed it.

Think about the great cities today, like New York City: murder, wicked music, buying and selling, stealing, the wife looking over at the white woman or the Chinese woman. The same thing going on now is what was going on back then, because man is what he was.

thread.label: Ecclesiastes 8:9
thread.text: All this have I seen, and applied my heart unto every work that is done under the sun: there is a time wherein one man ruleth over another to his own hurt.

classes.title: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.label: Zechariah 1:15
precepts.why:
“there is a time wherein one man ruleth over another to his own hurt.” That is Esau. The way Esau treated us is going to be to his own detriment.

The Lord says it in Zechariah: “And I am very sore displeased with the heathen that are at ease: for I was but a little displeased, and they helped forward the affliction.” Yes, we sinned against our God. Yes, the Lord allowed us to go into the hands of our enemies. But they took it too far.

God was but a little displeased with Israel, and the heathen helped forward the affliction. You think Christ ain't see that? That is why Esau's rule over Jacob is to his own hurt: he went past what God allowed, and the Lord is sore displeased with him for it.

precepts.label: Isaiah 63:9
precepts.why:
“In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them”. In all of our affliction, through all of our slavery, the Lord saw all of it.

In all our affliction he was afflicted. So when he comes back, he is going to feel all of that pain and all of that suffering they did to the children of Israel, and he is going to wreak havoc on these nations.

“the angel of his presence saved them”. Salvation is not for the oppressors. Salvation is for those who have been afflicted. The man that ruled over another did it to his own hurt, because the one he afflicted is the one the Lord saves.

precepts.label: Psalms 119:85
precepts.why:
“The proud have digged pits for me, which are not after thy law.” The proud have digged pits for God's people.

They are not after God's laws. Look at it: how come you can abort in America? How come gay marriage is legalized? They don't keep God's laws and they don't uphold God's laws, but a lot of you coons out there follow behind this white man. They are not after God's commandments.

And who are the proud? Obadiah answers: it is Edom. The man that rules over another in Ecclesiastes 8 is the same proud one digging pits for Jacob, and his own pit is where he is headed.

precepts.label: Obadiah 1:1-3
precepts.why:
Who are the proud that digged the pits? “The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?”

And who is he speaking to? Verse 1: “The vision of Obadiah. Thus saith the Lord God concerning Edom”. Concerning Edom: Esau, your friendly neighborhood white man, your Europeans, and the Americans.

Edom's pride has deceived him into thinking none shall bring him down. That is the one man who rules over another, and Solomon says he does it “to his own hurt.”

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 27:26-29
precepts.why:
“Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that setteth a trap shall be taken therein.” The proud digged pits for us, and they will fall in them. They thought evil against us, but the Lord saw it for good. Jacob is going to win in the end.

“He that worketh mischief, it shall fall upon him, and he shall not know whence it cometh.” That is what they do: they work mischief and call it law. And he is not going to know where it came from, because his pride has deceived him.

“Mockery and reproach are from the proud”. That is all they do: they accuse us, falsely accuse us, and mock us. “but vengeance, as a lion, shall lie in wait for them.” That lion is the one in Jeremiah 4:7.

“They that rejoice at the fall of the righteous shall be taken in the snare; and anguish shall consume them before they die.” Remember when they said raze it, raze it to the ground? The Lord has not forgotten. They will be taken in the snare. It does not pay to be wicked, and it does not pay to follow after your oppressor, because in the end they are going to be destroyed.

precepts.label: Psalms 94:20
precepts.why:
He that worketh mischief: that is what they do. “Shall the throne of iniquity have fellowship with thee, which frameth mischief by a law?” They work mischief and then call it law.

Two men getting married, two women getting married: all of these laws. Think about what Trump has done since he came into office: all of the firing and all the DEI hires, all of this is against us. They frame mischief and call it law.

A throne of iniquity cannot have fellowship with God. The ruler that frames mischief by a law over another man is ruling to his own hurt, and the mischief he works shall fall upon him.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 4:7
precepts.why:
Sirach said vengeance, as a lion, shall lie in wait for the proud. Jeremiah shows the lion: “The lion is come up from his thicket, and the destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way; he is gone forth from his place to make thy land desolate; and thy cities shall be laid waste, without an inhabitant.”

The destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way, to make the land desolate, without an inhabitant.

And that is twofold. It is talking about Nebuchadnezzar, and it is talking about Christ. The lion that came up against the land in the days of Jeremiah is a picture of the Lion that is coming for the nations that ruled over Israel to their own hurt.

precepts.label: Isaiah 26:10-14
precepts.why:
“Let favour be shewed to the wicked, yet will he not learn righteousness”. If favour was shown to Esau, he still wouldn't change his wicked ways. It does not pay to be wicked.

“in the land of uprightness will he deal unjustly, and will not behold the majesty of the Lord.” Where is the land of uprightness? The land of Israel. And what did he do there? He stole it. He will not behold the majesty of the Lord: he changes his image to a white man with stringy blonde hair and blue eyes.

“Lord, when thy hand is lifted up, they will not see: but they shall see, and be ashamed for their envy at the people”. The people are God's chosen people, the ones the heathen envy in 2 Esdras 2:28. “yea, the fire of thine enemies shall devour them. Lord, thou wilt ordain peace for us”, like we read earlier in Ephesians 2: he is going to ordain peace for us and destruction for our enemies.

“O Lord our God, other lords beside thee have had dominion over us”: like the so-called white man, like the Babylonians, like the Assyrians. “but by thee only will we make mention of thy name. They are dead, they shall not live; they are deceased, they shall not rise: therefore hast thou visited and destroyed them, and made all their memory to perish.” All of our enemies, all of these other lords that had rule over us, are dead. That is the hurt of the man that ruled over another.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 2:28

The heathen shall envy the Israelites. But they shall be able to do nothing. They can't stop it, because they ain't going to be in rulership any more. They are not going to have ownership any more.

That is the end of the man who ruleth over another to his own hurt: the time of his rule runs out, and all his envy cannot stop what the Lord has spoken for Israel.

thread.label: Isaiah 9:6-7
thread.text: For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.

classes.title: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.label: John 14:8-9
precepts.why:
Isaiah calls the son that is given “The everlasting Father.” Most Christians, and even some Israelites, cannot explain that, because they have not figured out that the everlasting Father in the Old Testament was Christ. They say we always spoke to the Father. No, you did not speak to the Father; you spoke to Christ. That is why he is called the everlasting Father. John 14 is a precept for it.

“Philip saith unto him, Lord, shew us the Father, and it sufficeth us.” See Christ’s response: “Jesus saith unto him, Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip? he that hath seen me hath seen the Father; and how sayest thou then, Shew us the Father?”

Yes, Christ looks like his Father. But what is he actually telling Philip? I created you. I am your Father, your everlasting Father. You were brought forth through me.

Remember, Christ is the only begotten of the Father. That means the Father created only Christ, and then told Christ to create everything else. So when Isaiah names the child born unto us “The mighty God, The everlasting Father”, it is because everything that exists was brought forth through him. That is why Philip, who had been with him so long, should have known him.

precepts.label: John 1:1-3
precepts.why:
In case anyone is still confused about why Christ is called “The everlasting Father”, John 1 settles it. We have to shake the Christian thoughts.

“In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” Christ was in the beginning with God, and he was God. “The same was in the beginning with God.” God is a plural there.

Then the part that matters: “All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.” All things were made by Christ, and without Christ was not any thing made that was made. The Father only begat Christ, and through Christ everything else was created.

That is why he said to Philip, “Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip?” I created all of this. That is too heavy for a Negro, because you have Baptist on your mind and Catholic in your head. It was hard for us in the beginning too, but the Most High has shown us. Let it marinate.

So the child born and the son given in Isaiah 9:6, with the government upon his shoulder, is the same one who made all things: the Word, the mighty God, the everlasting Father.

precepts.label: Matthew 13:31-32
precepts.why:
“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.” Christ explains that increase in Matthew 13: “The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field: Which indeed is the least of all seeds.” If you grew up in the city you may not know what a mustard seed looks like; it is one of the smallest of all seeds.

“but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs.” When it is grown: that is the increase of his government. It starts small. What we have here is small. We may think we have a lot, but this is nothing yet; we are still at the mustard seed stage.

And the kingdom of heaven is a government, not a church group. That is why it behooves us to learn God’s laws, commandments and statutes: to set up a government you need everything that makes a community, and God’s laws are going to filter everything for us. Right now we think small. God says think bigger. A house? Bigger. Property? Bigger. The world is ours, and for the world to be ours we have to be able to set all of that up.

Think how the Most High uses something as small as the human mind. As a man thinketh, so is he. Everything you lay your eyes on, every object and invention, was a thought first. We shortchange ourselves with doubt, but that is not what God made. Untapped greatness is waiting to bud; remove the doubt and the fear and let the Lord work on that head.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 7:12-21
precepts.why:
The mustard seed government is small now, and we think small. Compare what God did for Solomon with where we are today.

“I learned diligently, and do communicate her liberally: I do not hide her riches.” Solomon learned wisdom and gave it out freely, and that is what we are doing today: we don’t hide the riches of the wisdom of God. “For she is a treasure unto men that never faileth: which they that use become the friends of God, being commended for the gifts that come from learning.” If we use this wisdom we become the friends of God. And it comes from learning, not once but daily; that is what the classes every day are about.

“For he hath given me certain knowledge of the things that are, namely, to know how the world was made, and the operation of the elements.” You might say you know how the world was made. You don’t: what elements make the air, what elements were made for the sun? Solomon understood that. He knew “The beginning, ending, and midst of the times”, from Adam to the second coming of Christ. He knew “the alterations of the turning of the sun, and the change of seasons”, “The circuits of years, and the positions of stars.”

“The natures of living creatures”: Esau puts cameras on animals, even in their butts, to learn how they defecate, trying to get on Solomon’s level with all that freakiness. Solomon knew “the furies of wild beasts”, “the violence of winds”, the tornadoes and storms, “the reasonings of men”, “the diversities of plants and the virtues of roots”, which herb is for what, and “all such things as are either secret or manifest, them I know.”

We are not even on Solomon’s level yet. We need the Lord to open our minds up to get there, and when he does we will be on that level and greater. That is what the mustard seed is about: we start small and it grows. This is the beginning of that government.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 23:5-6
precepts.why:
Isaiah says the government shall be upon his shoulder, “upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice.” Jeremiah says the same: “Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch.” That righteous Branch is Christ.

“and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.” See what he is going to do: execute judgment and justice in the earth. The nations don’t want that. Some of us in here may not want that either: I don’t want no justice and judgment, hell no. Yes, it is coming anyway.

“In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely: and this is his name whereby he shall be called, THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS.”

So the throne of David in Isaiah 9 is the reign of this King, the Branch raised unto David. The increase of his government is a kingdom of judgment and justice, of law and order, and in his days Judah is saved and Israel dwells safely. That is why we learn God’s laws now: it is the government we are going to live under.

thread.label: Isaiah 9:16
thread.text: For the leaders of this people cause them to err; and they that are led of them are destroyed.

classes.title: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

precepts.label: Hosea 8:3-4
precepts.why:
“For the leaders of this people cause them to err; and they that are led of them are destroyed.” Who are the leaders in the Black community today? Your Black leaders have you fighting for Palestinians and fighting all kinds of stupid battles. And you Black Christians that are led of them are destroyed. Our people are so destroyed they don't even know it: destroyed with a warm fuzzy feeling every Sunday. The pastors are the new taskmasters. They get sent out by Esau, they learned the doctrines from Esau, and they bring it into your community, pulling up in the Benz while you walk to church in the cold and give him your last.

Hosea shows how it came to this. “Israel hath cast off the thing that is good: the enemy shall pursue him.” What is good? The laws of God, this Bible. Israel cast them off, and because of that the enemy pursues him.

“They have set up kings, but not by me: they have made princes, and I knew it not.” You set up leaders, brothers and sisters, but it isn't of the Lord. “Of their silver and their gold have they made them idols, that they may be cut off.” You make these men, these so-called leaders, your idols. You follow them wholeheartedly. Pastor says he needs an extra thousand dollars and you say, Pastor, I'mma work it out, I'mma get you your money. That's cold pimping.

And look at the fruit: a grandmother in Jamal Bryant's church sowing her twelve hundred dollars and being embarrassed because it was not enough; Eddie Long on the throne while the white man holds the mic and tells him he is no longer a commoner. These are your leaders that cause you to err.

“That they may be cut off.” And now we are cut off. That is what comes of casting off the law of God and setting up kings the Lord never chose.

precepts.label: Proverbs 3:31
precepts.why:
“Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways.” Put the oppressors on the screen: Pope Nicholas V and Pope Alexander VI. In 1452 Pope Nicholas V issued Dum Diversas, authorizing King Alfonso V of Portugal to fight, subjugate and conquer the Saracens and pagans in African territory. Those were good Christians.

Think about it. Without those two devils, those two Christians, there would be no such thing as an African-American, a Jamaican, a Haitian, a Puerto Rican. We are named after whatever landmass we were scattered to, and we are the result of those men. Christians did this to us. And now we revel in it, reverence them, and follow their laws and their ways of life.

The scripture says choose none of his ways. But tomorrow at 11 o'clock Sunday morning, where will all our people be? Not listening to the truth. They will be in church getting a good dose of the doctrine of the man that enslaved them, that turned them into African-Americans and Jamaicans and Haitians. They can't wait to go learn about a good Jesus.

That is the leaders of Isaiah 9:16 causing our people to err. Look at the results of being taught Christianity: a man on television saying he is a Christian first and that black is a construct, when the white man put us in chains and did not do that to his own people; a girl who let a boy call her the N-word and call him master; our people turning up on each other and showing teeth to everybody else. That is what comes of envying the oppressor and choosing his ways.

precepts.label: Mark 8:36-37
precepts.why:
Terence Crawford said there was not a number that could get him back in that ring, and then said for 100 million dollars you can have my soul. That nigger was dead serious; look at his eyes. That is a dangerous man: a man who would sell out his mama and his children and do anything for money. That is the result of 400 years with Esau, and he just said out loud what the majority of Black celebrities, rappers and singers think.

“For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?” Esau gives you whatever you want: all the riches, all the connections, all the power, wealth you can't run from. But in order to get it, you lose your own soul.

“Or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?” What do these celebrities give in exchange for their souls? Their booty. They give it up, and Amalek takes it. Your Jay-Zs and 50 Cents, your Mariah Careys and Whitneys: they have to give in order to receive.

What are you going to stand for if everything is about money? You have no dignity and no morals. These are the results of the leaders of this people causing them to err, and of Black Christians led by them being destroyed. There are no laws with them, because they were taught the laws are done away with.

thread.label: Isaiah 14:3-4
thread.text: And it shall come to pass in the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve,

precepts.label: Revelation 18:10
precepts.why:
“That thou shalt take up this proverb against the king of Babylon, and say, How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!” In the day the Lord gives us rest from our sorrow, our fear and the hard bondage we were made to serve in, we are going to be speaking against America. The king of Babylon here is America, and this is how we know Lucifer is not an angel: Lucifer is called the king of Babylon, the oppressor, the golden city. In Revelation it is mystery Babylon the great, and Revelation 18 explains that city.

“Standing afar off for the fear of her torment, saying, Alas, alas, that great city Babylon, that mighty city! for in one hour is thy judgment come.” Remember what we read in Isaiah 14: the king of Babylon. Here it is that great city Babylon, that mighty city, and her judgment comes in one hour.

So Lucifer is a city, a country, rulers, a government. “The Lord hath broken the staff of the wicked, and the sceptre of the rulers.” It is not talking about a fallen angel; it is talking about America, the king of Babylon, whose ceasing Israel will proclaim when the Lord gives us rest from the hard bondage.

precepts.label: Revelation 18:17
precepts.why:
Isaiah calls the king of Babylon “the golden city”: “How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!” Why does it say golden city? Revelation 18 explains it: “For in one hour so great riches is come to nought.”

So great riches: that is the golden city. It is called golden because America is rich. Lucifer is talking about America. And all those riches come to nothing in one hour, the same hour of judgment in verse 10, when they stand afar off crying, “Alas, alas, that great city Babylon, that mighty city!”

The golden city ceasing in Isaiah is the great riches coming to nought in Revelation. It is not an angel that falls; it is a rich nation, a government, the oppressor that made us serve in hard bondage, and in the day the Lord gives us rest, we will take up this proverb against it.

precepts.label: Lamentations 2:1
precepts.why:
“How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground.” Who is Lucifer, and what heaven did he fall from? When it says fall from heaven, it is not talking about literal heaven. In the scriptures there are the heavens where the Lord is, which is paradise; there is heaven that is the sky and space; and there are heavens that are a place of authority. Lamentations shows that last one.

“How hath the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger, and cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel.” The beauty of Israel was cast down from heaven to the earth. That means we were brought down low: brought into captivity, no longer on top, no longer ruling. It is a good analogy showing that heaven also goes into rulership.

So Lucifer falling from heaven is a ruler falling from his place of authority, not an angel falling out of the sky. Read on in Isaiah 14 and he is named: Israel will “take up this proverb against the king of Babylon, and say, How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!” Lucifer is the king of Babylon, the oppressor, the golden city, because America is rich. And “They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble, that did shake kingdoms”: Lucifer is a man, the man of sin, the fourth beast, the white man.

The same Lord who cast Israel down from heaven to the earth will cut this ruler down to the ground. It is a future prophecy of America being destroyed.

thread.label: Isaiah 14:21
thread.text: Prepare slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers; that they do not rise, nor possess the land, nor fill the face of the world with cities.

precepts.label: Isaiah 54:16
precepts.why:
“Prepare slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers; that they do not rise, nor possess the land, nor fill the face of the world with cities.” “For I will rise up against them, saith the Lord of hosts, and cut off from Babylon the name, and remnant, and son, and nephew.” To cut them off means he is going to kill all of them. When Esau falls, Esau will never rise back again.

Some think Esau will never fall. You forgot what happened to the Babylonians, the Persians and Medes, the Greeks, Rome and Egypt, all superpowers in their time. America has bombs, lasers, all types of weapons, the most powerful military on the planet. But the Most High is more powerful than America.

Isaiah shows how he does it: “Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire, and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work; and I have created the waster to destroy.” The smith today is what you call the scientist who makes weapons. Back then they were called smiths; they bring forth the instrument for the work. And the waster is nuclear power. God let them create the waster, and it is made to destroy.

Job shows it striking the wicked: “He shall flee from the iron weapon, and the bow of steel shall strike him through.” The iron weapon is the missile.

So the slaughter prepared for Esau’s children is by the very weapons God allowed their own smiths to make. Nobody is innocent, and whatever evil was done to the Israelites, no one is getting away with it.

thread.label: Isaiah 19:1
thread.text: The burden of Egypt. Behold, the Lord rideth upon a swift cloud, and shall come into Egypt: and the idols of Egypt shall be moved at his presence, and the heart of Egypt shall melt in the midst of it.

precepts.label: Revelation 11:8
precepts.why:
“The burden of Egypt. Behold, the Lord rideth upon a swift cloud, and shall come into Egypt: and the idols of Egypt shall be moved at his presence.” The commentaries say this is about ancient times, but verse 1 lets you know it is future: the Lord coming into Egypt has not happened yet. So how do we know who this Egypt is?

Revelation tells us: “And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.” The dead bodies are the Israelites, not literally dead but spiritually dead. The great city is Babylon the great, the United States of America. “which spiritually”: that is the key.

It is called Sodom because of the same-sex marriages, the transgenderism and all that filth in this country. It is not the real Sodom but a spiritual Sodom. And it is called Egypt: America knows its foundation is ancient Egypt. Look at the dollar bill: the pyramid, the all-seeing eye of Horus, 1776 at the bottom, Novus Ordo Seclorum, the New World Order, and the obelisk in Washington DC. America is aware that this is a spiritual Egypt; only the black and Latin Christians have not figured it out, and so they read the scriptures desperately confused.

“where also our Lord was crucified.” Christ was crucified in Jerusalem, but this is a spiritual crucifixion: they have crucified Christ’s image here and crucified his teachings here.

So Isaiah 19 is spiritual Egypt: “And I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: and they shall fight every one against his brother, and every one against his neighbour; city against city, and kingdom against kingdom.” Americans against Americans, a house divided: Democrats against Republicans, red cities against blue cities, white man against white man. There will be a civil war in this country.

thread.label: Isaiah 19:18-20
thread.text: In that day shall five cities in the land of Egypt speak the language of Canaan, and swear to the Lord of hosts; one shall be called, The city of destruction.

precepts.label: Joel 2:15-20
precepts.why:
Isaiah says “they shall cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors.” What will the oppressors be doing? The same thing 2 Esdras 16, Revelation 12:17, Matthew 10 and Matthew 24 say: Jacob's trouble. Joel shows the crying.

“Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly: Gather the people, sanctify the congregation, assemble the elders, gather the children, and those that suck the breasts.” This is going to be a major fast, because there will be so much devastation to our people. “Let the bridegroom go forth of his chamber, and the bride out of her closet”: when this fast goes out, we are not doing weddings or planning weddings. Weddings are finished. We have to pray to the Lord because our people are dying.

“Let the priests, the ministers of the Lord, weep between the porch and the altar, and let them say, Spare thy people, O Lord.” That is the cry of Isaiah 19, crying bitterly because there is going to be death. “And give not thine heritage to reproach, that the heathen should rule over them: wherefore should they say among the people, Where is their God?”

“Then will the Lord be jealous for his land, and pity his people.” He answers, “I will send you corn, and wine, and oil” and “I will no more make you a reproach among the heathen: But I will remove far off from you the northern army.” That is the great multitude after us in 2 Esdras 16. He will “drive him into a land barren and desolate, with his face toward the east sea, and his hinder part toward the utmost sea.” The east sea is the Dead Sea and the utmost sea is the Mediterranean: the land of Israel between them, what they call the Middle East. The Lord is going to cause things to pop off there.

“And his stink shall come up, and his ill savour shall come up, because he hath done great things.” The Lord is going to destroy them over there: tribulation, World War III, Armageddon. It is all laid out for us. Yes, you are dying, but you are not dead; the Lord takes the northern army down, and then he sends us “a saviour, and a great one”, Christ, to deliver us.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 49:20-22
precepts.why:
Joel says the Lord will remove the northern army far off and drive it into the land between the Dead Sea and the Mediterranean. Jeremiah shows what happens there.

“Therefore hear the counsel of the Lord, that he hath taken against Edom; and his purposes, that he hath purposed against the inhabitants of Teman.” Teman is still Edom. “Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out”: the least of the flock is these Israelis, the fake Israelis. That whole area on the map is where it is all going to go down. “Surely he shall make their habitations desolate with them.”

“The earth is moved at the noise of their fall, at the cry the noise thereof was heard in the Red sea.” The ships in the Red Sea are going to hear about this fall.

“Behold, he shall come up and fly as the eagle, and spread his wings over Bozrah.” Bozrah is Jordan, that area on the map. America is going to come to Israel's rescue, so they think. “And at that day shall the heart of the mighty men of Edom be as the heart of a woman in her pangs.” They are going to be afraid, because they don't realize it's a trap: NATO turns against them, and everybody is against America and Israel.

That is how the Lord takes the northern army down over there, while he tells us, don't worry, you are dying but you are not dead. Jacob's trouble is great, “but he shall be saved out of it.”

thread.label: Isaiah 21:1-17
thread.text: The burden of the desert of the sea. As whirlwinds in the south pass through; so it cometh from the desert, from a terrible land.

classes.title: Final Call: Message to the Black Man

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 15:28-45
precepts.why:
Isaiah sees “the burden of the desert of the sea”: “the treacherous dealer dealeth treacherously, and the spoiler spoileth.” That is America, which invites you to a peace talk and then bombs your country, as it did Iran, and now tells every nation to take the deal: only white folks can have nuclear weapons, no weapons for you brown people. “Go up, O Elam: besiege, O Media”: Iran, Pakistan, India, that whole section. Right now they are in a sighing period, bases destroyed and generals killed by drones, building up their arsenal and waiting. Then the burden upon Arabia, the sons of Ishmael, and “all the glory of Kedar shall fail.” Ezra shows how it all comes together.

“Behold an horrible vision, and the appearance thereof from the east: Where the nations of the dragons of Arabia shall come out with many chariots.” Turkey, which is part of NATO, is making a defense pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, a NATO of the Arab nations, because Erdogan hates the Israelis so much. When Israel bombed Qatar, the Muslim world called an emergency summit, and Saudi Arabia called for revenge. “Also the Carmanians raging in wrath shall go forth as the wild boars of the wood, and with great power shall they come, and join battle with them, and shall waste a portion of the land of the Assyrians.” The Carmanians are Iran, joining the Arabs, and the land of the Assyrians here is the Israelis.

“And then shall the dragons have the upper hand, remembering their nature.” Right now the Arabs are kissing America's butt, but they will remember their nature. Genesis 16 gives it: Ishmael “will be a wild man; his hand will be against every man, and every man’s hand against him; and he shall dwell in the presence of all his brethren.” Wild enough to run into a crowded room with C4 strapped to his chest for 72 virgins. His hand against every man means you have no friends among them: they are true nationalists, and all twelve princes dwell together through that region.

It is only Black people that are not nationalists. We love everybody, we have to be friends with everybody, and meanwhile we are put to death left and right. Stop being stupid, men. A nationalist loves his nation and his people; that is the greatest commandment, love God and love your brother. Every nation loves its own. Christ was a nationalist: I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel. And now Ibrahim Traoré is uniting Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso, the most docile nations; the spirit of life is coming into them through the brothers teaching and preaching in Africa.

“And if they shall turn themselves, conspiring together in great power to persecute them, Then these shall be troubled” … “and shall flee. And from the land of the Assyrians shall the enemy besiege them, and consume some of them.” All the Arab nations conspiring together against the Israelis, just as we saw in the clip.

“Behold clouds from the east and from the north unto the south” … “full of wrath and storm.” The east is Asia, China and North Korea; the north is Russia, Turkey and Europe; the south is the Arabs and Africa; the clouds are their ships. “They shall smite down a great multitude of stars upon the earth, even their own star”: missiles, like the ones the Iron Dome shoots down. “And blood shall be from the sword unto the belly, And dung of men unto the camel’s hough.” Then “great storms from the south, and from the north, and another part from the west”: the west is America and Canada.

Then “they shall pour out over every high and eminent place an horrible star.” That is different from the stars before: the horrible star is the ICBM. With it, “Fire, and hail, and flying swords”, the conventional missiles. “And they shall go stedfastly unto Babylon, and make her afraid” … “then shall the dust and smoke go up unto the heaven, and all they that be about her shall bewail her”, like the kings of the earth in Revelation 18 standing afar off, crying that in one hour her judgment is come. Ezra 15:60 even shows them returning to Babylon that was destroyed: the air force and navy still fighting from a base that is gone.

That is what Isaiah's watchman saw: “Babylon is fallen, is fallen; and all the graven images of her gods he hath broken unto the ground.” Fallen twice, because the Israelis over there fall too. Cesare Borgia, Santa Claus, the Thanksgiving turkey, the Easter bunny, the Greek statues everywhere: all of it finished. It is Bible prophecy unfolding before our eyes, and while it happens, get yourselves together, brothers and sisters.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 13:9-17
precepts.why:
Every kingdom on earth has failed because of pride, even ours. Isaiah says “Woe to the crown of pride, to the drunkards of Ephraim”: the northern kingdom fell because of pride. They separated from God, went to the north and said, we are doing our own thing. It goes back to the split between Rehoboam and Jeroboam. Rehoboam could have listened to the elders who were already there to run the nation correctly, but he mocked the leadership above him and dealt with his buddies, and we are in the condition we are in today because of that pride.

The northern kingdom was the first to fall, but the southern kingdom was not exempt. “Thus saith the Lord, After this manner will I mar the pride of Judah, and the great pride of Jerusalem.” Judah looked at what their brother was doing and followed right after their treacherous sister Israel. The great pride of Jerusalem takes in Benjamin and Levi too: all of the southern kingdom was full of pride in God's eyes.

“This evil people, which refuse to hear my words, which walk in the imagination of their heart, and walk after other gods, to serve them, and to worship them, shall even be as this girdle, which is good for nothing.” When pride comes, you separate yourself from your maker, as Sirach 10 says, and walk after your own heart. When you are full of pride you are good for nothing in God's eyes.

Then the judgment for it: “And I will dash them one against another, even the fathers and the sons together, saith the Lord: I will not pity, nor spare, nor have mercy, but destroy them.” Pride destroyed the kingdom, and it destroys every kingdom.

“Hear ye, and give ear; be not proud: for the Lord hath spoken.” You better listen up, Israel, and not separate yourself from him. He is our creator and he controls all of this, so you better humble yourself and do as he tells you. This could be over right now if all of us said, Lord, I'm done with pride, I humble myself, what do you want me to do? And Christ would crack the sky.

But not on the surface, saying forgive me and then waiting till you get out of here. You are not fooling God. That is why we are still here as a people: even those of us that repented are not ready to go back to the kingdom yet. And pride is not always loud. It can be subtle, shutting down, thinking you can do it on your own, and Satan still has you there.
