thread.text: Behold, the eyes of the Lord God are upon the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from off the face of the earth; saving that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob, saith the Lord.

classes.title: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.label: Revelation 11:8
precepts.why:
Amos says, “Behold, the eyes of the Lord God are upon the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from off the face of the earth”. In Amos he calls us, wicked Israel, the sinful kingdom. But if you choose to use the sinful kingdom for America, as brothers do, here is the precept: “And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.”

The great city is Babylon the great. “Spiritually” is the key word to highlight: it is called Sodom and Egypt, a spiritual Sodom and a spiritual Egypt.

“Where also our Lord was crucified.” Christ was crucified in Jerusalem, so what is it saying? America is a spiritual Jerusalem. Just as they hated Christ in the real Jerusalem, they hate the true Christ and his teachings here as well.

Either way the order of Amos stands. The sinful kingdom is destroyed, “saving that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob”: not all the Israelites are wiped out. We are sifted among all nations, yet the least of us is not lost. The sinners who say the evil shall not overtake them, just like Christianity saying we good in White Jesus name, die by the sword. And then, “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen”, the twelve tribes that were split into two kingdoms, “and I will build it as in the days of old”. He is already letting us know his plan, because we are predestined, foreknown from before the foundation of the earth.

thread.label: Amos 9:11
thread.text: In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old:

classes.title: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.label: Micah 5:3
precepts.why:
Amos says, “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old.” Why does it have to be raised up? Because we fell.

Micah shows the order of it: “Therefore will he give them up, until the time that she which travaileth hath brought forth.” God gave Israel up until the woman in travail, Israel, brought forth. “then the remnant of his brethren shall return unto the children of Israel.” Then the remnant of Christ's brethren returns to the children of Israel.

That is the tabernacle of David being raised. We were given up and we fell, and now he is raising us up as in the days of old. We are coming back to who we are.

precepts.label: Hosea 3:4-5
precepts.why:
Amos says the tabernacle of David is fallen. Hosea tells how long it lies fallen: “For the children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod, and without teraphim.” Teraphim are the little images we made of family members. Many days with none of it: no king, no prince, no priesthood.

“Afterward shall the children of Israel return, and seek the Lord their God, and David their king; and shall fear the Lord and his goodness in the latter days.”

So in these latter days, David is going to be here. Who he is, we don't know. But the children of Israel who have gone so long without a king will return and seek the Lord their God and David their king, and that is the tabernacle of David raised up and built as in the days of old.

precepts.label: Psalms 80:1-3
precepts.why:
Amos says, “I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old.” Asaph cries out for that raising: “Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, thou that leadest Joseph like a flock; thou that dwellest between the cherubims, shine forth.” The Shepherd of Israel is Christ.

“Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh stir up thy strength, and come and save us.” The tribes cry for him to stir up his strength and save them.

“Turn us again, O God, and cause thy face to shine; and we shall be saved.” Turn us again to your laws; turn us again to our identity, our nationality, and we shall be saved.

That is how the fallen tabernacle of David is rebuilt: the Shepherd of Israel turns the tribes back to his law and back to who they are, and closes up the breaches as in the days of old.

thread.label: Obadiah 1:1-4
thread.text: The vision of Obadiah. Thus saith the Lord God concerning Edom; We have heard a rumour from the Lord, and an ambassador is sent among the heathen, Arise ye, and let us rise up against her in battle.

precepts.label: Luke 4:5-7
precepts.why:
Obadiah speaks “concerning Edom”: the white man, the Caucasian, by his biblical name. “Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars”. They were so proud that they went to the moon and claimed it for their own, something they did not even create. They do not let other nations plant a flag there; they said, the Eagle has landed. And now one of their government says, we own the moon, why not Greenland? That is pride.

There is a reason behind it, and Luke shows it: “the devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it. If thou therefore wilt worship me, all shall be thine.”

This Edomite is prideful because he has the spiritual power of Satan rolling with him. That is who gave him the power to go to the moon and to make these weapons to destroy all of mankind. No brown nation on the earth came up with the invention to destroy everybody; that belongs solely to the white man, because Satan is behind him. That is who he made a covenant with, not the God of the Bible.

So when you see In God we trust on the money, know he is not talking about anybody in this Bible. The Psalm proves it: “The wicked, through the pride of his countenance, will not seek after God: God is not in all his thoughts.” “The wicked in his pride doth persecute the poor”, and you judge whether a man is prideful or humble by how he treats the lowly: the blacks, Hispanics and Native Indians, who have no army. Out of all the kingdoms, Assyrian, Babylonian, Persian, Greek, Roman, none has been more prideful than Esau.

But the kingdoms Satan gives are not the Lord's, and Obadiah answers the pride: “thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord.” From the moment they said the Eagle has landed, they have been going down, because that is when the Israelites started hitting the streets with the word of God. The more we are gathered together, the more Esau comes down.

precepts.label: Sirach 12:10
precepts.why:
They tell you plainly they are the evil seed, and you can believe them if you want to, but they ain't fooling us. God said: “Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.” Never trust our enemies.

Then Micah shows the enemy at work: “Woe to them that devise iniquity, and work evil upon their beds!” That is Esau. In his sleep he is thinking, when I wake up, what type of evil am I going to do? “when the morning is light, they practise it”: he gets up and practises the same evil he was thinking of the night before, “because it is in the power of their hand.”

Picture it: we are going to steal the oil in Nigeria; let's say we are going in to defend the Christians. Nigeria is a black country, and if white men go in, they will be called racist. So find me a dumb black woman, the biggest hoe, one with millions of followers that dumb black people will believe, like Nicki Minaj, and put her up front. That is devising iniquity on the bed and practising it in the morning.

His wickedness rusts through everything like iron rusts. So never trust him when he says he is defending you, and never trust the peace he talks about.

precepts.label: Job 20:19
precepts.why:
Micah says, “And they covet fields, and take them by violence; and houses, and take them away: so they oppress a man and his house, even a man and his heritage.” They covet the oil in Nigeria and Venezuela, the diamonds and copper in all the African countries, and take them by violence. America was built by violence: this is stolen land, and millions of indigenous people died for it. After they killed, murdered and raped, they built churches and said, God so loved the world.

Job describes the same man: “Because he hath oppressed and hath forsaken the poor; because he hath violently taken away an house which he builded not”. Esau has oppressed, and we are the poor.

He violently took away houses he did not build. In the South, in Georgia, they drove whole black communities out of places like Lake Lanier and Forsyth and took the houses and businesses they never worked for, and they are still finding ways to take land that has been in black families for a century. When Esau came into Africa, King Leopold killed millions of our people, and the beauty of Europe was paid for with that. It is still happening: the wars in Sudan and the Congo, the minerals in the iPhone in your hand. He throws the rock and hides his hand, then says, black people killing black people. But black people don't make the weapons.

The dumb Christian says it was a long time ago. But every September 11 they want a moment of silence. It is not a long time ago; he is still violently taking away houses he builded not.

thread.label: Micah 2:10
thread.text: Arise ye, and depart; for this is not your rest: because it is polluted, it shall destroy you, even with a sore destruction.

precepts.label: Isaiah 30:12-13
precepts.why:
Micah says, “Arise ye, and depart; for this is not your rest: because it is polluted, it shall destroy you, even with a sore destruction.” America, Babylon the great, all the lands we have been enslaved and colonised in, are not our rest. Isaiah shows why staying in them destroys us: “Wherefore thus saith the Holy One of Israel, Because ye despise this word, and trust in oppression and perverseness, and stay thereon”.

We despise God's word and trust in oppression. It was a sin for us to trust in this oppression and to stay and believe in it. “Therefore this iniquity shall be to you as a breach ready to fall, swelling out in a high wall, whose breaking cometh suddenly at an instant.” There is no comfort and no protective covering in this society, in assimilating into America, Babylon the great. Our brothers and sisters that love this society and this world, it is our downfall as a people.

That is the pollution Micah speaks of. When you forget where you come from and get comfortable in the land of your captivity, it destroys you, because you begin to take on the attributes of your oppressor. That is not for us. We are God's children, and trying to make the oppressor's ways work for us always backfires. The white man has had the sword and the power to rule the world, but God will not let his children follow after him like the rest of the world and prosper.

So the wall breaks suddenly. In every place we have been, oppression, death and destruction follow behind us, and there is no peace there. Look at the families of Nolan Wales, of Kendrick Johnson, of the young woman found hanging from a tree in Mississippi: they never have rest again. And look at how we think as a people on social media and in all these podcasts: from the aged man and aged woman down to the children, we are in a sore destruction, because we have gotten comfortable in our captivity, “forgotten their restingplace”, and do not even want to go back to our homeland.

thread.label: Habakkuk 2:1-12
thread.text: I will stand upon my watch, and set me upon the tower, and will watch to see what he will say unto me, and what I shall answer when I am reproved.

precepts.label: Isaiah 30:8
precepts.why:
Habakkuk was in the Babylonian captivity, around 606 BC. The princes and the king were taken away, and Habakkuk was left because he was a poor prophet, so he stood on his tower complaining about what ancient Babylon did to us under Nebuchadnezzar. The Lord answered, “Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables”. Isaiah explains the tables for new people: “Now go, write it before them in a table, and note it in a book, that it may be for the time to come for ever and ever”.

The table is the book, and the book is what we call the Bible today. The vision was not only for Habakkuk's day; it was noted in a book “for the time to come”, because “the vision is yet for an appointed time”.

Sometimes you read prophecy and want it to happen in your lifetime, but God says it is for a later date: though it tarry, wait for it. It was written down in the book so that when the end came it would speak and not lie. We are in that time period now, and the vision is plain on the tables for whoever will read it.

precepts.label: Amos 8:11-12
precepts.why:
The vision is written plain “that he may run that readeth it.” Amos explains the running: “Behold, the days come, saith the Lord God, that I will send a famine in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the Lord”.

There would be a famine of the word of the Lord. “And they shall wander from sea to sea, and from the north even to the east, they shall run to and fro to seek the word of the Lord, and shall not find it.” People would travel from sea to sea, running to and fro, looking for the word and not finding it.

That is what happened after Christ and the disciples died: there was no truth being taught in the earth, nowhere. By the time of Constantine, around 325 AD, you had the churches, and there was no truth there; they were worshiping idols. Some of the Moors were Islamic, and some were black Jews following the Talmud and the Cabala. When white folks rose up it went crazy, into idolatry like you never saw: the church fathers making doctrine, and Tertullian, the devil that created the Trinity.

And they were traveling. The crusades went here and there trying to get the cup Christ drank from and to find the cross, trying to get some kind of glimpse of understanding. They ran to and fro, just as Amos said, because the word written plain in the book had nobody left to teach it.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 7:28-30
precepts.why:
Amos says they would run to and fro to seek the word of the Lord and not find it. Ezra gives the precept that explains why: “For my son Jesus shall be revealed with those that be with him, and they that remain shall rejoice within four hundred years.” Those with him were the apostles, the followers, the disciples. From Ezra's time to the time of Christ was four hundred years.

“After these years shall my son Christ die, and all men that have life.” Christ was crucified, and all the apostles and all the disciples that followed him either died or were murdered and crucified by Rome. All the men and women that had understanding were dead.

“And the world shall be turned into the old silence seven days, like as in the former judgments: so that no man shall remain.” So that no man that has truth shall remain. From the time after Christ and the disciples died, there was no truth being taught anywhere in the earth. There were no Israelites saying, we are the Israelites and we have to keep the commandments. Instead you had the church fathers, the damn devils, making doctrine, and Tertullian creating the Trinity.

That silence is the famine of hearing the words of the Lord. The world ran to and fro in it for centuries, and that is why the vision had to wait for its appointed time: at the end it shall speak, and not lie.

precepts.label: Habakkuk 1:6
precepts.why:
Habakkuk says, “Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him”. Who is he talking about? Go back to chapter 1: “For, lo, I raise up the Chaldeans, that bitter and hasty nation, which shall march through the breadth of the land, to possess the dwellingplaces that are not theirs.”

Did not America do that? The white man came throughout this land and took all the dwelling places that were not his. And the so-called Israelis are doing the same thing over there today.

Though Habakkuk prophesied in the days of Babylon, the vision was for the appointed time at the end, and we are in that time now. So the proud man of chapter 2 is the man raised up in the last days. “He transgresseth by wine”: philosophies and lies. “He is a proud man”, like Edom in Obadiah. He “neither keepeth at home”: America is in everybody's country, with over 850 bases worldwide. He “enlargeth his desire as hell”: when he takes your land he brings democracy and Christianity, and your whole society turns to hell. He destabilizes and bombs your country, then lets a remnant come to the United States, which is why America is called the great melting pot.

“Woe to him that increaseth that which is not his!” Did you forget Venezuela already? He took Venezuela and the oil. He steals and robs, possessing dwelling places that are not his, just as the Chaldeans did.

precepts.label: Isaiah 14:13-14
precepts.why:
Habakkuk says, “Woe to him that coveteth an evil covetousness to his house, that he may set his nest on high, that he may be delivered from the power of evil!” Is that not what Nimrod and them were doing? Before we get scattered, let us build a tower and get up to heaven. Today's Babylon has the same characteristics and attributes. Jeremiah said it too: “Though Babylon should mount up to heaven, and though she should fortify the height of her strength, yet from me shall spoilers come unto her”.

Isaiah shows the heart of it: “For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God”. That is space travel. NASA and SpaceX are advancing plans for a permanent presence on the moon through the Artemis program, and Artemis 2 just went up. Elon Musk talks of colonizing Mars. Why does Esau the Edomite want to go to Mars? Because it is the red planet.

“I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north”: that is us, in North America. “I will ascend above the heights of the clouds”: that is airplanes. How could that part be true, because you see it, while the verse above it about the stars is fake? You can have your doubting Thomas saying it's all fake. Is it fake like the planes you fly on and the helicopters you see? Stop watching stupid YouTube clips.

He sets his nest on high thinking he will be delivered from the power of evil when destruction comes. But he “hast consulted shame to thy house by cutting off many people”. “Woe to him that buildeth a town with blood, and stablisheth a city by iniquity!” America was built with blood: the schools, the churches and the courthouses are on the bones and blood of our brothers and sisters. Did not Cain establish a city by iniquity? There is no new thing under the sun.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 12:10-11
precepts.why:
Habakkuk says, “Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him”. Something is wrong with that man; he is not normal. Wisdom of Solomon shows Esau: “But executing thy judgments upon them by little and little, thou gavest them place of repentance”. By little and little: a war here, a war there, a storm here, a tsunami there, a plague here, a plague there.

“Not being ignorant that they were a naughty generation, and that their malice was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed.” A naughty generation, like the border of wickedness. Their hatred was bred in them: when God created them, a couple of drops of hatred, put in the oven and baked, and you cannot get it out of the dough. Their cogitation, their way of thinking, their mind frame, will never change. The Lord created him that way.

Sometimes they do things they don't even know why they do. In Florida a man caring for handicapped kids lay flat on the ground with his hands up, and the cop shot him; asked why, the cop said, I don't know. In the South bodies are found hanging and the judgment is suicide, as if our brothers had superpowers to tie their own hands behind their backs and dunk their necks into the noose.

“For it was a cursed seed from the beginning”. Not a blessed seed: Cain was cursed from the beginning, and he came back as Esau, cursed from the beginning. “Neither didst thou for fear of any man give them pardon for those things wherein they sinned.” They cannot be pardoned. Their malice is bred in them, they are cursed from the beginning, their cogitation will never change, and no matter what they do they can never be pardoned for the sins they have committed. Your pastor done lied to you.

precepts.label: Micah 2:11
precepts.why:
Habakkuk says of the proud man, “because he transgresseth by wine”. What is the wine he transgresses by? Micah gives the precept: “If a man walking in the spirit and falsehood do lie, saying, I will prophesy unto thee of wine and of strong drink; he shall even be the prophet of this people.”

The wine is the falsehood and the lying. Esau is a liar. He gave you Protestant: lies. Mormon: lies. Seventh-day Adventists, Jehovah's Witnesses, Pentecostal: lies. Freemasonry, Rosicrucian, Thelema: lies. Every institute of doctrine he put on this earth for you to follow and worship is a lie, and all they do is take you away from God.

That wine is how he rules. He “neither keepeth at home”: the US controls about 850 military bases in more than 90 countries, and there are more churches than military bases. The real way to control us is through Christianity, because we are more obedient to Christianity than to his military. And the church convinces you it is okay to be broke, okay to be poor and hurt, okay for your country to lie desolate while another man eats your riches: just pray to Jesus and you will be all right.

No, it is not okay. The earth belongs to us and it is going to come back to us. The just shall live by his faith, not by the wine of the prophet of lies.

precepts.label: Genesis 36:8
precepts.why:
Malachi moves from one name to the other. God says “Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith the Lord: yet I loved Jacob, And I hated Esau,” and then in the next breath, “Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished.” He goes from Esau to Edom because they are the same man. Genesis 36:8 settles it: “Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.” There is no argument. Esau is Edom, the one who came out of his mother red, hairy like a garment, and whose name was changed to Edom, meaning red. He became the father of the Edomite nations.

So when Malachi says “I loved Jacob,” it is Jacob and all his descendants, the twelve tribes, the whole nation of Israel. When he says “I hated Esau,” it is Esau and all his nation. God does love us, even though, looking at our condition in the ghetto with everything going wrong, we ask “Wherein hast thou loved us?”

Edom said, “We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places.” Living in the Caucasus Mountains and in the caves, they came back; it is called the Renaissance. They built major cities and took control of the whole earth. But “They shall build, but I will throw down”: the Lord, the God of war, will tear it down.

“they shall call them, The border of wickedness”: not him, but them, all of them. There is not one righteous Edomite in that verse, and no one can make the Bible say what it does not say. They are “The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” Indignation is anger aroused by something unjust, unworthy, and Esau is both. Forever means forever. If the Lord has indignation against them forever, the Christian who argues they can be saved has been drugged by his religion.

precepts.label: Psalms 50:16
precepts.why:
“And I hated Esau.” God said he hates Esau, and Esau is the white man. “Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places.” That is the rebirth, the Renaissance: we will build. “They shall build, but I will throw down”, which they call the dark ages, “and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.”

Keep in mind it says the people. A lot of us think they are not the same. Oh, they are the same, from the little baby all the way to the oldest. Some of them are more iced than others and show it more, but make no mistake: every single one of them hates your guts. They are all Edomites, the same people.

David shows what God says to that wicked people: “But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?” Esau is the wicked. Esau has no business opening the Bible at all.

That is why it makes no sense for an Israelite to go into a debate with Esau over the Bible. We teach that the scripture says Esau is not going to get the kingdom. Why would I debate him over John 3:16 to prove to him he is going to get the kingdom? Do not be concerned with Esau. He is not even supposed to open the Bible.

precepts.label: Isaiah 14:12
precepts.why:
The Lord hated Esau and calls his people “The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” Isaiah shows what that people does in the earth: “How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!” Esau weakens the nations.

How? Economic, political and military power. Look at what Donald Trump is doing in Venezuela and in Africa right now. They bombed Nigeria on Christmas Day and claimed it was to protect Christians from persecution. They bombed Venezuela and claimed it was to stop drug trafficking, while Mexico, on America's own border, has more drug cartels than any place in the world. They want the oil. Later Trump said it plainly, return the oil to our land, as if Venezuela ever stole oil or land from America. The rich think the poor are stupid and will believe anything, and our people believe it.

And America always puts a black face on it. Before they attacked Iraq it was Colin Powell, lying about weapons of mass destruction. Before they bombed a black nation for its oil, they did not pick a lawyer, a doctor or an engineer. They picked a hoe, the same black woman who was shaking her behind, reading what they told her to read about defending Christians in Nigeria. That is the ultimate disrespect to black people.

The hypocrisy is plain. In Jerusalem the so-called Jews say they spit on the ground when they see a crucifix, call for killing Christians, and spit in a Christian woman's face in the street, and nobody bombs them to defend Christians. There is no truth in the white man. If he says look up, you better look down.

Micah shows the same people: “Woe to them that devise iniquity, and work evil upon their beds! when the morning is light, they practise it, because it is in the power of their hand. And they covet fields, and take them by violence.” The oil in Nigeria and Venezuela, the diamonds and the copper in Africa. America was built by violence on stolen land. That is Lucifer weakening the nations, and why God says, “Never trust thine enemy.”

precepts.label: Isaiah 9:1-2
precepts.why:
Some Israelites had come back to the land, and watch what they were calling part of the kingdom of Israel: “The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles.” They were calling them Gentiles.

Isaiah wrote it first as prophecy: “when at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict her by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.” That affliction is the Assyrian captivity: wham. Zebulun and Naphtali were carried away, and their land became Galilee of the nations, of the Gentiles.

Then Isaiah says what would come to them: “The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: they that dwell in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined.” Matthew gives it back as “The people which sat in darkness saw great light.” Isaiah is prophesying and Matthew is revealing what it is really talking about.

“From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.” Christ was that great light spoken of, shining on the scattered tribes of Israel that had been made Gentiles.

precepts.label: Isaiah 42:6-7
precepts.why:
“I the Lord have called thee in righteousness, and will hold thine hand, and will keep thee, and give thee for a covenant of the people, for a light of the Gentiles.” The one given for a light is Christ, the great light that sprung up in Galilee.

Those Gentiles there are not talking about other nations. It is talking about what we just read in Matthew: “Galilee of the Gentiles”, the land of Zabulon and Nephthalim, the tribes of Israel carried away and called Gentiles.

Why is he sent? “To open the blind eyes, to bring out the prisoners from the prison, and them that sit in darkness out of the prison house.” Them that sit in darkness are the same “people which sat in darkness” in Matthew 4:16, the people that walked in darkness in Isaiah 9. It all goes back to Matthew 4:15-16 and Isaiah 9:1-2.

So when Christ began to preach “Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand”, he was the covenant of the people and the light of the Gentiles, sent to Israel sitting in darkness to bring them out of the prison house.

precepts.label: Luke 1:6
precepts.why:
Christ said to men, “Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.” The trinity doctrine says no: only God can keep the commandments, so Christ cannot be fully a man, because a full man can't keep those laws, but a full man and a full God can. The insidiousness behind it is to make it impossible for man to keep God's commandments.

Luke answers that with John the Baptist's parents, Zacharias and Elisabeth: “And they were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless.” Both righteous. Walking in all the commandments. Blameless: that's perfect. So human beings can keep God's commandments, perfect as the Father in heaven. It can be done.

The scripture also says we are gods but shall die like men, so we are the two anyway; for not keeping the commandments we die like men.

Peel back the layers of confusion and the doctrine is all about removing the humanity of Christ, or keeping some of it and making him a god too, so that man can't keep the commandments: Christ kept the laws so we don't have to do anything. That's the whole premise behind the great swelling words. “The discourse of fools is irksome, and their sport is the wantonness of sin”: their sport is not having to keep the commandments. Where is Christmas, New Year, Halloween, carnival, Labor Day, the Fourth of July or birthdays in the Bible? Your three-in-one God has nothing to say about them.

precepts.label: Luke 9:5
precepts.why:
“Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and turn again and rend you.” Don't waste your time talking to dumbass people; they'll turn against you and fight you. There is no magic scripture. You cannot save everyone. Some people are meant, predestined, to be stupid.

Luke gives the instruction Christ gave: “And whosoever will not receive you, when ye go out of that city, shake off the very dust from your feet for a testimony against them.” Shake off the very dust. Wash your hands of them and leave them alone.

If you explain that the heavenly Father is the Most High God, that he has a son, and that his son has sons, the children of Israel, and they can't understand it and say no, they're all one, leave that negro alone. You're wasting your time; he is on medications or should be.

The proverbs read with it say the same: “If a wise man contendeth with a foolish man, whether he rage or laugh, there is no rest.” There is no conclusion; it is a circular argument that goes nowhere. “The heart of the foolish is like a cartwheel; and his thoughts are like a rolling axletree.” Three is one, one is three, round and round. These are unreasonable people, so you shake off the dust and move on.

precepts.why:
A Christian pastor was played saying the other nations will come in the same gate Abraham comes through, because Abraham was not an Israelite. They try to get slicker and slicker. “Thus saith the Lord of hosts; Behold, I will save my people from the east country, and from the west country; And I will bring them, and they shall dwell in the midst of Jerusalem: and they shall be my people.” My people. So that's only the Israelites.

The chapter opens with who it is for: “I was jealous for Zion with great jealousy.” Zion is not all nations on the planet. The ones coming from the east country and the west country to sit down with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob are Zion.

And the mere fact that he has to address it proves our teaching is in his school, his church. He is trying to do a cleanup; it is impacting the church.

precepts.why:
They always like to go to Abraham, like that is going to get the other nations in. The pastor said the nations come in through Abraham's gate because Abraham was not an Israelite and we have the faith of Abraham. Paul had to clean that up.

“Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called.” Being of Abraham does not make you one of the children. The calling is on Isaac: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, 12 tribes. That is why Christ said the many from the east and west “shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob”, the fathers of one line.

That cuts his stuff about bringing up Abraham. You just close your Bible up and sit down.

precepts.label: Zechariah 12:7
precepts.why:
Christ commanded the twelve, “Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not: But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” Those Gentiles are the northern kingdom; that's why they are in the same sentence with Samaria. Here's the prophecy of it: “The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.” The tents of Judah first.

So when Christ came, he wasn't going, hey, I'm just gathering all Israel at once. He said, no, I got to start with Judah, and then the rest of them come later on. That is why he held the apostles back from the Gentiles and the Samaritans in Matthew 10: the order was set by the prophet, Judah first.

precepts.label: Psalms 83:3
precepts.why:
Christ says, “And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul”. They can't kill the real you, brothers and sisters. You think that body is the real you, but it is just a shell that corrodes in time. So why is our people so afraid to die? David shows it: “They have taken crafty counsel against thy people, and consulted against thy hidden ones.”

Slavery, miseducation and religion are all part of that crafty counsel. Their religions make you think this is all there is, like the Sam Cooke song: I don't know what's up there beyond the sky. It puts a spirit of fear on you: if you die, you're going to hell and you're going to burn down there. So everybody is afraid to die.

But when you read the Bible, how come our foremothers and forefathers did not have the spirit we have today? They knew something we don't. The woman with the seven sons said, kill me now, cut my arms off, cut my tongue. We say, what the hell is this? Because the crafty counsel taught us lie after lie about reality: that after this you're done.

The Bible calls death sleep, many times. That's all it is, and you wake up before the Lord. Paul said to be absent from the body is to be present with the Lord. But do we believe that, or what the white man says on his television screens?

Christ goes on, “but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell”: that is the lake of fire, which is not now. When you die now, everybody is at rest, even the wicked. When the Lord returns he takes the keys of hell and death and opens it all up, and that is when the lake of fire comes. So don't fear them that kill the body, because the things we teach will get us killed, and you will not deny Christ if you have not swallowed their crafty counsel.

precepts.label: Acts 26:10-11
precepts.why:
Christ says, “But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.” Under what conditions? Not at work saying, yeah, I believe in God. Read in context, it is tribulation, persecution, Jacob's trouble: I never believed that Israelite stuff, I don't believe in those commandments, my husband forced me, my wife forced me.

Paul testified what denying looks like from the persecutor's side: “Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them.”

“And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme”. Compel means he forced them to blaspheme. That is what Christ was talking about: deny me under torture, persecution, tribulation, hard times. That is the trial all of us alive at this time must go through.

Paul was not the only persecutor. What Paul did, they were all doing: the Pharisees, and later the inquisitors under Queen Isabella and King Ferdinand in the time of Spain and Portugal, whose job was to hunt down Israelites keeping the commandments, to Africa, to Mexico, to South and North America.

And “being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.” That is why Christ said, when they persecute you in this city, flee into another.

Everybody in here says they love God, but some of us are liars. Some are not valiant for the truth; you are a professional student, a hireling. The hireling sees the wolf coming and leaves the sheep. Think about being compelled to blaspheme, as in the film Unthinkable, where they brought in a man's wife and kids to make him confess. You think that could never happen to you; the devil is a liar. What Paul was doing is what Christ said is going to happen.

That's mercy, and we need that mercy.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 5:2
precepts.why:
“And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold.” Why is iniquity going to abound? Because of the false prophets: the false Christians and these foolish Abrahamic religions teaching lie after lie. They glorify sin; sin is being glorified. And the love of many waxing cold means we are going to start to hate one another.

Ezra was told the same thing: “But iniquity shall be increased above that which now thou seest, or that thou hast heard long ago.” The angel was telling Ezra that iniquity would go way beyond anything he had known or seen.

And look at it now. Men are cutting their privates off and having a vagina cut in there. That was unheard of. Women are getting penises sewn on. You cannot make this stuff up. Magic Johnson's son says he is only attracted to straight men; if he is attracted to you, he is not straight.

That is iniquity increased above anything heard of long ago, exactly as the angel said. So repent. “But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved”: we have to endure the hardships, the tribulation and the persecution Christ said would come, and not let our love wax cold.

precepts.label: Revelation 7:1-4
precepts.why:
“And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come.” Earlier Christ said in Matthew 10, “Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come.” So we are not going to reach all the Israelites. Then what does “all the world” mean, and when does the end come? Revelation 7 answers.

“I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth”. That is the fighting, the wars. “That the wind should not blow on the earth”: the armies. “Nor on the sea”: the marines and the navies. “Nor on any tree”: what is above the trees is the air force.

“And I saw another angel ascending from the east, having the seal of the living God”. The seal of the living God is not the hexagram. It is the law: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” He cried to the four angels “to whom it was given to hurt the earth and the sea”, hurt it with destruction: “Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.”

“And there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” So the end begins when the 144,000 are sealed. The world Christ is talking about in Matthew 24 is the 144,000: when they are sealed, then shall the end come.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 13:5
precepts.why:
Revelation 7 has four angels holding the four winds of the earth. Let the Bible say what the wind is. Write it down: “And after this I beheld, and, lo, there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea”.

Where did the multitude come from? From the four winds of heaven. And what did they come for? To subdue the man that came out of the sea. So the winds are their armies coming against the Son of God, coming against the master.

That is why the four angels hold the winds so they do not blow on the earth, the sea or any tree: the armies on land, the navies and marines on the sea, and the air force above the trees. The destruction is held back until the servants of God are sealed. When the 144,000 are sealed, the winds are let go, the nations gather for war, and after that tribulation the Son of man comes in the clouds of heaven.

precepts.label: Isaiah 8:16
precepts.why:
In Revelation 7 another angel ascends from the east “having the seal of the living God”, and the destruction is held back “till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.” What is the seal of the living God?

It is not the hexagram. Many of us thought so years ago when we were young. Isaiah says what it is: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” The seal of the living God is the law, bound up and sealed among his disciples. Pay attention, because if you blink you might miss it.

So the servants sealed in their foreheads are the ones with the law of God in their minds: “an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” When they are sealed, the four winds are loosed and the end comes. That is why this gospel, the law and the testimony, has to be preached in all the world for a witness: to seal the 144,000 before the end.

precepts.label: Isaiah 66:19-21
precepts.why:
Remember, the 144,000 have to be sealed, and then the end comes. Isaiah shows what they do: “And I will set a sign among them, and I will send those that escape of them unto the nations”. Those that escape are the 144,000. He sends them “to Tarshish”, Spain; “Pul”, Libya; “and Lud, that draw the bow, to Tubal”, Turkey; “and Javan”, the Grecian islands; “to the isles afar off, that have not heard my fame, neither have seen my glory”.

There will be people who have not heard the fame of the Lord and have not seen his glory: Israelites who have not heard or seen anything, and we have to go get them. “And they shall declare my glory among the Gentiles.” That is “this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations”.

You might think that is talking about now. The next verse clears it up: “And they shall bring all your brethren for an offering unto the Lord out of all nations upon horses, and in chariots, and in litters, and upon mules, and upon swift beasts, to my holy mountain Jerusalem”. Jerusalem is already established as holy. Is Jerusalem holy today? No, there are bombs and missiles going off there. So this is not now; the kingdom is already set up.

“And I will also take of them for priests and for Levites, saith the Lord.” The brothers gathered from among those nations, the Lord will make them priests and Levites. With that, Matthew 24:14 gives a deeper understanding: the gospel preached in all the world is the work of the 144,000, and once they are sealed, the end comes.

thread.text: And many false prophets shall rise, and shall deceive many.

thread.label: Matthew 24:14
thread.text: And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come.

thread.text: For then shall be great tribulation, such as was not since the beginning of the world to this time, no, nor ever shall be.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 32:17
precepts.why:
With the technology Esau has, just imagine a white Jesus coming out of the sky in the middle of war, making all the armies of the world put down their weapons, ending war. The elect are not going to believe it, and we are going to be enemy number one. Why? Because we know the scriptures. Christ already warned us: “believe it not.” It might be possible to deceive some, but not the elect.

“They sacrificed unto devils, not to God; to gods whom they knew not, to new gods that came newly up, whom your fathers feared not.” New gods that came newly up. The white Jesus is a new god; he was created during the Renaissance. Islam is a new god, created around 600 AD, after Christ. Those are the new gods our people went after, gods our fathers never feared.

So when a Christ appears in the sky, or they say he is in the desert or in the secret chambers, it is another new god come newly up, and to worship it is to sacrifice unto devils, not to God.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 16:36
precepts.why:
“Behold, the word of the Lord, receive it: believe not the gods of whom the Lord spake.” Receive it means believe it. Receive the word of the Lord, and do not believe these false gods out here.

It is the same warning Christ gave in Matthew 24: “Then if any man shall say unto you, Lo, here is Christ, or there; believe it not.” Whatever they show in the sky with their signs and wonders, the word of the Lord is what we receive, and the gods the Lord spoke against, the new gods that came newly up, we do not believe.

That is how the elect are kept from being deceived: not by what they see, but by holding to the word, because Christ said, “Behold, I have told you before.”

precepts.label: Matthew 24:4-5
precepts.why:
“And Jesus answered and said unto them, Take heed that no man deceive you. For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many.” That happened from the time of the Renaissance, when Spain, Portugal, and Rome worked together to conquer all the dark nations and force Christianity on them.

Then, in the order of the chapter, Christ goes into 70 AD from verse 15, and at verse 22 into World War II: “And except those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved: but for the elect’s sake those days shall be shortened.” Then “if any man shall say unto you, Lo, here is Christ, or there; believe it not. For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders”. What we are reading about there is the last days, this time period.

So the many who came in his name at the Renaissance deceived many, and in this time period the false Christs will come with great signs and wonders, technology so astronomical that, if it were possible, they would deceive the very elect. We have not seen anything yet. But when Christ comes it will be like lightning, out of the east and shining unto the west, not in any desert and not in any secret chambers.

thread.label: Matthew 24:24
thread.text: For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect.

classes.title: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

thread.label: Matthew 24:29-31
thread.text: Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:

precepts.label: Isaiah 34:4-5
precepts.why:
“Immediately after the tribulation of those days”: the churches argue about a seven-year dispensation, pre-trib and post-trib, and say the church is not going through tribulation. They do not know the Bible. Those who are alive must and will go through tribulation. Then “the stars shall fall from heaven”: missiles, rockets. “And the powers of the heavens shall be shaken”: that is war. Notice it says heavens, plural; it is not talking about the sky. What powers of the heavens?

Isaiah shows it: “And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll”, the mushroom effect. “And all their host shall fall down, as the leaf falleth off from the vine, and as a falling fig from the fig tree”: missiles and rockets falling.

“For my sword shall be bathed in heaven”. Christ said his sword would be bathed in heaven, so what heaven is he going to bathe his sword in? “Behold, it shall come down upon Idumea, and upon the people of my curse, to judgment.” Idumea is the so-called white man, the leading race on the planet. The powers of the heavens shaken is the war with Idumea, all these Edomite nations.

So Christ comes back for war, not only to save. The order is tribulation, then war between the nations, then the sign of the Son of man. The gap may be five years, as World War II was once America entered, or seven; it does not say.

precepts.label: Isaiah 45:4
precepts.why:
“And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” Who is the elect? Not everybody.

Isaiah says: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect”. We are the elect. Israel is the elect. Not the Baptist church, and not all races on the planet.

And it is from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other, because Isaiah 66 already showed there are Israelites scattered in the isles afar off who have not heard his fame nor seen his glory, and we have to go get them.

Before that gathering, “then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn”. It is going to be a happy day, but we will be crying and fearful too. And it comes only after the tribulation. Christ is not returning this year or next year; bad things have to happen first and we have to be proven. Not being able to pay your light bill is not tribulation. We are too comfortable, still smoking weed, going to the club, defiling the Sabbath, the women dressed like hoes with no clothes; in their affliction they will seek him, and the affliction has not even begun.

precepts.label: Luke 21:25-28
precepts.why:
Luke tells the same coming, and shows where we are in it. “And there shall be signs in the sun”, like a solar eclipse, “and in the moon”, blood moons and lunar eclipses, “and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations”: we are seeing that now. “With perplexity”: perplexity means confusion. “The sea and the waves roaring”: the nations roaring.

“Men’s hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth: for the powers of heaven shall be shaken.” That is war. “And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.” Right now we are in verse 25 going into the top part of verse 26.

“And when these things begin to come to pass”: the signs in the sun, the moon and the stars, the distress of nations with perplexity. “Then look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh.” We are supposed to be looking up and lifting up our heads, knowing redemption is soon to come.

But we know the order of what is going to happen: tribulation, war, then Christ. So this is our time to clean ourselves up and get right with the Lord, because the time is drawing close.

precepts.label: Isaiah 66:15-16
precepts.why:
When Christ comes after the tribulation and the war, he does not come only to gather; he comes to judge. Isaiah shows it: “For, behold, the Lord will come with fire, and with his chariots like a whirlwind, to render his anger with fury, and his rebuke with flames of fire.”

“For by fire and by his sword will the Lord plead with all flesh: and the slain of the Lord shall be many.” All flesh. The slain of the Lord shall be many, and that is not just Esau. The wicked Israelites too.

That is why Christ is not coming tomorrow to rapture a comfortable church out of trouble. He comes with fire and sword against the nations of Idumea, and against every wicked one, including our own people who keep smoking, clubbing, and defiling the Sabbath. The powers of the heavens are shaken, his sword is bathed in heaven, and only his elect, Jacob and Israel who repented and endured, are gathered from the four winds.

thread.label: Mark 4:16-17
thread.text: And these are they likewise which are sown on stony ground; who, when they have heard the word, immediately receive it with gladness;

precepts.label: Matthew 24:9-10
precepts.why:
Those sown on stony ground hear the word and “immediately receive it with gladness”, but they have no root, and “when affliction or persecution ariseth for the word's sake, immediately they are offended.” For the word's sake means for teaching the gospel and living the gospel. Christ told us that affliction and persecution would come.

“Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name's sake.” Hated of all nations, for his name's sake. The religions that enslaved and destroyed our people, Christianity, Islam and Judaism, are now coming together side by side, like Nimrod bringing everybody together as one, and the ones hated by all of them are those who hold to the truth of Christ.

“And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.” Many shall be offended: that is the stony ground. They received the word with gladness, but when the persecution came, they were offended, betrayed their brothers and turned to hate.

It is already written. “In the latter times some shall depart from the faith”, and we are in the latter times now. Some of you, men and women listening, will depart from this faith: some because of persecution, some because they see signs and wonders, technological signs and wonders, and believe we've been wrong all this time. Christ said, “Behold, I have told you before.” He warned us, so that the persecution finds roots in us and not stony ground.

thread.label: Luke 4:5
thread.text: And the devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time.

precepts.label: Job 9:24
precepts.why:
How did Esau get all this power? “And the devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time.” He showed Christ all the great kingdoms: America, Russia, China, France, Germany, Europe. “All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it.” All these kingdoms were delivered to Satan, and he can give them to whoever he wants. But Christ answered, “Get thee behind me, Satan”, and worshipped God only. Satan tried to give Christ what already belonged to Christ.

Job shows who the power was given to: “The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof”. We are the judges of the earth, and the wicked covered our faces. The scripture says the earth was created for the Israelites, so the earth belongs to us. Esau covered the faces of the judges, and now Esau tries to give us what actually belongs to us, and some of us fall for it.

“if not, where, and who is he?” If this man is not the devil, show me who is. When you look, the most evil things on planet earth were caused by the white man. Somebody said, you want peace on earth, get rid of the white man. Picture the peace this land had before the white man came here, the peace the so-called American Indians had among themselves, the peace the continent of Africa had before the white man docked his boat there. They brought disease, rape, murder and stealing. That is what Malachi 1 is talking about: everywhere you see evil, move the curtain, and the white man is right there.

But the triumphing of the wicked is short, and the joy of the hypocrite but for a moment. The kingdoms the devil gave him will be broken, and the God of heaven will set up a kingdom which shall never be destroyed.

thread.label: Luke 12:7
thread.text: But even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Fear not therefore: ye are of more value than many sparrows.

classes.title: Civil War & the Son of Perdition

precepts.label: Romans 8:28
precepts.why:
“But even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Fear not therefore: ye are of more value than many sparrows.” Every hair on your head is numbered, so nothing can happen to you unless the Lord allows it. Don't be living and rolling in fear, and don't be scared of no damn ICE. A man's going is of the Lord. The spirit of Christ dwells in you; you are valuable.

Paul adds, “And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God.” If you love God, whatever happens, even bad things in your life, happens for good. When Aquila and Priscilla were deported, it was for good: they ended up as Paul's helpers teaching the gospel. God had a plan for them.

“To them who are the called according to his purpose.” Every last one of us is called according to God's purpose. None of us knows where our going is or what the Lord has planned for us, but he has a purpose for each of us.

A brother in France was told to stop teaching the word of God or leave. He would not stop, so they labelled him an extremist, refused to renew his papers, and deported him. Right now he is in Ghana, doing good, all praises to the Lord. So don't think papers, a green card or citizenship will protect you; laws are being set up to take them away from those who speak against America or Christianity. If they take your green card and send you back, it is what it is, of the Lord. Don't run, don't cry and lose your dignity; make preparation, and go over there and teach the word, because all things work together for good to them that love God.

thread.label: Luke 15:7
thread.text: I say unto you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance.

classes.title: Final Call: Message to the Black Man

precepts.label: Luke 15:10
precepts.why:
Christ says “joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance”, and then says it again: “Likewise, I say unto you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth.” The heavenly host, the angels, are happy when you change your life, when you get it together.

That is why we are weapons. “The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life; and he that winneth souls is wise.” You have the potential to convert sinners, to have a brother or sister change his life, and that makes you dangerous. When one sinner repents, the angels rejoice.

How do you win a soul? Ultimately it is the word of God, but the Lord gave a secret: “By long forbearing is a prince persuaded”. We are fishers of men, on duty all day, handing out flyers even at a gas station, not waiting till Saturday or till you feel like it. But you have to be patient; you can't be brutish. Are you looking to win the argument or to win the brother or sister? Listen, study the person, wait for the moment. Don't take it personal when someone doesn't take the flyer; maybe next time. If you get mad now you close the door on them, and what if Christ had closed the door on you? Believe the information will do its job and let the Lord do his part, because no man can come unto Christ except the Father draw him.

thread.text: And he said unto the disciples, The days will come, when ye shall desire to see one of the days of the Son of man, and ye shall not see it.

thread.label: Luke 19:11-27
thread.text: And as they heard these things, he added and spake a parable, because he was nigh to Jerusalem, and because they thought that the kingdom of God should immediately appear.

classes.title: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.label: Acts 1:9-11
precepts.why:
Christ spake this parable “because he was nigh to Jerusalem, and because they thought that the kingdom of God should immediately appear.” A lot of people thought the kingdom was coming at that time. That's why Paul later said, let no man deceive you: that day shall not come except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed.

“A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return.” The far country in this context is the heavens. Acts shows him going: “while they beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight.”

And Acts shows him returning: “Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye gazing up into heaven? this same Jesus, which is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven.” The nobleman is Christ. He went into heaven to receive the kingdom, and he is coming back, and when he returns he calls his servants to account.

precepts.label: Psalms 119:127
precepts.why:
“And he called his ten servants, and delivered them ten pounds, and said unto them, Occupy till I come.” What are the pounds? God's word.

David says: “Therefore I love thy commandments above gold; yea, above fine gold.” The commandments are more precious than gold, so the money the nobleman hands his servants is his word: the knowledge, the understanding, the faith he bestowed on each of us.

Occupy till I come means do something with it until he returns. When he comes back he wants to know “how much every man had gained by trading”: how much each one went out and taught the word. The servant who laid his pound up in a napkin kept the word to himself, and that is how he is judged.

precepts.label: Mark 8:31
precepts.why:
“But his citizens hated him, and sent a message after him, saying, We will not have this man to reign over us.” Who hated him? Mark shows it: “the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders, and of the chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.”

Rejected is the word to highlight. The elders, the chief priests and the scribes rejected him: back then it was the scribes and Pharisees and those that followed them who said, we will not have this man to reign over us.

Today there are no groups called scribes and Pharisees, but the same spirit is here. They are the Christians, they are the Muslims; they fall into this. They reject his reign, and at the end of the parable the King says what becomes of them: “But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me.”

precepts.label: Revelation 2:26-27
precepts.why:
“Well, thou good servant: because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.” That's what we all want: dominion. Revelation says the same: “And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations: And he shall rule them with a rod of iron; as the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers.”

We're not going to play with the nations. We've got to teach them to honor the King of kings. We've got to teach them the civil law, the ceremonial law, the dietary law, the moral law, and the history of Israel too. They are not going to be glorifying China any more, or the white man; they are going to glorify the history of Israel.

Just one city is too much to handle in this body and mind we have now. That's why it's exciting to read this: the Lord is going to have to change this. Some of you have problems dealing with that one black woman you've got right now, and you're talking about being lord over five cities. Being faithful in a very little now is what earns the authority then.

precepts.label: Romans 12:11
precepts.why:
The nobleman gave the pounds “that he might know how much every man had gained by trading.” The trading is going out teaching the word. It is business: “Not slothful in business; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord.”

This is talking about God's business. If it were the white man's business, you wouldn't be slothful, because you've got to eat, you've got to have a place to live. But in God's business people get slothful. Be fervent in spirit, on fire in spirit, serving the Lord.

The first servant's pound gained ten pounds and the second's gained five, and they were rewarded with cities. The servant who was slothful in the Lord's business laid his pound up in a napkin and gained nothing.

precepts.label: John 15:1-2
precepts.why:
“Take from him the pound, and give it to him that hath ten pounds.” Imagine the order, like the king in Game of Thrones giving orders to the men next to the throne. It's pure order. “For I say unto you, That unto every one which hath shall be given; and from him that hath not, even that he hath shall be taken away from him.”

John shows the same judgment: “Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away.” Not bearing fruit means you're not increasing in the fruits of the spirit. You're the same grimy person you were five years back; there's no change in you, no transformation. It goes for men and women: the same gossiper, murmurer, complainer you were five years ago, just here with fringes and a border of blue. He taketh away means he takes you away and kills you.

“and every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit.” You've got to be purged to bring forth more fruit. There are things in us that have to be cut: cut this off, cut that person off from you, cut this out of your soul and your spirit, so you can bear more fruit.

We've seen it. Brothers came among us with certain skills and did not expand on them, so the Most High, like musical chairs, moved them out of the way. Other brothers came in, took that office and ran with it, and you don't hear anything about the men who were here with the ability to do just that.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 32:17
precepts.why:
The third servant came with excuses: “Lord, behold, here is thy pound, which I have kept laid up in a napkin: For I feared thee, because thou art an austere man.” And the Lord answered, “Out of thine own mouth will I judge thee, thou wicked servant.”

“A sinful man will not be reproved, but findeth an excuse according to his will.” For every solution, these people have five excuses. The wicked servant would not own that he did nothing with what he was given; he blamed his lord for being austere.

Your excuses are not going to fly with Christ. He doesn't care about your excuses. He knew exactly what the servant knew: “Thou knewest that I was an austere man, taking up that I laid not down, and reaping that I did not sow.” If you knew it, you should have done something with it.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 2:20-21
precepts.why:
“Wherefore then gavest not thou my money into the bank, that at my coming I might have required mine own with usury?” This is the bank: the congregation. Usury means interest. So when Christ comes back, he wants interest on what he gave each of us.

Paul shows the great house: “But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.” The bank is his great house. Your work, your love, your zeal, your understanding: bring it into the bank, the congregation.

“If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master’s use, and prepared unto every good work.” The servant who brings what he was given into the house and purges himself becomes a vessel of honour, fit for the master's use when he returns and requires his own with usury.

precepts.label: Matthew 7:21-23
precepts.why:
“And another came, saying, Lord, behold, here is thy pound, which I have kept laid up in a napkin.” See that? Hirelings. I kept it laid up; I didn't do anything with the knowledge you bestowed on me, the faith you gave me.

“Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.” Many will say they prophesied and did many wonderful works in his name, “And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.” That goes back to this servant: he was in the truth, and he took his talent and hid it in a napkin. I'm not helping them any more; I did it full time, but I don't want to do it any more.

Remember the rift from Rehoboam; that was always the problem.

Hosea gives the reason: “Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.” Remember, Jeroboam set up priests in the land, and Ephraim went into idolatry. So we did not deal with them.

He revealed himself to her, “I that speak unto thee am he”, which he would not do if she were not an Israelite, and his disciples marvelled that he talked with her, because the Jews had no dealings with the Samaritans. precepts.label: Isaiah 7:9
precepts.why:
Why is a woman of Samaria an Israelite, and why did the Jews have no dealings with her? Isaiah names it: “And the head of Ephraim is Samaria”. Samaria was the capital of Ephraim, the head city of the northern kingdom.

So when John says Christ “must needs go through Samaria” and met “a woman of Samaria”, he is in the land of Ephraim, among the northern kingdom. That is why she could say “our father Jacob, which gave us the well”, and “Our fathers worshipped in this mountain”. Her fathers were the fathers of Israel.

The rift between the kingdoms went back to Rehoboam, and Judah had nothing to do with Ephraim and its capital. But Christ said “the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father”, the hour of 70 AD, when nobody would be worshipping in Jerusalem or Samaria. “Ye worship ye know not what: we know what we worship: for salvation is of the Jews.” He stayed two days in Samaria and many believed on him. That is the raising up of the tabernacle of David that fell: both houses gathered back to the Messiah.

precepts.label: Isaiah 9:6-7
precepts.why:
“For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder.” When Acts 7:38 speaks of “the church in the wilderness”, it is speaking of the government of Christ. That church was Israel, the twelve tribes, and it is his government that rests upon his shoulder.

“And his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.” Christ is called the everlasting Father because many times in the Old Testament, when you read about the Father, it is making reference to Christ. That is why, when Philip asked Christ to show them the Father, Christ answered that he had been so long time with him and still Philip had not known him. Christ is letting you know: I am the father that created you. Not the Father, but your father.

“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.” Increase means it starts small. Christ said the kingdom of heaven starts like a mustard seed, but in the end it is the largest. Once that mustard seed is planted and growing, there is no stopping it. It sits “upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice from henceforth even for ever. The zeal of the Lord of hosts will perform this.”

This truth cannot be stopped. No matter how many Israelites they attempt to kill or arrest, the church that was in the wilderness, the government on Christ’s shoulder, keeps increasing and has no end.

precepts.label: Daniel 2:44
precepts.why:
“And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed.” These kings are the last kings of the image, the ten toes, the ten common markets, and America is that iron and that clay. In their days God sets up his kingdom, and that is what is happening now: Israelites are waking up all over the world.

“Which shall never be destroyed.” That says the same thing as Isaiah 9: “Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.” The church in the wilderness, the twelve tribes under Christ’s government, is a kingdom God himself sets up, and it will not be brought down.

That is the difference between this truth and the movements of men. Asked in an interview how Israel in Christ differs from the Black Panthers, Martin Luther King, SNCC or the Young Lords, the answer was plain: those were all man-made, they all had an end, and most of them do not even exist today. This kingdom is not man-made.

“And the kingdom shall not be left to other people, but it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever.” The God of heaven set it up, so no government of this world can stop it.

precepts.label: Matthew 16:15-18
precepts.why:
Christ asks, “But whom say ye that I am?” and Peter answers, “Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.” Christ tells him “flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven.”

Then verse 18 is the key: “upon this rock I will build my church”. That rock is Christ himself, not Peter. And the church he builds is the same government we read of in Isaiah 9, the same church in the wilderness in Acts 7:38: Israel.

“And the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.” There is no stopping us. Once you get the proper understanding of the word of God, you cannot stop it; it is going to flourish and grow. The gates of hell will attempt to stop it, but they will not prevail. They attempted it when they murdered Nat Turner, Denmark Vesey and Gabriel Prosser, men who knew they were Israelites. They said kill them, and it did not stop. Through whispers and hushes, this word kept going.

The gates of hell are not a flesh and blood enemy: “For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.” In our carnal mind we think that if we organize we can overthrow the system, but we cannot. The governments of this earth are set up by Satan, and God allows it. Only God can bring all that down, and Christ has promised that none of it will prevail against his church.

precepts.label: Acts 22:12
precepts.why:
Cornelius is called “A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway.” How do you become a devout man? People go, yeah, he was another nation, but he was devout. No, no, no.

Look at how the scripture uses the word: “And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews which dwelt there”. You see? A devout man according to the law. The other nations did not have the law.

So how was Cornelius a devout man according to the law? How did he fear God? How did he know how to pray to God? He had to know the law. He even kept the hours of prayer: the angel came to him “about the ninth hour of the day”, and he told Peter, “at the ninth hour I prayed in my house”.

So yes, Cornelius is an Israelite, northern kingdom. His devotion was devotion to the law of God, which was given to Israel and to no other nation.

precepts.label: Acts 21:16
precepts.why:
Cornelius was “a certain man in Cesarea”. Write this down: Caesarea is in the land of Israel. It is in the land of West Manasseh, right beside Samaria. It is not some foreign country; it is the land of the northern kingdom.

And Acts shows believers coming out of that very place: “There went with us also certain of the disciples of Cesarea, and brought with them one Mnason of Cyprus, an old disciple, with whom we should lodge.” You had some disciples that came from Caesarea as well, the same place Cornelius is from.

Peter lived in Joppa, the seaport there, and he sailed up north to visit Cornelius. Christ was raised further up, in Galilee, so he was raised around them in that area. And the place called Scythopolis means city of the Scythians, and the Scythians are northern kingdom also: that is who Paul wrote to in Colossians 3:11.

So Caesarea was a place of disciples in the land of Manasseh, and Cornelius and his kinsmen were northern kingdom Israelites living in their own land, not a Roman people God took in instead of Israel.

precepts.label: Hosea 8:8
precepts.why:
In the dream Peter “saw heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending unto him, as it had been a great sheet knit at the four corners”. What is that vessel? Hosea says it: “Israel is swallowed up: now shall they be among the Gentiles as a vessel wherein is no pleasure.”

Israel is the vessel. Swallowed up among the nations, a vessel no one has pleasure in: that is what came down to Peter in the sheet.

That is why the dream was never about eating unclean animals. Verse 28 is where Peter breaks the dream down: “God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean.” Any man. It is not talking about roaches or ants or eating unclean pig. The dream was about man.

What man? The Israelites being cleansed, the northern kingdom being cleansed. The vessel full of fourfooted beasts and creeping things is Israel scattered among the Gentiles, and God was showing Peter it was time to bring them back in.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 37:21-23
precepts.why:
The voice spake unto Peter the second time: “What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common.” So what does God cleanse? Does he cleanse Esau? I never read that one. Ezekiel tells us who God cleanses.

“Behold, I will take the children of Israel from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land: And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all”.

Then: “but I will save them out of all their dwellingplaces, wherein they have sinned, and will cleanse them: so shall they be my people, and I will be their God.” God says he is going to cleanse us, the twelve tribes.

So what God hath cleansed is Israel, the northern kingdom brought back to Judah. That is why Peter could go into Cornelius’ house. Christians read verses 34 and 35, “God is no respecter of persons: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him”, and say God accepts everybody, that Cornelius was a white man, an Italian, a Roman. That is supersessionism, replacement theology. The next verse explains it: “The word which God sent unto the children of Israel”.

precepts.label: Obadiah 18

Obadiah shows Samaritans, Gentiles and Israel at the same time: “And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble”.
