precepts.label: Luke 20:20
precepts.why:
“Think not upon those that have walked feignedly before thee.” To feign means to pretend, to fake, to give a false show of something. And Luke shows feigning in action: “And they watched him, and sent forth spies, which should feign themselves just men, that they might take hold of his words.” They pretended to be just men so they could catch Christ in his words.

During the time of Christ there were a lot of fake brothers among them, so we expect that to be true today. There is going to be an explosion, a spiritual explosion, an influx of believers, especially from the Christian church: 3,000 one day, 5,000 another day. It's going to happen, because the scriptures say it.

But we have to be mindful: there will be feigned people among them. Ezra asks God not to think upon those, “but remember them, which according to thy will have known thy fear.”

precepts.label: Luke 9:62
precepts.why:
“And Jesus said unto him, No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.” That's a hireling: he put his hand to the work and then looked back. Some of y'all are sitting here right now. There is a God; remember that.

This is where you self-examine. Am I being a phony, a hypocrite among the brethren? Am I walking feignedly? Only you can answer that. You and God know the answer; we don't.

Ezra prays that God would think not upon those that walked feignedly, but remember them that have known his fear. The one who looks back from the plough is not fit for the kingdom.

precepts.label: Hebrews 10:38
precepts.why:
“Now the just shall live by faith: but if any man draw back, my soul shall have no pleasure in him.” That was the guy who put the talent in the napkin: he drew back.

As we're doing the restructuring, certain captains get asked, why did you move this brother from this position to that position? Oh, he's not the same any more. When he came in, he was on fire; we didn't have to tell him what to do. Now you've got to yell at him, you've got to force him. So drop him down and move him to the side, like we read in 1 Corinthians 6 today.

The Lord has no pleasure in the one who draws back. That is walking feignedly before him, and Ezra asks God to think not upon those, but to remember them that according to his will have known his fear.

precepts.label: Psalms 44:18
precepts.why:
Against the hireling who puts his hand to the plough and looks back, and the man who draws back, stands Israel's confession: “Our heart is not turned back, neither have our steps declined from thy way.” That's how you've got to be. That's how we have to be.

The heart that does not turn back and the steps that do not decline are what it means to walk before God unfeignedly. Those are the ones Ezra asks God to remember: “remember them, which according to thy will have known thy fear.”

So examine yourself. Has your heart turned back? Have your steps declined from his way since you first came in on fire? You and God know the answer.

precepts.label: Luke 24:32
precepts.why:
“And they said one to another, Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?” When those scriptures come out, your heart is supposed to be burning for this.

How do I get this word out? What ideas do I have? I want to give my time to this truth; everything else outside of this doesn't matter. If your heart is not burning with the word of God, if you don't have the desire to learn, to teach, to better yourself, to better the nation of Israel, you are going to fade away. You're a hireling.

You could be in 5 years, 10 years, 20 years, but this word is supposed to make your heart burn to get it out. The hireling walks feignedly; the one whose heart burns is the one who has known God's fear.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 1:5
precepts.why:
Feign is a verb that means to pretend, to fake, to give a false show of something. It includes pretending an illness: a lot of sisters get Sabbath sick. It includes faking an emotion, or making up an excuse. Remember the brother who used to go around teaching fake it till you make it? Don't raise that man up; he isn't right. To feign means to pretend: you are a fake brother, you are pretending.

Paul sets the opposite: “Now the end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned.” Unfeigned faith: not feigned, not folly.

The whole end of the commandment is charity from a pure heart and a faith that is not pretended. That is the walk Ezra asks God to remember, and the feigned walk is the one he asks God to think not upon.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 1:22
precepts.why:
“Seeing ye have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit unto unfeigned love of the brethren, see that ye love one another with a pure heart fervently.” Unfeigned: don't be fake, don't be phony.

Some brothers can fake it real good. If a sister asks us, what about this brother, we can only tell her what you show us. Is he really like that? She's got to talk to him more in depth, more personally, to find out how he truly is.

That is why the love of the brethren has to be unfeigned, out of a pure heart. Only you and God know whether you are walking feignedly; we only see what you show us.

precepts.label: Romans 12:10-11
precepts.why:
“Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another.” That is the unfeigned love of the brethren, real and not put on.

“Not slothful in business”: not lazy concerning God's work. “fervent in spirit”: be on fire in your spirit. “serving the Lord.”

This is the opposite of walking feignedly. The feigned brother came in on fire and now has to be yelled at and forced; the hireling looked back from the plough. The one Ezra asks God to remember, one “which according to thy will have known thy fear”, is kindly affectioned to the brethren, not slothful in God's business, and on fire in spirit, serving the Lord.

The roaring lion, Christ, comes out of the wood and speaks to the eagle, to America: “Art not thou it that remainest of the four beasts, whom I made to reign in my world, that the end of their times might come through them?” Who is going to be ruling in the last kingdom? That lets you know that Esau is not done away. He is not gone off the face of the earth. How could he be, when he is the ruler of the last kingdom? Esau is still on the earth. precepts.label: Daniel 7:7
precepts.why:
Ezra saw “an eagle, which had twelve feathered wings, and three heads” come up from the sea, and she “spread her wings over all the earth.” Then the angel told him: “The eagle, whom thou sawest come up from the sea, is the kingdom which was seen in the vision of thy brother Daniel. But it was not expounded unto him, therefore now I declare it unto thee.”

Go back to Daniel and see what he saw: “a fourth beast, dreadful and terrible, and strong exceedingly; and it had great iron teeth: it devoured and brake in pieces, and stamped the residue with the feet of it: and it was diverse from all the beasts that were before it; and it had ten horns.” Daniel saw the lion, the symbol of Babylon; the bear of the Persians and Medes; the leopard of the Greeks. But this fourth one was diverse, different from every beast before it, and Daniel never understood it and never saw its animal symbol.

What was hidden from Daniel was revealed to Ezra: the fourth kingdom is the eagle. We are living in the United States of America, and what is their symbol? The eagle. This eagle has three heads: Rome, America, Britain.

That is the same beast of Daniel 7:25 that “shall speak great words against the most High, and shall wear out the saints of the most High, and think to change times and laws.” So the fourth beast is not some kingdom long gone. It is the eagle kingdom we live under now, the one that devoured, brake in pieces and stamped the residue, and wore our people out in slavery.

precepts.label: Hosea 1:10
precepts.why:
“Afterward saw I the same man come down from the mountain, and call unto him another peaceable Multitude.” The same man is Jesus the Christ, the black Messiah of Revelation 1, with feet like burnt brass and hair like wool. And the angel explains it: “he gathered another peaceable multitude unto him”, those are the ten tribes, the northern kingdom. That is who Christ gathers in these last days, through the work the prophets are doing in the worldwide blitzes, in Puerto Rico, Ecuador, Mexico, Chile.

The historians knew who that peaceable multitude was. Columbus gave the peaceable multitude of the islands the name Indios, because he took their home to be the Indies, but perhaps also because he thought of them as living in God, en Dios. Columbus was reading the book of Esdras. The scriptures call them a peaceable multitude; the world called them noble savages.

The historian Duran found more confirmation in Hosea: “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered.” Surely, he argued, that promise was fulfilled by the multitudes the Spanish found in the new world. Remember Israel blessed Ephraim and Manasseh to be a multitude of nations; that is what the Spaniards found.

Duran also noted that the Indians of Mexico had traditions of long journeys like the one from Assyria to Arzareth, flights like the Exodus from Egypt, earthquakes that swallowed evil men, manna falling from heaven, and an old man who began the tale of his people’s origins with the words in the beginning, like Genesis. Why would so-called Indians be quoting the Bible unless they were Israelites? We had books, we carried the Bible with us, and they stole our records.

So the peaceable multitude Christ calls is the ten tribes scattered on this side of the world, and Hosea’s promise stands over them: “in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.”

That is a jump in history, into the Persian captivity, when Cyrus the Persian gave us freedom.

For our people who don't know that history, Ezra 1 shows it: “Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled, the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia”. Whether we were in Assyria or in Persia, wherever we were scattered and displaced, we were given freedom to go back to Israel and build the house of God.

That is what 2 Esdras 13 is recording. The ten tribes were given that freedom, but they took counsel to go instead “into a further country, where never mankind dwelt, That they might there keep their statutes, which they never kept in their own land.” The northern kingdom wanted a fresh start, tired of captivity after captivity: Assyrian, Babylonian, Persian. So they went into Arsareth, the land Columbus identified as America. Our land is Israel; we were not always in the islands.

precepts.label: Sirach 33:27
precepts.why:
“For, behold, the burning wrath of a great multitude is kindled over you”. That great multitude is what Christ said: you shall be hated of all nations for my name's sake. And “they shall take away certain of you, and feed you, being idle”. Idle, i-d-l-e: a person avoiding work; lazy, indolent, slothful, workshy, shiftless, loafing; without purpose or effect, pointless.

In this truth, if you are idle you are avoiding work. Not work in the world: God's work. You are lazy in this truth. You have no purpose; you are just here. Some of you have been here for years and you have no office, doing nothing. You are idle.

“Send him to labour, that he be not idle; for idleness teacheth much evil.” Brothers and sisters, when you are idle in the truth, you are learning evil. That is why you spend your time on porn, smoking cigarettes, smoking weed, hitting women up in their DMs. You have idle time, and there is a whole lot of work in this truth to be done.

We can spot that idleness as soon as you come in: the one who sits down and just looks around, looking at the women's side, taking no notes. If this means something to you, you are engulfed in it; you are writing things down and trying to put it to memory. The idle are the certain ones the multitude will take away and feed.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 4:1-5
precepts.why:
The idle will be fed “with things offered unto idols.” Idols in the Bible are statues, figurines, golden calves, and also money, career and power that compete with God for worship. So what is the most idolatrous religion here in America? Christianity. You may think that is biased; Paul identifies the religion.

“Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils”. This is the latter times. Why will some give heed to seducing spirits? Because you are idle; you have idle time. “Speaking lies in hypocrisy”: I believe in God, but I am not going to do anything the Bible says. “having their conscience seared with a hot iron; Forbidding to marry”: what religion forbids men to marry? Catholics; that is Christianity. “and commanding to abstain from meats”: who cannot eat meat for 40 days? Catholics; they call it Lent.

Those meats “God hath created to be received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth”, and the truth is God's law. “For every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving: For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.” Where is the food sanctified by the word of God? Leviticus 11.

The Roman Catholic Church is the mother church of every Protestant denomination on the tree: Orthodox, Jehovah's Witness, Presbyterian, Lutheran, Methodist, Episcopalian, Mormon, Evangelical, Pentecostal, Baptist, Adventist, Anglican, all the way to Christian nationalism. That is the idolatry the multitude will feed the idle, and they are already saying out loud that they are going to impose it on this country.

precepts.label: Revelation 13:6-8
precepts.why:
What do all those churches have in common? They worship the image of the beast. “And he opened his mouth in blasphemy against God, to blaspheme his name, and his tabernacle, and them that dwell in heaven.” Their blasphemy is the perversion of the gospel of Christ, the perversion of the truth.

“And it was given unto him to make war with the saints, and to overcome them”. Esau made war with us: Rome, Spain, Portugal. Pope Nicholas V made that edict to enslave us and force us into Christianity. And they overcame us; they enslaved us. “and power was given him over all kindreds, and tongues, and nations.”

“And all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him”: the same man that overcame us. A book published in 1920, The Pillory, the Tale of the Borgia Pope, says it is an open secret that Cesare Borgia, son of Pope Alexander, posed for the image of Jesus. Salvatore, the savior: that is Cesare Borgia. Even Muslims will tell you that image is Jesus; ask a Buddhist and he will say the same. Everybody acknowledges it as Jesus the Christ.

All that worship him are those “whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.” That is the idol the multitude will feed to the idle.

precepts.label: Revelation 12:17
precepts.why:
In every place and in the next cities there shall be “a great insurrection upon those that fear the Lord.” Revelation shows who is behind it: “And the dragon was wroth with the woman, and went to make war with the remnant of her seed, which keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.”

The dragon is wroth: our enemies see us and they are angry. That is why in France they already said, shut down IUIC; a black Jesus, the Israelites, that is anti-semitic, we cannot allow this to go on. And he went to make war with the remnant: that is physical war, not only spiritual. That is tribulation, Jacob's trouble, persecution against those who keep the commandments and the testimony of Jesus Christ.

Christ warned of the same: “Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name's sake. And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.” You say you would never consent to their religion, but a whip across your back will change some of you, and you will be compelled to blaspheme.

And those who consent will be had in derision. Nobody likes a traitor. Like the apes in Planet of the Apes who betrayed their own and wore the word donkey before they were killed, Esau will use you and get rid of you. The ones who keep the commandments and the testimony are the ones the dragon makes war with; that is why Christ said, if they persecute you in this city, flee to the next.

thread.label: 2 Esdras 16:68
thread.text: For, behold, the burning wrath of a great multitude is kindled over you, and they shall take away certain of you, and feed you, being idle, with things offered unto idols.

precepts.label: Isaiah 19:20
precepts.why:
“For, behold, the burning wrath of a great multitude is kindled over you”. Who is this great multitude that is over us? It is law enforcement, their military, set over the believing Israelites. Isaiah proves it.

“In that day shall there be an altar to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a pillar at the border thereof”. This Egypt is a spiritual Egypt: America. An altar is used for sacrifice, so there is going to be a lot of death. “And it shall be for a sign and for a witness unto the Lord of hosts in the land of Egypt: for they shall cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors”.

Why would we cry unto the Lord? Because of the oppressors, with an s on it: more than one. That is the great multitude whose burning wrath is kindled over us. That is Jacob's trouble, and we have not gotten to that part yet.

So the great multitude of 2 Esdras 16 is the oppressors of Isaiah 19, the power of spiritual Egypt that will be over our people in this land, and it is because of them that Israel will cry unto the Lord.

precepts.label: Joel 2:17
precepts.why:
Joel shows the same cry. “Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly”, and “Let the priests, the ministers of the Lord, weep between the porch and the altar, and let them say, Spare thy people, O Lord, and give not thine heritage to reproach, that the heathen should rule over them: wherefore should they say among the people, Where is their God?”

Why will we cry, Spare thy people? We just read it in Isaiah 19: because of the oppressors. They will say, we killed you, where is your God? We cut your throat, we ended your bank account, where is your God?

“Then will the Lord be jealous for his land, and pity his people.” He pities his people because we are not in the land. But he promises not to leave us alone: “Behold, I will send you corn, and wine, and oil”, “and I will no more make you a reproach among the heathen”.

“But I will remove far off from you the northern army”. That is the name the Bible gives to the power that is going to be on us: the oppressors of Isaiah 19, the great multitude of 2 Esdras 16, is the northern army. He will drive him into a land barren and desolate, with his face toward the east sea, the Dead Sea, and his hinder part toward the utmost sea, the Mediterranean, “and his stink shall come up”. The white man shall meet death when he goes to that land, because he has done evil things.

precepts.label: Sirach 33:27
precepts.why:
The great multitude “shall take away certain of you, and feed you, being idle, with things offered unto idols.” Spell that word: i-d-l-e. “Send him to labour, that he be not idle; for idleness teacheth much evil.”

Idle means a person avoiding work: lazy, indolent, slothful, shiftless, inactive, sluggish, lethargic; without purpose or effect. Those words fit some of you in here, men and women. Not the new people who just came, but those who have been with us two years or more. What are you doing? Do you have an office? Is there something you are doing here in Israel? If not, you are idle, and idleness teaches much evil.

And what will the idle be fed? Things offered unto idols, i-d-o-l: an image or representation of a god used as an object of worship. Look at the images of the Roman Catholic Church; those are idols. One word: Christianity.

So the ones the multitude takes away and feeds with idolatry are the ones with no purpose in here. Because you were idle, you will be seduced and given Christianity, that idolatrous religion. Stay busy in the work of the Most High.

thread.label: 2 Esdras 16:71-78
thread.text: They shall be like mad men, sparing none, but still spoiling and destroying those that fear the Lord.

precepts.label: 1 Maccabees 1:41-50
precepts.why:
“They shall be like mad men, sparing none, but still spoiling and destroying those that fear the Lord.” We read the book of Acts and think that could never happen again, but Paul himself said, “being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.” The prophecy says it is going to happen again, and it happened under the Greeks too.

“Moreover king Antiochus wrote to his whole kingdom, that all should be one people, And every one should leave his laws: so all the heathen agreed according to the commandment of the king. Yea, many also of the Israelites consented to his religion, and sacrificed unto idols, and profaned the sabbath.” That is what is going to happen again. It happened in the time of Paul, in the time of the Maccabees, in Babylon when they tried to get us to worship the false god. That which has been is that which shall be; there is no new thing under the sun. Idolatry: leave that God and come worship this god.

They sent letters “that they should follow the strange laws of the land”, profane the sabbaths and festival days, sacrifice swine's flesh, leave their children uncircumcised, “To the end they might forget the law, and change all the ordinances. And whosoever would not do according to the commandment of the king, he said, he should die.” You think they cannot make a Sunday law and say, that Sabbath thing, no, worship God on the day we say?

The same thing we read in the Maccabees is what Rome, Spain and Portugal did to our people in the Inquisition; read Jews and Moors. And you say it can never happen, this is the United States of America? It happened during slavery. The same thing.

precepts.label: Hebrews 10:34
precepts.why:
“For they shall waste and take away their goods, and cast them out of their houses.” They did it in the time of Rome, when the Pharisees did it with Rome's guidance. Paul tells the Hebrews, “For ye had compassion of me in my bonds, and took joyfully the spoiling of your goods, knowing in yourselves that ye have in heaven a better and an enduring substance.”

Ye had compassion of me in my bonds: when Paul was in prison, they supported him. And they took joyfully the spoiling, the robbing, of their goods: their homes and houses, lands and properties. Those Israelites sacrificed their whole livelihood. They knew that supporting Paul would reveal them, and whatever they had would be taken.

Are we prepared for that? Do we really think about it? The cushy side of the room: I'm so comfortable, I got my new house, my new car, my new hair, my new nails. Are you ready for what the scriptures say is going to happen? Are we willing to lose everything, knowing we have in heaven a better and enduring substance? That is another level of faith we have to build ourselves up to in the short, limited time we have.

Even the world is warning that if a crisis comes and the government says get on a bus for your safety, do not get on: prepare your food, water, power and shelter so you do not have to rely on them. We have been telling our people that for years.

precepts.label: Matthew 10:32-33
precepts.why:
“Then shall they be known, who are my chosen; and they shall be tried as the gold in the fire.” That verse is very important, because it goes back to what Christ said: “Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven. But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.”

Christ is talking about tribulation, persecution, Jacob's trouble. So what will the chosen be saying about Christ in that day, will they deny him or confess him? They are going to confess him.

Why does it say “Then shall they be known”? Because right now everybody says they believe in the Lord. Women say it; men say it. But when this starts to happen, you are going to see who is real and who is fake. On that day the ones who confess Christ before their tormentors are the ones known to be his chosen, tried as gold in the fire, and he will confess them before his Father.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 3:1-6
precepts.why:
The chosen are “tried as the gold in the fire”, and Wisdom gives more detail. “But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and there shall no torment touch them.” Christ said we will be afflicted, so what does no torment mean? That is the lake of fire. That torment will not touch us.

“In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die: and their departure is taken for misery, And their going from us to be utter destruction: but they are in peace.” Christ said, fear not them which kill the body; fear him who can kill body and soul. Man cannot touch your soul. They seem to die because the body died, but the real man, the real woman, is not dead. We keep falling for Esau's craftiness: it's all over, we're finished. It is not over. They are in peace; that is sleep, rest.

“For though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality. And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded”. Jacob's trouble is just a little chastisement. “for God proved them, and found them worthy for himself.” God is going to prove us. Everybody says they believe; he will say, let that one get caught early and see what they do. He found them worthy because they confessed Christ before their tormentors.

“As gold in the furnace hath he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering.” The death of the saints is as a burnt offering to the Lord. Christ gave his life, and he said if you will not take up your cross and follow him, you are not worthy of him.

precepts.label: Matthew 10:38
precepts.why:
Wisdom says the righteous are tried as gold in the furnace and received as a burnt offering. Christ said, “And he that taketh not his cross, and followeth after me, is not worthy of me.”

Christians say that means you cannot pay your bills and you have to carry all your problems on your back. No, that is not what it is talking about. When Christ was carrying the cross, where did it lead him? To death. He is saying the same thing for us.

We have to be willing to sacrifice ourselves. That is what Wisdom of Solomon was just saying: the souls of the righteous who die for the truth are in the hand of God. If you cannot confess the Lord, even unto death, you are not worthy to be his disciple. That is the cross, and that is how the chosen will be known.

precepts.label: Acts 12:1-15
precepts.why:
“Hear, O ye my beloved, saith the Lord: behold, the days of trouble are at hand, but I will deliver you from the same. Be ye not afraid neither doubt”. Why neither doubt? Because doubt comes. My mama just got put to death, my children, my wife; Lord, are you going to save us? Remember John the Baptist when he was imprisoned; that little bit of doubt crept in. Acts shows the situation.

“Now about that time Herod the king stretched forth his hands to vex certain of the church. And he killed James the brother of John with the sword. And because he saw it pleased the Jews, he proceeded further to take Peter also. (Then were the days of unleavened bread.)” James was beheaded; Peter was in prison. The angel brought Peter out, and he went to “the house of Mary the mother of John, whose surname was Mark; where many were gathered together praying.” That was a safe house where Israelites were hiding and praying. When the damsel knew Peter's voice, “they said unto her, Thou art mad”, and “Then said they, It is his angel.”

What did they think had happened to Peter? That he had been put to death. It shows you could not go visit him. There was no visitation, as there are prisons like Guantanamo Bay in Cuba today, with no lawyers and no visitors, and they are building more like it. So do not think, the brothers don't care about me, the sisters didn't come visit me. There will be places nobody can visit you. It is not that we do not care; we cannot get to you. All the saints could do was pray.

And Peter was on the run, a fugitive from the government the rest of his life. The Lord intervened for one and gave him more time, and the other, James, was killed. It is going to get like that, brothers and sisters. That is why we study, pray and apply: knowing ahead of time is supposed to strengthen your resolve, so that you are not afraid, neither doubt.

precepts.label: 1 John 1:8-10
precepts.why:
“for God is your guide, And the guide of them who keep my commandments and precepts, saith the Lord God: let not your sins weigh you down”. Why say, let not your sins weigh you down? Because we do sin, and churches love to try to trap you with it. “If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.”

Christians on the street will say, do you sin, my brother? Yes. But my sin cannot justify you continuing in sin. Verse 9 is the key; verse 9 is the difference between me and you.

When we start cutting them up, they say, you think you're better than us? Do you sin? Tell them yes, and go right here and show them the difference. They are liars, because they teach that you can sin with no consequences. We teach that if we do sin, the black Messiah laid down his life, if we believe on him, so that we can fight to stop sinning. Simple answer; don't let them jam you up.

We do make errors and fall into folly at times. Confess it and keep fighting, and let not your sins weigh you down.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 2:11
precepts.why:
“let not your iniquities lift up themselves.” “Woe be unto them that are bound with their sins”. When you keep entertaining that sin, eventually you will be bound by it. Peter says, “Dearly beloved, I beseech you as strangers and pilgrims, abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul”.

This is a spiritual war, a war for your soul. Take porn. Brothers say, I got it under control; it don't bother me. No, you don't have it under control. Picture a hallway of doors. A lot of you say, I only watch straight porn, like it is a good thing. That is door number one. Then the threesome, then the train. After a while you get desensitized; that does not excite you anymore, so you go to the next door down: chicks with dicks, then bestiality, then scat, then lesbian, then pedophilia. That is where the doors lead.

It is not normal. And you know it is the devil: when the Bishop was a little kid, his father had magazines hidden up in the drop ceiling. How did two little boys know to get a chair and climb up there, when they never saw their father do it? Playboy, Hustler, then VHS, then DVDs, and today easy access in your hand.

That is how iniquity lifts itself up until you are bound with your sins, covered like a field with thorns. Abstain from fleshly lusts; they are at war with your soul.

precepts.label: Romans 6:14-16
precepts.why:
When you keep entertaining a sin, it binds you. Paul says, “For sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under the law, but under grace.” We are not under the law of sacrifice, but under grace. “What then? shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace? God forbid.”

“Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?” His servants ye are to whom ye obey. If you wake up thinking about porn, go to work thinking about porn, and go to sleep thinking about porn, that is your god. You are its servant.

Grace is not a license to keep sinning; it is so that sin shall not have dominion over you. Christ laid down his life so we could fight to stop sinning, not so we could be bound in it. And when you are bound, there is no magic scripture that will release you; you have to want to be released.

precepts.label: Hebrews 6:4-8
precepts.why:
“Woe be unto them that are bound with their sins, and covered with their iniquities like as a field is covered over with bushes, and the path thereof covered with thorns, that no man may travel through! It is left undressed, and is cast into the fire to be consumed therewith.” Hebrews says the same thing.

“For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come, If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance”. Those who were once enlightened, who came into this truth, and fall away back into their sin or back into false religion: it is impossible to renew them again to repentance.

“For the earth which drinketh in the rain that cometh oft upon it, and bringeth forth herbs meet for them by whom it is dressed, receiveth blessing from God: But that which beareth thorns and briers is rejected, and is nigh unto cursing; whose end is to be burned.”

That is the field of 2 Esdras 16:78, covered with thorns, left undressed and cast into the fire. The ground that drinks in the word and brings forth fruit receives blessing; the one bound with its sins and bearing thorns ends in the fire.

precepts.label: Psalms 96:4-5
precepts.why:
Wisdom tells the kings of the earth that “the desire of wisdom bringeth to a kingdom”, and to “honour wisdom, that ye may reign for evermore.” David shows why the kingdoms of the nations never did: “For the Lord is great, and greatly to be praised: he is to be feared above all gods. For all the gods of the nations are idols”.

They are all idols. All kingdoms fall because they do not walk after the wisdom of God. Name a kingdom that has kept the commandments of God. They don't. They fall because they serve idol gods, and pride destroys them, as it destroyed Herod, who gave not God the glory and was eaten of worms. Assyrian, Babylon, Greek, Rome, America: nobody is exempt from pride and God destroying them.

It is no different with Babylon the Great. This Edomite has the most gods of all: he has all the idol gods of every kingdom wrapped up in one, in different forms. That is why Obadiah follows, “concerning Edom”, the white man, the Caucasian, his biblical name: “thou art greatly despised”, and “The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee”. None of the kings before him, Assyrians, Babylonians, Persians, Greeks or Romans, was more prideful than Esau.

The same judgment is on us. The power God gave was given to us by God too, and for our pride as a nation we have been destroyed. The only way our kingdom will last for ever is when we walk in wisdom and humility toward God. Outside of that, the kingdom comes down, the same as it did with all the nations before us.

precepts.label: Psalms 50:21
precepts.why:
Why is it that when our iniquity had an end, Esau refused to let us go and kept shedding our blood? Solomon speaks of the ancient Egyptians, and this is modern Egypt today: “not being ignorant that they were a naughty generation, and that their malice was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed.” Their malice is bred in them: God made them that way. They will never change as a race of people. That's why it has been a perpetual hatred from Cain to Abel, Jacob to Esau, blacks and whites, playing itself out over and over, while Christianity blinds us from accepting what God is telling us.

Name a century that black people have had pure peace around this white man. Not we-got-the-vote peace: you still get jailed, racially profiled, shot down, and you can't do what white people do when they get pulled over. The record lists it: the transatlantic slave trade and child slavery from 1619 to 1865, racial terror after emancipation, massacres in Memphis, Colfax, Wilmington, Atlanta, East St. Louis, the Red Summer, Arkansas, Tulsa, Rosewood. And that is only what was reported; imagine what was not documented.

As a result of all this enslavement and all these massacres, Esau is thinking a certain way now. He thinks he's getting away with it: “These things hast thou done, and I kept silence.” Oh, wait a minute, we just enslaved the Lord's people and he didn't do anything.

“thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself.” That is what Esau is thinking to this day. That's why they don't hold themselves accountable for anything. They hold themselves not guilty when they slay us, when they kill us, when they put us into slavery, when they don't give us reparations. Esau thinks he is God.

“but I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes.” There will be a judgment for these things. So don't think that smiling white man in your face means to do you good.

precepts.label: Revelation 13:6-8
precepts.why:
Wisdom says “a father afflicted with untimely mourning, when he hath made an image of his child soon taken away, now honoured him as a god”. Pope Alexander VI, Rodrigo Borgia, died on August 18, 1503, before his son Caesar Borgia, who lost his power and was killed in a skirmish in Spain in 1507. But it was the father’s instruction to use his son as white Jesus. Caesar Borgia is the one they set up as Christ. Revelation 13 shows what that beast did.

“And he opened his mouth in blasphemy against God, to blaspheme his name, and his tabernacle, and them that dwell in heaven.” They set themselves up: the white man set himself up as God and went against all God’s laws. This is the creation and function of the Roman Catholic Church.

“And it was given unto him to make war with the saints, and to overcome them”. Spain and Portugal made war against the saints of God, and they overcame us in slavery. “And power was given him over all kindreds, and tongues, and nations”: the white man conquered everybody.

“And all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him, whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.” Shall worship him, the so-called white man. In The Tale of the Borgia Pope by John Bond, under the bust of the Saviour: it is an open secret that Caesar Borgia, the son of Pope Alexander, had posed for it. So all the world started to worship him as God, the son of God.

That is Wisdom’s “ungodly custom grown strong” that “was kept as a law, and graven images were worshipped by the commandments of kings.” The custom of worshipping the white man as Jesus grew strong in the earth, and his images stand in Brazil, New York, Mexico, you name it: “the counterfeit of his visage”. The worshipping of idols is “the beginning, the cause, and the end, of all evil”; it goes back to Adam and Eve, whose sin was idolatry, and the sin of these last days is the same. Christianity is an idolatrous religion.

thread.text: Pride is hateful before God and man: and by both doth one commit iniquity.

precepts.label: Psalms 100:3
precepts.why:
“Pride was not made for men, nor furious anger for them that are born of a woman.” Pride, arrogance, disdain, the inability to admit fault, the inflated ego: God said it wasn't made for you. You are nothing but dust that shall return to where it came from. And anger doesn't get you anywhere either; it holds you back and stunts your growth.

Why wasn't pride made for us? “Know ye that the Lord he is God: it is he that hath made us, and not we ourselves”. You didn't put one finger on your hand. You didn't put the knee bone with the hip bone and the leg bone. All of that belongs to God, the Creator, from way back when he said, Let us make man in our image.

He didn't consult you: where should I put the knee? How high up on the leg should it go? What should the arch of the foot look like? What skin tone should I give them? What should I make their hair like? None of us were included in that conversation.

So pride has no ground to stand on. The one who did not make himself cannot be proud before the one who made him. That is why the beginning of pride is turning away from your Maker.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 11:5
precepts.why:
“As thou knowest not what is the way of the spirit”: you don't know how the spirit was even made, and the body doesn't function without a spirit in it. We say someone is soulless, and it may be jacked up and crooked like the Esau in them, but that body isn't walking around with nothing in it. This is not a movie where they clone you and you come back with no soul, or a vampire who lives forever and can't see his reflection. There is a spirit in all of us, and the Most High made that.

“nor how the bones do grow in the womb of her that is with child”. Science tries to explain it the best way it can, by the mitochondria and this and that, but they don't know what God did to make it. Science is God giving man some sense of his mastery, and man takes it and says, I can do better than God: let me put this rod on you as a woman, let me cut yours off. That's why the Bible warns us to beware of science that opposes God.

“even so thou knowest not the works of God who maketh all.” So why is earth and ashes proud? Man does not even know how he himself was made; pride was not made for men.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 12:7
precepts.why:
Solomon mentions that spirit again: “Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.”

The body goes back to the dust it came from, and the spirit goes back to God who made it. All of this, the dust and the spirit, belongs to the Most High God. That is why pride is not made for us.

Sirach asks, “Why is earth and ashes proud?” and says that when a man is dead “he shall inherit creeping things, beasts, and worms.” The man who is today a king tomorrow shall die. Neither the body nor the spirit is ours to boast in: one returns to the earth, the other to its Maker. So the beginning of pride, departing from God and turning the heart away from the Maker, is turning away from the very one the spirit must return to.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 6:20
precepts.why:
“For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God’s.” That is who your body belongs to.

This isn't something the young ones usually fight with. It's us, as we get older, who start smelling ourselves: I'm going to do this, this is what I want to do. We forget that at the end of the day we are still the children of the Most High God. You don't get to tell him what you are going to do with that body. The way parents look at their son and say, you'll always be my baby, even at forty-seven with gray hair: apply that to your life with God.

You have to keep these commandments, because he is still your Father and that is what he said to do. And that is the beginning of pride in Sirach 10: “when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker.” As we get older we start thinking we can decide whether to serve God or obey our Father, and that is pride. Pride is the beginning of sin; don't tell yourself you have a good heart while you depart from his commandments. Pride is hateful before God, and what he hates has an expiration date.

precepts.label: Matthew 4:15
precepts.why:
“The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles”. Zebulun and Naphtali are tribes of Israel, part of the northern kingdom, and yet their land is called Galilee of the Gentiles. So the southern kingdom was calling the northern kingdom Gentiles and uncircumcised. Very simple.

How did Israelites come to be called Gentiles? In the days of the Maccabees, “according to the commandment they put to death certain women, that had caused their children to be circumcised. And they hanged the infants about their necks”. They were enforcing it: you could not be circumcised; you had to be like the Gentiles. They were hanging babies. So what is the next generation going to be? Uncircumcised. And the next one, uncircumcised, not keeping the laws, profaning the Sabbath, calling themselves and being called Gentiles.

Zondervan's compact Bible dictionary says Gentiles usually means a non-Israelite people. Usually: meaning there are certain contexts, like this one, where it is not talking about the other nations at all, but about Israelites who were made to live like the heathen. That is how Ephesians 2 has to be understood.

precepts.label: Psalms 96:5
precepts.why:
The third brother, when they came to cut him, put out his tongue right away and held forth his hands manfully: come on, let's get this over with. He said courageously, “These I had from heaven; and for his laws I despise them; and from him I hope to receive them again.” And “the king, and they that were with him, marvelled at the young man's courage, for that he nothing regarded the pains.”

Why did they marvel? They had to understand there was a certain spirit in these brothers; there was something the brothers knew that the king did not. The psalm tells what it is: “For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens.”

All the gods of the nations are idols, so the nations have no living God. The king had power, arrogance and the fire, but his gods were dead. These brothers served the Lord that made the heavens, the God who gave them their tongues and hands and would give them again. That is why they were ready to die rather than transgress the laws of their fathers, and why the heathen could only stand there and marvel.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 8:5-6
precepts.why:
The king marveled at the young man's courage, and Paul shows the reason. “For though there be that are called gods, whether in heaven or in earth, (as there be gods many, and lords many,) But to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him.”

Because we understand that there is only one living God, that is why they marvel. That is why the king was marveling. The nations have gods many and lords many, but a man who knows the one God, the Father, and the one Lord Jesus Christ can say, “we are ready to die, rather than to transgress the laws of our fathers.”

Do you know what level of faith that is? You truly cannot desire anything left in this world. We are already captives: you have bills, you work fourteen hours a day. What are you leaving? There has to be something better. So the brothers went to the fire expecting “the King of the world” to raise them up “unto everlasting life”, and the fourth told the king, “as for thee, thou shalt have no resurrection to life.”

That hope belongs to those who have the one God. What kind of mercy would it be for the same people that torment us to get an equal reward in the kingdom? That is not a merciful God. The one God of Israel will of his own mercy give his servants breath and life again.

precepts.label: Acts 12:21-23
precepts.why:
Cyrus the Persian humbled himself and let all Israel go, and God said, you can rule. But the Greek Antiochus “had spoken proudly”, saying “he would come to Jerusalem and make it a common burying place of the Jews.” As soon as he spoke those proud words, “a pain of the bowels that was remediless came upon him, and sore torments of the inner parts”, and that most justly, because he had tormented other men’s bowels. He fell from his chariot, rotted until he could not abide his own smell, and finally said “It is meet to be subject unto God, and that a man that is mortal should not proudly think of himself if he were God.”

It did not stop with the Greeks. Now we come down to the Romans, because that is what Herod was: “And upon a set day Herod, arrayed in royal apparel, sat upon his throne, and made an oration unto them. And the people gave a shout, saying, It is the voice of a god, and not of a man.”

Black folk always think the white man is God, and God always has to remind you who he is. “And immediately the angel of the Lord smote him, because he gave not God the glory: and he was eaten of worms, and gave up the ghost.” Antiochus rotted with worms rising out of his body; Herod was eaten of worms. The same judgment for the same pride.

Pride destroyed them. All kingdoms fall because of pride, and nobody is exempt: Assyria, Babylon, Greece, Rome, America. That is the judgment for it. So check yourself before you wreck yourself: a man that is mortal must not think of himself as if he were God.
